Migrating this screen will help reduce UI boilerplate, improve readability, and align the codebase with modern Android UI development practices already adopted in other parts of the project.

### 🎯 Goals
- Implement the UI using Jetpack Compose.
 - Use MVI in `Settings`.
- Remove XML layout usage from ` Composition defaults` screen.
- Ensure no regression in functionality.

title: Automate and improve Monthly Progress Reporting
body:
We want to write a monthly progress report, but doing so got more and more difficult, due to the increased number of contributions.

To have a nice overview we would like to:

- Introduce labels on PRs to help identify their relevance for the progress report (e.g., report: include, report: exclude, report: highlight).
- Enforce labels on all PRs via GitHub Actions.
- Add a script to generate a report of all merged PRs during a month.

Having the PR check in place moves the responsibility to the reviewer to properly assign the right report relevance. As a result, we don't need to retroactively figure out what was done and if it's relevant for the report.

body:
The current implementation of `Modifier.draggable` in Compose unintentionally triggers swipes when scrolling a `LazyColumn`. However, version 1.11.0 of the `compose-foundation` library addresses this issue. To ensure the reliability of our `SwipeableRow` composable, we will fork the necessary parts of the code.

For more details, please refer to the following links: [Issue Tracker](https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/269627294) and [Compose Foundation Release Notes](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-foundation#1.11.0-alpha05).

A follow-up task will be created to remove the fork once 1.11.0 is released.

title: [ML 0.5/MVI.01.4] - Enable State Machine history tracking
body:
## Description
As part of the MVI foundation for the Message List feature, we want to enable history tracking in the State Machine to improve debuggability, traceability of transitions, and confidence during further migration steps.

This task introduces state history tracking capabilities to the existing State Machine implementation, allowing us to inspect previous states and transitions without altering the current business behaviour.

The solution should be safe by default and avoid introducing unnecessary runtime or memory overhead in production builds.

## Goal
Enable optional history tracking for the Message List State Machine so that:

- State transitions can be recorded in chronological order.
- Developers can inspect previous states and dispatched intents/actions.
- Debugging and testing of complex state transitions becomes easier.
- Production performance remains unaffected (or minimally impacted).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The State Machine supports history tracking of:
  - Previous states
  - Triggering intents/actions (where applicable)
  - State transitions (from -> to)
- History tracking can be enabled/disabled (e.g., via configuration, debug flag, or build type).
- When disabled, there is no functional change in behaviour.
- When enabled, the State Machine records transitions in a bounded structure (to prevent unbounded memory growth).
- The history mechanism does not alter the state reduction logic.
- No changes are introduced to the public API of unrelated modules.
- Unit tests are added/updated to verify:
  - History is recorded when enabled.
  - No history is recorded when disabled.
  - The bounded buffer behaves as expected.

## Out of Scope
- UI to visualize the state history.
- Logging infrastructure changes beyond what is required for tracking.
- Refactoring the overall MVI architecture.
- Performance optimization beyond reasonable safeguards (e.g., bounded buffers).

title: [ML 0.1/UI.01.10] - Connect Message List Screen Composable with legacy data
body:
Depends on #10573.

## Description
With the `MessageListScreen` composable contract and UI scaffold in place, this task focuses on connecting the screen to the existing legacy data sources and business logic.

The goal is to bridge the new Compose-based UI layer with the current Message List state management, data providers, and interaction handlers, ensuring feature parity while maintaining clear module boundaries.

## Goal
Connect `MessageListScreen` to the legacy Message List data flow so that:

- Real message list data is rendered in the Compose UI.
- Existing refresh, pagination, swipe, and item interaction logic are properly wired.
- The screen behaves consistently with the legacy implementation.

The integration must preserve the separation between:
- `:feature:mail:message:list:api`
- `:feature:mail:message:list:internal`

while ensuring legacy dependencies remain encapsulated and not exposed through the public API.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `MessageListScreen` is backed by real legacy data sources (no mock or placeholder data).
- Pull-to-refresh triggers the legacy refresh mechanism.
- The footer button (legacy "lazy load") is correctly wired to the appropriate legacy action.
- Swipe actions trigger existing legacy handlers without altering their behaviour.
- Message item click interactions are delegated to the existing navigation/interaction logic.
- Any required state mapping layer (e.g., legacy model → UI model) is introduced in `:feature:mail:message:list:internal` and not exposed publicly.
- No business logic is migrated or rewritten in this task — only wiring and adaptation.
- Existing behaviour parity with the legacy Message List screen is maintained.

## Out of Scope
- Infinite scrolling is out of scope for now, but will be included if simple.
- Refactoring or rewriting legacy business logic.
- Architectural changes to the legacy data layer.
- UI redesign or structural changes to the screen or list items.
- Performance optimizations beyond what is required for safe integration.

## Notes
- This task acts as a bridge between the new Compose UI surface and the legacy implementation.
- Must use adapter/mapping layers over direct coupling between Compose and legacy classes.
- Maintain strict module boundaries and avoid leaking legacy types through the public API.
- Any temporary interoperability code should be clearly documented for future cleanup during full migration.

title: Migrate K9.lockScreenNotificationVisibility to PreferenceDataStore
body:
The current implementation in Thunderbird Android directly accesses the static field K9.lockScreenNotificationVisibility to determine Lock Screen Notification Visbility. This approach bypasses the modern PreferenceDataStore, which is the preferred mechanism for managing application settings.

This task involves refactoring all direct references to K9.lockScreenNotificationVisibility and replacing them with proper usage of PreferenceDataStore. This will improve consistency, testability, and alignment with the app’s current architecture for preference management.

title: [ML 0.5/MVI.01.3] - Separate LegacyMessageListFragment and MessageListFragment implementation
body:
Our initial approach for refactoring the Message List was to create an abstract class. This would allow us to gradually override methods as we completed the migration, helping us avoid code duplication and making it easier to apply any changes from the legacy implementation to the new one.

However, this approach has started to produce unexpected side effects that we did not anticipate.

For this reason, we are shifting to a different strategy. Instead of using an abstract class, we will revert all the changes made so far. We will remove the abstract `BaseMessageListFragment` and replicate the code from the `LegacyMessageListFragment` into the new `MessageListFragment`. After that, we will apply the state changes.

This new approach will enable us to progress more quickly with the state changes, as the `LegacyMessageListFragment` will remain untouched during this transition.

Additionally, we need to add a note in the `LegacyMessageListFragment` to inform developers that whenever a change is made to it, we must also propagate that change to the new `MessageListFragment` to maintain consistency.

- Alterations to the Excerpt when the message is encrypted

title: docs: introduce `AGENTS.md` to define rules for AI-Assisted contributions
body:
We are seeing an increasing number of AI-assisted and AI-generated contributions to the project. While such contributions can be valuable, they need to follow clear project rules around architecture, quality, privacy, security, and licensing.

This issue proposes adopting the open **AGENTS.md standard** (https://agents.md/) and adding an `AGENTS.md` file at the repository root to define expectations for AI agents and contributors using AI tools.

The goals are to:

- Ensure AI-assisted changes respect existing architecture and module boundaries
- Require proper testing, linting, and documentation
- Prevent introduction of telemetry, insecure patterns, or unnecessary dependencies
- Clarify contributor responsibility, including disclosure of AI assistance and licensing compliance

AI-assisted contributions may be accepted if they meet the same quality, security, and review standards as any other contribution.

title: Security: Stored credentials can be extracted without master password via NSS API
body:
## Summary

Thunderbird (and its underlying Mozilla credential storage) allows any local process to extract all stored email passwords in plaintext when no Primary/Master Password is configured — which is the **default** state.

## The Problem

Mozilla's credential storage (`logins.json` + `key4.db`) uses NSS (Network Security Services) to encrypt stored passwords. However, when no Primary Password is set (the default), the encryption key in `key4.db` is protected by an empty string. This means:

1. Any application running under the same user account can load `nss3.dll` / `libnss3.so`
2. Call `NSS_Init()` with the profile path
3. Verify the empty master password via `PK11_CheckUserPassword(slot, "")`
4. Decrypt **all** stored credentials via `PK11SDR_Decrypt()`

This requires **no privilege escalation**, no exploitation of any vulnerability — just standard API calls to Mozilla's own libraries.

## Proof of Concept

```python
import ctypes, json, os, base64

nss3 = ctypes.CDLL('nss3.dll')  # or libnss3.so
nss3.NSS_Init(profile_path.encode())

slot = nss3.PK11_GetInternalKeySlot()
nss3.PK11_CheckUserPassword(slot, b'')  # Returns 0 = success

# Decrypt any entry from logins.json
nss3.PK11SDR_Decrypt(encrypted_input, decrypted_output, None)
# → plaintext password
```

Full working implementation exists at [firefox_decrypt](https://github.com/unode/firefox_decrypt).

## Impact

- **All stored email credentials** (IMAP, POP3, SMTP passwords) are extractable
- **OAuth2 tokens** for services like Gmail are also stored and extractable
- Any malware, rogue browser extension, or script running as the user can silently harvest all credentials
- Users are **not warned** that their passwords are effectively stored in plaintext equivalent

## Suggested Mitigations

1. **Require Primary Password on first credential save** — Don't make it optional with an easy-to-dismiss prompt
2. **OS keychain integration** — Use Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service instead of NSS's own key storage. These are protected by the OS login session and are not trivially accessible via API
3. **Warning indicator** — Show a persistent security warning in the account settings when credentials are stored without a Primary Password
4. **Restrict NSS access** — Consider sandboxing or access control on the profile directory to prevent other processes from loading the key database

## Environment

- Thunderbird ESR (Desktop, Windows 11)
- Default configuration, no Primary Password set
- NSS credential storage with `encType: 1` (3DES-CBC / AES-256-CBC via PBES2)

## References

- [firefox_decrypt](https://github.com/unode/firefox_decrypt) — Demonstrates this exact extraction
- [Mozilla Wiki: NSS](https://wiki.mozilla.org/NSS)
- This applies equally to Firefox, Thunderbird Desktop, and Thunderbird Android if the same credential storage model is used

title: Relocate showAccountSelector from DrawerConfiguration to DrawerState
body:
Currently, **showAccountSelector** is part of **DrawerConfig**, and its value is persisted using Preferences via the static **K9.showAccountSelector**.

However, this setting no longer needs to be persisted, nor does it need to live inside **DrawerConfig**.

Goal of this issue:

- Hoist **showAccountSelector** from **DrawerConfig** to **DrawerState**.

- Remove the static **K9.showAccountSelector** and eliminate its associated persistence logic.

body:

16.0

Fairphone 6

### Steps to reproduce

This can be best reproduced with Airplane mode on, as it mostly revolves around local update of the view:

3. Turn on airplane mode
4. Open the specific account's Inbox
5. Open the same unread email as above
6. Go back
7. Email is immediately marked as read

### Expected behavior

When opening an email and locally marking it as read, the Unified Inbox should behave the same way as account inboxes.

### Actual behavior

Unified Inbox does not update when going back from mail view.

title: [ML 0.5/MVI.02.6] Implement Outbox Integration and Backend Enqueueing

* **Testing:** Unit tests verifying that the correct `Enqueue` commands are emitted when the Outbox or specific delete policies are involved.

title: [ML 0.5/MVI.02.5] Initial Implementation of DeleteMessages Orchestration Flow
body:
## Description
Implement the `DeleteMessages` use case from scratch. This component orchestrates sub-use cases (`MoveMessages`, `UpdateMessageFlags`) and providers to execute the message deletion logic.

## Goal
Develop a robust, reactive orchestrator that manages the complex deletion state machine using a Flow pipeline, ensuring high maintainability and compliance with single-exit-point constraints.

## Acceptance Criteria
* Implements the `DeleteMessages` interface using Flow transformation operators (e.g., `flatMapConcat`).
* Successfully branches between "Soft Delete" and "Hard Delete" paths using the `LocalDeleteOperationDecider`.
* Triggers `removeMessageNotification` for all targeted messages.
* Emits all specific `DeleteMessagesOutcome` states as defined in the sealed interface.
* **Testing:** Unit tests using Fakes (orchestration tests) to verify that the Flow emits the correct sequence of `DeleteMessagesOutcome` states for both Soft and Hard delete paths.

## Technical Requirements
* Must utilize the `MoveMessages` and `UpdateMessageFlags` flows to build the execution chain.
* Must satisfy Detekt's return-count and complexity rules.
* Error outcomes from sub-flows must be mapped to `DeleteMessagesOutcome.Error` and terminate the stream gracefully.

title: [ML 0.5/MVI.02.1] Define and Implement MoveMessages UseCase (Flow-based)
body:
## Description
Implement the `MoveMessages` use case within the `MessageOperationsContract`. This use case is responsible for moving messages between folders in the local database and coordinating the move on the remote server.

## Goal
To provide a reactive way to move messages that can be easily chained within the `DeleteMessages` orchestration pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria
* The use case returns a `Flow<Outcome<MoveMessagesOutcome.Success, MoveMessagesOutcome.Error>>`.
* Successfully updates message folder associations in the local repository.
* Triggers the corresponding move operation on the `Backend`.
* Correctness is verified via unit tests using Fakes (e.g., FakeMessageRepository, FakeBackend) covering success and failure (e.g., move error) scenarios.


## Technical Details
* Must provide a mapping of source `MessageUid`s to new destination `MessageUid`s (for UIDs that change during a move) to support downstream flag updates.

title: MessageList reanimates too often
body:
When entering the app or composing a message and returning back to the message list. The list animates on a sort order change.

This issue was introduced with #10444 and needs to be fixed before the next **main -> beta** merge 26.02.2026

> When the message list loads for the first time, we are not yet using the new state to load the message items. As a result, the SortType and the MessageList loading process are not synchronized. This leads to the app performing a sort operation after the items have loaded, which displays an animation as the items are sorted. This issue should be resolved once we start loading the message items using the new MessageListState.

title: Prevent need to use "Skip version bump (beta)" on b1 releases
body:
When running the Shippable Build & Signing workflow for a b1 release, you have to select the "Skip version bump (beta)" checkbox to keep the suffix at b1. Otherwise, b1 will be incorrectly incremented to b2.

This is because after the merge from main->beta, the beta suffix is already set to b1. Therefore we don't need to increment it.

This is only the case for b1. For b2 and beyond, we always need to increment it.

If we set it to b0 in main, it will be b0 after the merge of main->beta, and ready to increment to b1. This way we will have to increment it for all beta versions.

title: Add merge automation workflow
body:
We currently have a merge script at scripts/ci/merges/do_merge.py. It should be getting to a point where it doesn't need to be run manually. We need to add some more merge driver support first. Once we're at that point, let's create a github workflow that can be manually triggered to run the merge.

Additional things the merge workflow should do (mostly taken from docs/release/RELEASE.md merge steps):

**main->beta**

1. Send a message to the #tb-mobile-dev:mozilla.org matrix channel to let them know the merge is starting
2. Run merge
3. Open a new milestone for the new version and close the oldest milestone (there should always be 3 open milestones - automation that adds tasks to milestones depends on this) - this needs to be done before version bump in main
4. Submit a pull request with the merge results. We still need a human to look at the results.
5. Submit a pull request that increments the version in main

**beta->release**
- Same as above but no changes to milestones and no pull request to increment version

title: Replace Direct Usage of K9.notificationQuickDeleteBehaviour With PreferenceDataStore
body:
### Description

The Thunderbird Android notification's  Delete  buttons visibility preference ( Alwsys/Never/ For Single Message Notification) is determined by  static accessor `K9.notificationQuickDeleteBehaviour` . This approach bypasses the modern preference management architecture and creates tight coupling with legacy global state.

To align with the current preference system and improve maintainability, this task aims to:

### Goals:
 - Replace all direct reads of `K9.notificationQuickDeleteBehaviour` with the appropriate `PreferenceDataStore` getter.
 - Replace all direct writes to `K9.notificationQuickDeleteBehaviour`with the corresponding `PreferenceDataStore` setter.
 - Ensure that Notification UI  correctly observe preference updates instead of relying on static values.
 - Remove or deprecate the static `K9.notificationQuickDeleteBehaviour` field once migration is complete.
 - Verify that behavior remains consistent for users after the refactor.

title: [ML 0.7/LL.01] - API Design & Core Pagination
body:
# 🎯 The objective


Define the architectural contract for data fetching and implement the foundational pagination logic for standard folders. This milestone sets the stage for how the app will handle local database queries combined with remote data fetching.


### 🎒 Resources

- [Android Paging3 Documentation](https://developer.android.com/topic/libraries/architecture/paging/v3-overview)
- [Store5](https://github.com/MobileNativeFoundation/Store)
- #10409

## 🦮 Rules of the Road


### 🟢 In Scope

- Define the `MessageListRemoteMediator` API interface.
- Build cursor-based pagination logic for standard folders (non-unified).

### 🔴 Out of Scope

- Implementation of the Remote Mediator (just the API definition here).
- Pagination for Unified Folders (scheduled for LL.02).
- UI Integration.

### 🚧 Technical and/or Business Requirements

- **API Definition**:
	- Must support retrieving data from a single entry point.
	- Must support requesting newer data (push to refresh).
	- Ideally use `Flow` for data retrieval.
- **Pagination Logic**:
	- Use **Cursor pagination** based on sorting criteria (e.g., Date) + ID/Date as tiebreakers.

title: Rework App Launch
body:
# 🎯 The objective


Decouple the App Launch from the Message List and establish a standalone `MainActivity` that manages app state and navigation.


## 🦮 Rules of the Road


### 🟢 In Scope

- Decoupling of `MainActivity` from the Message List logic.
- Creation of a new `MainActivity` as the primary entry point and single point for navigation decisions.
- Integration of `FeatureLauncherActivity` functionality into the new `MainActivity`.
- Implementation of a unified navigation strategy using a Navigation Library. (Navigation 3?)
- Migration of app-level state management to a dedicated `MainScreenViewModel`.
- Handling of all external intents (Launcher, Notifications, Widgets) in the new `MainActivity`.
- Renaming the existing `MainActivity` to `MessageListActivity`.

### 🔴 Out of Scope

- Redesign of the Message List UI (beyond decoupling from the Activity).
- Migration of all app features to Compose (only the navigation shell is initially targeted).
- Changes to the backend or synchronization logic.

### 🚧 Technical and/or Business Requirements


**Technical Requirements**

- Use MVI architecture for the `MainScreenViewModel`.
- Ensure compatibility with existing Fragment-based destinations.
- The new `MainActivity` must be the designated `LAUNCHER` activity.

**Business Requirements**

- Maintain existing deep-linking and notification entry point functionality.
- Provide a more stable and maintainable foundation for future improvements.

body:

### App

Thunderbird for Android

Other

14

Samsung Galaxy A52s

### Steps to reproduce

**Note:** The cases below are different symptoms of the same underlying interaction issue in the To/Cc/Bcc recipient fields.
Related: #5996 (overlaps with Case A).

---

### Case A: Removing trailing space makes the field not editable
1. Create a new message.
2. Add one recipient so it becomes a chip in To/Cc/Bcc.
3. Place the cursor after the chip and delete the trailing whitespace, so the cursor is directly adjacent to the chip.
4. Tap into another field (e.g. Subject/body), then tap back into the recipient field.

**Video Case A**:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54e7a841-644a-42ed-99fb-4c23366b675f

### Case B: With multiple recipients, tapping a chip can open the wrong chip's popup menu
1. Create a new message.
2. Add 3 recipients to the same field so you have multiple chips.
3. Try tapping each chip (especially the middle one).

**Video: Case B:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/300f4737-864b-458a-9f5b-36a53c712f0b

### Case C: Cursor flicker when going from collapsed to expanded
1. Create a new message.
2. Add enough recipients so the field collapses (shows "+x").
3. Tap on the recipient field to expand it.

**Video Case C:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3852611-4338-4ad2-b65b-f46ecbeab0c4

### Case D: Keyboard flicker when opening a chip popup menu
1. Create a new message.
2. Add 2+ recipient chips.
3. Tap one chip to open the popup menu.
4. Tap the same chip repeatedly or tap different chips.

**Video Case D**: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64bf9a33-8ef8-4d73-9150-0177dc114f5c


### Expected behavior

- **Case A**: Even if the trailing space after the last recipient chip is removed, tapping an empty space in the recipient field should allow editing (i.e. show the keyboard and allow typing) rather than opening the recipient popup menu.
- **Case B**: Tapping a recipient chip should open the popup menu for *that exact chip*.
- **Case C**: When expanding from collapsed -> expanded, the cursor should appear directly at the end, without briefly showing at the beginning first.
- **Case D**: Tapping a recipient chip should not cause the keyboard to briefly open/close.

### Actual behavior

- **Case A**: After the trailing space is removed, tapping in the recipient field *only* opens the chip popup menu instead of allowing typing (keyboard doesn't show). This can force users to remove recipients one by one and re-enter them.
- **Case B**: With multiple recipient chips, tapping one can open the popup menu for a different chip (hit-testing is unreliable).
- **Case C**: When going from collapsed -> expanded, the cursor can briefly appear at the start of the field and then jump to the end.
- **Case D**: In some situations (tapping the same chip multiple times or tapping different chips), the keyboard briefly opens and immediately closes right before the popup menu appears.

### Logs

_No response_

body:
The funding feature must be updated to support the new Billing Library (migration from version 7.1.1 to 8.30).

With the updated API, historical one-time purchase data is no longer available. The previous method for retrieving purchase history is not supported in the new version.

**Expected Result:**

- Purchase validation works correctly without relying on server-side purchase history.
- Users upgrading from previous app versions retain proper purchase recognition without regressions.

title: Modernize Reading Mail Settings Using Jetpack Compose
body:
The **Reading Mail Settings** screen currently relies on an **XML**-based layout and **PreferenceGroup** for its UI. As part of our ongoing modernization and gradual transition to **Jetpack Compose**, this proposal suggests replacing the existing **XML** layout and **PreferenceGroup** with a fully Compose-based implementation.

Migrating this screen to Compose will reduce UI boilerplate, enhance code readability, and bring it in line with the modern Android UI practices already adopted elsewhere in the project.

### 🎯 Goals
- Implement the UI using **Jetpack Compose**.
- Use **MVI** in **Reading Mail Settings**.
- Ensure no regression in functionality.

title: Modernize AboutFragment Using Jetpack Compose
body:

Migrating this screen will help reduce UI boilerplate, improve readability, and align the codebase with modern Android UI development practices already adopted in other parts of the project.

### 🎯 Goals
- Remove XML layout usage from `AboutFragment`.
- Implement the UI using Jetpack Compose.
- Use MVI in `AboutFragment`.
- Ensure no regression in functionality.

title: PlugOS adoption note: K-9 Mail used as the built-in mail client in a privacy-focused OS
body:
Hi K-9 Mail / Thunderbird for Android team,

I’d like to share a real-world adoption note: K-9 Mail is preinstalled as the default email client in PlugOS.

[PlugOS](https://plugos.net) is a security- and privacy-focused Android-based system with a plug-and-play hardware form factor that works across iOS, Android, Windows and MacOS. It follows a clear design principle: the host phone is treated as an untrusted terminal, while the OS, apps, and sensitive user data run on a separate device.

All built-in applications in PlugOS are selected with a strong emphasis on security, privacy, and long-term maintainability, which is why we chose K-9 Mail as the default mail client.

Thanks for maintaining K-9 Mail and for your long-term commitment to open standards and user privacy. It’s great to see the project being used in security-oriented systems.

title: Display not updated when deleting certain items
body:
Let's say we pick a thread that has two items in it. 

We read the first item.
While we are reading it we push the delete button. 

Now we are back looking at those two items. 

That's funny, there should be only one. 

Okay let's tap that first item again.

Nothing happens. 

Well of course, the item doesn't exist anymore. 

I'm saying the display needs to be updated after we leave that first item, so we aren't shown two items instead of one.

title: Replace Direct Usage of K9.contactNameColor With PreferenceDataStore
body:
### Description

The Thunderbird Android codebase currently accesses and updates the contact name color preference using the static field `K9.contactNameColor`. This approach bypasses the modern preference management architecture and creates tight coupling with legacy global state.

To align with the current preference system and improve maintainability, this task aims to:

### Goals:
 - Replace all direct reads of `K9.contactNameColor` with the appropriate `PreferenceDataStore` getter.
 - Replace all direct writes to `K9.contactNameColor `with the corresponding `PreferenceDataStore` setter.
 - Ensure that UI components (especially in the Message List screen) correctly observe preference updates instead of relying on static values.
 - Remove or deprecate the static `K9.contactNameColor` field once migration is complete.
 - Verify that behavior remains consistent for users after the refactor.

title: Unified Account
body:
# 🎯 The objective


Currently, the app supports a single configurable Unified Folder. While this is typically used as a Unified Inbox, it can include messages from any folder that the user has selected to "integrate" into this unified view.



To conclude the drawer ui changes we need to add support for:

- A unified account view in the drawer.
- Provide dedicated unified folders for `Inbox`, `Outbox`, `Drafts`, `Sent`, `Spam`, and `Trash`.
- Ensure that selecting a unified folder displays messages from that folder type across all accounts.
- Distinguish between the existing configurable "Unified Folder" (which aggregates multiple folders) and the new type-specific unified special folders.

## 🦮 Rules of the Road


### 🟢 In Scope

- Support for global special folders in the unified account view.
- Infrastructure and search capabilities to support cross-account folder-type queries.
- UI and data layer updates to expose and display unified folders in the drawer.
- Consistency in behavior between the Unified Inbox and other unified special folders.

### 🔴 Out of Scope

- Support for custom unified folders (user-defined across accounts).
- Unified "Archive" folder (unless specifically requested later).
- Changes to the message list UI itself (beyond display of query results).
- Performance optimizations for extremely large sets of accounts (beyond current architecture).

### 🚧 Technical and/or Business Requirements

- Unified folders must behave exactly like the Unified Inbox in terms of selection and data flow.
- Provide a "true" unified account experience that users expect from a modern email client.
- Unified views must accurately reflect the combined state (unread/starred counts) of their constituent folders.
- Users should understand the difference between the integrated "Unified Folder" and type-specific unified views.

title: docs(adr): refine api/impl split into api/internal
body:
While the api/impl split is already a great step into better project organization it doesn't reflect our initial intention to split between code that is used and shared accross features and code that implements a specific feature but should not be visible to other parts of the app.

We propose clarifying and formalizing the module and package structure across Thunderbird for Android by:

* Renaming all `impl` modules to `internal` to clearly mark them as private implementation details.
* Keeping `api` modules as the only public contract surface between features and core areas.
* Establishing consistent package naming:
  * `api` modules use direct feature/core packages
  * `internal` modules mirror them under `.internal` package suffix.
* Enforcing dependency rules so only `api` modules may be referenced across areas; `internal` modules are only used by composition modules (`:app-common`, `:app-k9mail`, `:app-thunderbird`).
* Adding build checks to prevent accidental dependencies on `internal` modules.

## Tasks

- [x] Update documentation
- [ ] Build automatic checks

Samsung S10

### Steps to reproduce

The last two updates changed the path for switching top folders from "quick and unconscious" to "excessive and mindful".
Before:
- swipe from left
- click on account
- click on top folder

Now:
- swipe from left
- click on accounts
- read freshly unfolding accounts list and select the right one
- carefully click on the little arrow behind the parent folder to unfold it
- click on top folder


### Expected behavior

Have a quick way to access a folder that is explicitly marked as "show on top".

### Actual behavior

The new path requires a lot of thinking and careful finger targeting:
- The accounts list is hidden after the swipe and unfolds only on a second click, into the area previously used by folders. This leaves little time for mental preparation and requires mindfully targeting the selection after unfolding it.
- Subfolders show only after unfolding the parent folder, even if they are marked as "show on top". And again, they unfold into an area previously used by other names, which requires mental adaptation.

Common operations shouldn't require _any_ thinking at all, let alone careful finger targeting.
Switching accounts should be quick and easy, definitely not require more than one click.
Folders marked as "show on top" should show at the top, even if they are subfolders.

title: Account Setting Key Migration
body:
As [suggested ](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/10077#discussion_r2528575680) during the review of PR #10077, the preference key used for the “Expand all folders by default” setting should be renamed to better match its corresponding title.

However, this preference is already in use by existing users, which means renaming the key outright would cause their saved value to be lost. To avoid breaking existing behavior, we need to introduce a migration strategy.

**Tasks**:
- Define a new, clearer key name that aligns with the setting title.
- Implement a migration step that:
   - Reads the value stored under the old key.
   - Writes it into the new key.
   - Removes (or safely ignores) the old key afterward.
- Update all references to use the new key.
- Verify preference loading and default values behave as expected after migration.

title: Enable Memory Tagging Extension (MTE) Support on MTE-Capable Devices
body:
Enable [Memory Tagging Extension (MTE)](https://source.android.com/docs/security/test/memory-safety/arm-mte) on MTE-capable devices (Pixel 8 and later) to improve memory safety.
Although TFA doesn’t include explicit native code, it bundles `.so` libraries (likely from Compose) and interacts with Android framework components that use native code. Since TFA processes untrusted input (emails), enabling MTE adds a simple, effective layer of defense-in-depth.

Notes:
Successfully tested on a Pixel 8a (GrapheneOS, MTE force-enabled) without issues. Recommended to verify on an official MTE-compatible device.

**Rollout Plan:**

- **Phase 1:** Enable MTE for daily and debug builds and test internally on MTE-capable devices.
- **Phase 2:** If stable, roll out to beta builds for broader testing.
- **Phase 3:** If no major issues are observed, enable for release builds.

**Status:**

- **debug, daily:** no issues
- **beta:** released in 15.0b1 -> no issues
- **release:** in preparation

**References:**

* [Android MTE documentation](https://source.android.com/docs/security/test/memory-safety/arm-mte)
* [Introduction to ARM MTE blog post](https://thore.io/posts/2025/09/introduction-to-arm-memory-tagging-extensions/)

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

14.0b1

### Where did you get the app from?

Other

### Android version

13 (xiaomi.eu 14.0.3.0.TJUMIXM)

### Device model

Xiaomi POCO X3 Pro (global)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Thunderbird 13.0b5 and add accounts
2. Update to 14.0b1
3. Try to fetch messages

### Expected behavior

New messages arrive.

### Actual behavior

There are no new messages.

### Analysis

It looks like upgrade `91` that should add column `account_id` to table `messages` is not applied. I did not have time for analysis, but `DB_VERSION` is 90, while this column is added in version 91.

https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/d46a19dfb3fdcba9c1dbdcabf5b2ac9aa026a191/legacy/storage/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/storage/StoreSchemaDefinition.java#L15

Probably related:

- #9791
- #9722

title: Debug menu
body:
### Scope

- Provide a centralized UI for debugging without external tools.
- Allow non-engineers (QA/PM) to flip feature flags safely during testing.
- Make logs discoverable, searchable, and shareable from within the app.

### Out-Of-Scope

- Not a replacement for production-grade observability or remote config.
- No persistent remote sync of flags (local-only for now).
- No alteration of the app’s release build behavior unless explicitly allowed.

### Requirements

- Access:
  - Debug Menu is available only in `debug`/`daily` builds by default.
  - Optionally unlockable in `release`, `beta` with a hidden gesture and an additional confirmation warning.
- Feature Flags:
  - List all known flags with current values.
  - Toggle boolean flags.
  - Persist changes locally (survive app restarts?).
  - Expose a “Reset to defaults” action.
- Logs:
  - Display an on-device rolling buffer of recent logs (min 2,000 lines or 1–5 MB; configurable).
  - Filter by level (`VERBOSE/DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR`) and by tag.
  - Search text query across visible logs.
  - Ability to copy selected lines and “Share” as a text file attachment.
  - Option to clear the in-memory log buffer.
- Safety:
  - Changing flags applies immediately where feasible, otherwise after app restart (with do you really want to restart prompt).
  - Add visual indicators when non-default flags are active.

### UX Outline

- Entry point: from app’s settings menu within → `Debugging`. 
  - Optionally: tap app version 7 times on About screen to reveal in non-debug (store a flag in prefs).
- Debug Menu tabs or sections:
  1) `Feature Flags`
     - List of flags with current value, type indicator, and description.
     - Toggle/switches for booleans; dropdowns for enums; text fields with validation for strings/ints.
     - Buttons: `Reset All`
  2) `Logs`
     - Toolbar: Level filter, Tag filter (autocomplete), Search box.
     - Paginated/virtualized scrolling list of lines: `[time] [level] [tag] message`.
     - Buttons: `Clear`, `Share Logs`.

title: Resource Leak or Mismanagement
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

K-9 Mail

### App version

9.0b3

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

11

### Device model

Google Pixel

### Steps to reproduce

**Describe the bug:**
Our team is developing a tool that can automatically identify potential resource issues in Android applications.

To detect resource anomalies, we designed five **neutral cycles**—GUI event sequences that should not increase resource usage:

① **DOC (Double Orientation Change)**
② **Home (Return to Home Screen → Resume AUT)**
③ **Notification (Open Notification Bar → Close Notification Bar)**
④ **Text (Input Text → Clear Text)**
⑤ **Scroll (Swipe Down/Right → Swipe Up/Left)**

The first three cycles are designed to trigger **3 main pairs of lifecycle callback functions** (i.e., onCreate() and onDestroy(), onStart()/onRestart() and onStop(), onResume() and onPause()), while cycles ④ and ⑤ are based on UI interaction semantics, covering user **input** and **scrolling** scenarios that may also affect resource usage.

If executing a specific neutral cycle 50 times in a given state leads to continuous growth in certain resource metrics, we regard it as a potential **resource leak or mismanagement issue** that may cause software aging.

body:

title: Improve the Android CI setup
body:
We currently have two GitHub workflows: the older monolithic `android-ci` and the newer, more granular `android-pr`. These workflows trigger many unnecessary runs on pull requests and are not configured to effectively reuse the Gradle cache.

We should merge them into a single workflow and optimize Gradle cache usage to prevent excessive cache evictions. Building the `app-common` module should be sufficient to contribute to the shared cache.

1. Convert both classes from Java to Kotlin.
2. Maintain singleton pattern using private constructor + companion object.
3. Use idiomatic Kotlin features:
  - `when `expressions for validation
  - `mapNotNull `instead of manual loops
  - Null safety (?., ?:, etc.)
  - Avoid redundant operations (e.g., Base64 decoding)
4. Logging should be consistent using a dedicated TAG constant.
5. `parseAllAutocryptHeaders`/`parseAllAutocryptGossipHeaders `should accept `Collection<String>` for flexibility.
6. Preserve existing functionality and validation rules.
7. Add` @VisibleForTesting` annotations to parsing functions where applicable.

title: Add Interactions Subcategory and Migrate Volume Key Setting
body:
We need to introduce a new Interactions subcategory under GeneralSettings to group settings related to user interaction patterns.

As the first step, migrate the existing `K9.isUseVolumeKeysForNavigation` setting, which controls whether volume keys are used for navigating the message list, to the preference DataStore and place it under the new Interactions subcategory.

**Tasks:**
-  Create a new InteractionsSettings data class under **net.thunderbird.core.preference.interactions**.
-  Create` InteractionSettingsPreferenceManager`  under **net.thunderbird.core.preference.interaction** and provide it's implementation to handle reading and writing interaction settings to Preference DataStore.
- Add interactions: InteractionsSettings field to `GeneralSettings`.
- Update `GeneralSettingsManager `to read/write the new setting from **DataStore**.
- Migrate existing `K9.isUseVolumeKeysForNavigation` preference to the new DataStore-backed setting.
- Ensure UI for volume key navigation toggle reflects the new setting.

title: Migrate K9.isSensitiveLoggingEnabled to PreferenceDataStore
body:
The current implementation in Thunderbird Android directly accesses the static field K9.`isSensitiveLoggingEnabled `to determine whether the to show sensitive information in log or not. This approach bypasses the modern `PreferenceDataStore`, which is the preferred mechanism for managing application settings.

This task involves refactoring all direct references to K9.`isSensitiveLoggingEnabled `and replacing them with proper usage of PreferenceDataStore. This will improve consistency, testability, and alignment with the app’s current architecture for preference management.

title: VERBOSE logs are hidden when "Enable debug logging" is selected and will never be shown, even in debug builds
body:
There are some verbose logs that are emitted only when "Enable debug logging" is selected and will never be shown, even in debug builds, because of minimum `DEBUG` level when this setting is enabled:

- Guarded by `K9MailLib.isDebug()`:
  - 6 in `RealImapConnection.kt`
  - 1 in `XOAuth2ChallengeParser.java`
  - 1 in `ImapResponseParser.java`
- [`StorageEditor.putStringWithLogging`](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/a3e80598c5ecbeb9fc1fc86ed83f7ad3b3e50880/legacy/core/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/preferences/GeneralSettingsWriter.kt#L40-L59) if `isDebugLoggingEnabled` argument is `true` (all callers get this from `generalSettingsManager.getConfig().debugging.isDebugLoggingEnabled`)

F-Droid ### Android version 13 ### Device model _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce Try to read the text of read emails in the message list when using a dark color scheme and being in a bright environment, e.g. outside in the sun. ### Expected behavior You should be able to read everything without problems. ### Actual behavior You can't, since https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/9565 ### Logs The original problem (unread messages can't be easily distinguished from read ones anymore) https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/8448 is claimed to be fixed by https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/9565. Technically, it is – but actually, it only exchanged this problem with another one, because the way unread messages are displayed was not changed, but the way the read ones are. This leads to the problem that the list of read messages has a real bad contrast when using a dark color scheme, esp. surfacing when you try to read through them in a bright environment (outside, sun, with sunglasses): … and this screenshot is way more readable on a desktop computer's screen than on a mobile "in the wild". This may be associated with the general complaint about the dark color mode filed recently at https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/9684. I know it's hard to please all (or at least the majority of) users. I'm a KDE Dev myself. Thus I don't want to bitch about this or nag you again and again, but leave constructive criticism here. This is not really a bug or asking for a new feature. It's a regression. We did have a perfectly working dark color scheme until recently, one could distinguish read from read messages and could read both types in the messages list effortlessly, also in a bright environment. The color scheme was changed, and now everybody complains. I'm pretty sure you use K-9 Mail yourselves, some in a dark mode. And I'm pretty sure you noticed the problems yourselves. If not, just try in real life, on a mobile. Please consider to revert this color scheme change, instead of tinkering on the new one. It has a severe negative impact on the usability of the whole app – otherwise, one would not see so many complaints, to the point that users think about switching to another mail app after years. Thanks in advance for considering this, or at least fixing the contrast problem. And thanks for taking your users seriously!

title: Android workflow doesn't use cache
body:
I observed that the android workflow is not consuming the Gradle cache produced by the
gradle-cache workflow. This is because of GitHub changes on how caches work, see: [Using the cache read-only](https://github.com/gradle/actions/blob/main/docs/setup-gradle.md#using-the-cache-read-only) and [Restrictions for accessing a cache](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#restrictions-for-accessing-a-cache)

As the android workflow is never excecuted on the main thread it will never write to the Gradle cache. We need to fix this.

title: ZWJ emoji as account symbol only shows the first element of the emoji
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

11.0

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

GrapheneOS 16 Build 2025081400

### Device model

Pixel 9a

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to Settings
2. Edit one account
3. General Settings
4. Account name
5. Put any [ZWJ Emoji](https://emojipedia.org/emoji-zwj-sequence) as the first character, e.g. 🐦‍🔥 (Phoenix)

### Expected behavior

In the account overview the account symbol is the phoenix

### Actual behavior

The account symbol is 🐦 (Bird, the first symbol of the ZWJ sequence)

In the settings the emoji is correctly displayed as phoenix.

### Logs

> The Phoenix emoji is a [ZWJ sequence](https://emojipedia.org/emoji-zwj-sequence) combining [🐦 Bird](https://emojipedia.org/bird), [Zero Width Joiner](https://emojipedia.org/zero-width-joiner) and [🔥 Fire](https://emojipedia.org/fire). These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.

https://emojipedia.org/phoenix-bird

Note there can also be longer sequences like [Family with two kids](https://emojipedia.org/family-man-woman-girl-boy) 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦

_

Let me say thank you for introducing the possibility to customise the account symbol with two letters or a single emoji.

Seems like the one emoji instead of two characters was even implemented purposefully instead of two emojis.

title: Logging - Enable debug logging option not providing useful data
body:
After our recent changes to the Logging API, the "Enable debug logging" option is no longer providing useful data. 

We now use the `Logger` interface for logging, which uses the `CompositeLogSink` to determine whether any logging should occur. As a result, the log level remains unchanged, and logs are not displayed in the logcat. Additionally, the `CompositeLogSink` has its own `LogLevel`, which overrides the log levels of the individual sinks. This makes it impossible to update the log level at runtime, as it is defined as a singleton through Koin.

As a result, when exporting logs using `logcat -d` within `LogFileWriter`, there are no useful logs available.

title: Folders on IMAP servers with prefixes are completely broken since 12.0b4
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report. - [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. ### App Thunderbird for Android ### App version 12.0b4, 12.0b5 ### Where did you get the app from? Other ### Android version 13 (xiaomi.eu 14.0.3.0.TJUMIXM) ### Device model Xiaomi POCO X3 Pro (global) ### Steps to reproduce Requires an IMAP mail server that uses prefix for non-INBOX mailboxes (e.g. GMail - #9616). #### Variant 1 - fetching folder 1. Fetch list of folders 2. Open any folder other than _Inbox_ (e.g. _Spam_ - `INBOX.Spam`) 3. Load messages/refresh #### Variant 2 - deleting messages 1. Make sure that there is a trash folder (e.g. `INBOX.Trash`) 2. Delete a message from inbox ### Expected behavior #### Variant 1 - fetching folder Messages from the selected folder are fetched from server (e.g. using command `EXAMINE "INBOX.Spam"`) and displayed. #### Variant 2 - deleting messages Deleted message is moved to the trash folder. ### Actual behavior #### Variant 1 - fetching folder Command `EXAMINE "INBOX.INBOX.Spam"` is sent and obviously fails, because there is no such folder. #### Variant 2 - deleting messages Command similar to `UID MOVE 27707:27708,27714:27715 "INBOX.INBOX.Trash"` (here I was deleting multiple messages) is sent and also fails. This leads to a desync, because messages end up in the local trash, disappearing from inbox, but still exist on server and are shown to other clients. I was wondering why desktop Thunderbird and webmail showed 15 more unread messages than Thunderbird for Android and thought it is a weird sync problem. ### Regression analysis This regression is caused by #9241 that was uplifted to beta in #9523 (I guess now some of the associated risk is known) and released in 12.0b4. `serverId` is _absolute_ - it includes folder name including the prefix. Previously most folder `serverId`s were "old server IDs" and [had the prefix removed](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/commit/74cbed1bdb1375cb15014b16cd75463b48f60071#diff-b88fcb0b0a4fbe9cda33c13ffc19bf81f7bc110a545cf81e24c87532fdef03b5L193-L203). Now folders are initialised with `serverId` that contains prefix, but commands either use `encodedName` which is just [`folderNameCodec.encode(prefixedName)`](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/5a296ceaccbb5c4976cd109119f8a6135c376b40/mail/protocols/imap/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/mail/store/imap/RealImapFolder.kt#L98-L102) or directly call `folderNameCodec.encode(folder.prefixedName)` ([`copyMessages`](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/5a296ceaccbb5c4976cd109119f8a6135c376b40/mail/protocols/imap/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/mail/store/imap/RealImapFolder.kt#L309-L310) and [`moveMessagesUsingMoveExtension`](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/5a296ceaccbb5c4976cd109119f8a6135c376b40/mail/protocols/imap/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/mail/store/imap/RealImapFolder.kt#L345-L346)) - in either case [`prefixedName`](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/5a296ceaccbb5c4976cd109119f8a6135c376b40/mail/protocols/imap/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/mail/store/imap/RealImapFolder.kt#L73-L96) is used and [`prefixedName`](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/5a296ceaccbb5c4976cd109119f8a6135c376b40/mail/protocols/imap/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/mail/store/imap/RealImapFolder.kt#L73-L96) prefixes the `serverId` (that already has prefix). ### Logs

### Checklist - [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report. - [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. ### App Thunderbird for Android ### App version 12.0b4, 12.0b5 ### Where did you get the app from? Other ### Android version 13 (xiaomi.eu 14.0.3.0.TJUMIXM) ### Device model Xiaomi POCO X3 Pro (global) Requires an IMAP mail server that uses prefix for non-INBOX mailboxes (e.g. GMail - #9616). #### Variant 1 - fetching folder 1. Fetch list of folders 2. Open any folder other than _Inbox_ (e.g. _Spam_ - `INBOX.Spam`) 3. Load messages/refresh #### Variant 2 - deleting messages 1. Make sure that there is a trash folder (e.g. `INBOX.Trash`) 2. Delete a message from inbox #### Variant 1 - fetching folder Messages from the selected folder are fetched from server (e.g. using command `EXAMINE "INBOX.Spam"`) and displayed. #### Variant 2 - deleting messages Deleted message is moved to the trash folder. #### Variant 1 - fetching folder Command `EXAMINE "INBOX.INBOX.Spam"` is sent and obviously fails, because there is no such folder. #### Variant 2 - deleting messages Command similar to `UID MOVE 27707:27708,27714:27715 "INBOX.INBOX.Trash"` (here I was deleting multiple messages) is sent and also fails. This leads to a desync, because messages end up in the local trash, disappearing from inbox, but still exist on server and are shown to other clients. I was wondering why desktop Thunderbird and webmail showed 15 more unread messages than Thunderbird for Android and thought it is a weird sync problem. ### Regression analysis This regression is caused by #9241 that was uplifted to beta in #9523 (I guess now some of the associated risk is known) and released in 12.0b4. `serverId` is _absolute_ - it includes folder name including the prefix. Previously most folder `serverId`s were "old server IDs" and [had the prefix removed]([URL] Now folders are initialised with `serverId` that contains prefix, but commands either use `encodedName` which is just [`folderNameCodec.encode(prefixedName)`]([URL] or directly call `folderNameCodec.encode(folder.prefixedName)` ([`copyMessages`]([URL] and [`moveMessagesUsingMoveExtension`]([URL] - in either case [`prefixedName`]([URL] is used and [`prefixedName`]([URL] prefixes the `serverId` (that already has prefix). ### Logs

Thunderbird for Android

12.0b4

### Where did you get the app from?

Other

### Android version

13 (xiaomi.eu 14.0.3.0.TJUMIXM)

### Device model

Xiaomi POCO X3 Pro (global)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to Settings -> "General settings" -> Debugging
2. Enable all options (debug logging, sync debug logging, log sensitive information)
3. Refresh a folder
4. Export logs or observe logcat output

### Expected behavior

Logs include IMAP/POP3 commands sent to the mail server and received responses, as well as other debugging information (number of unsynced messages, etc.)

### Actual behavior

There is no useful debugging information in debug logs (see below for an example). This makes debugging problems with message synchronisation much harder.

This problem does not exist in debug builds, but most people who submit bug reports will most likely run a release version. In my case a debug build (from beta branch) synchronises correctly, but the release (12.0b4) downloaded from archive.mozilla.org doesn't, so I only have debug logs from a version where everything is ok...

#9250 introduced logging changes that prevented messages with level lower than INFO (VERBOSE and DEBUG) from being logged at all. #9359 changed the minimum log level to VERBOSE, but only for debug builds. Most log messages enabled by the "Enable debug logging" option are DEBUG or VERBOSE, so enabling this option does almost nothing.

title: Android 16/OneUI 8 (Samsung): New Mail notifications not happening/erratic
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

11.0b5

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

Android 16 and One UI 8 

### Device model

Samsung Galaxy Flip Z 7

### Steps to reproduce

Set up TBird with default install, add an account. (I have 3 Gmail and 2 IMAP). Use normal polling for new Mail check, not push. Close the phone (which locks it). Send new Mail to the account from some other system. 

### Expected behavior

The cover screen (and lock screen when phone is open) should show a new mail envelope notification. This worked on a Z Flip 5 running Android 15 and One UI 7. Other applications have their notifications appearing during this time.

### Actual behavior

No new mail notification appears for quite some time with the screen closed (sometimes never, sometimes hours). Even opening the TBird app after unlocking the phone will sometimes not show a notification until forcing a mail check manually - then notifications will appear as expected for current email. Closing the phone again will suspend the notifications.

### Logs

Just upgraded from A15/OneUI 7 to A16/OneUI 8. was running TB 11.0b5 on the old system, and notifications worked as expected with the phone closed. On the A16/OneUI 8 system the notifications are not appearing as they did - sometimes missing entirely. I also am running 11.0b5 on a Pixel Tablet with "pure" Android 16, and notifications show on the lock screen as expected.

title: Use Kover to calculate the test code coverage
body:
Currently, our project lacks comprehensive code coverage reporting for most modules, despite having some areas covered by tests. The existing Jacoco setup is incompatible with Kotlin, which limits its effectiveness.

To improve our testing infrastructure, we're transitioning to [Kover](https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx-kover) as the code coverage tool. 

To begin, we will aim to achieve a minimum target of 50% code coverage, but will not enforce this threshold initially due to the large proportion of the untested code.

title: Write a contribution guide
body:
While the overall architecture of the Android app is well-documented, there remains a need for clarity on contributing to the project. Many potential contributors are unclear on what tasks they can undertake, what expectations exist for code quality and submission, and how to integrate their work seamlessly into the existing codebase.

To address this knowledge gap, it would be beneficial to create a comprehensive contribution guide that provides more detailed information on:

* Code writing standards and best practices
* How to structure contributions (e.g., feature requests, bug fixes)
* Guidelines for testing, review, and validation processes
* Best practices for integrating new code with existing dependencies and modules
* Translation instructions are outdated and should be split into weblate and project specific docs

By establishing a clear contribution guide, we can ensure that all team members, including external contributors, have a solid understanding of their responsibilities and the expectations for high-quality contributions.

title: Swipe actions not available to TalkBack users
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

11.0b4

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

14

### Device model

Pixel 5

### Steps to reproduce

1. Turn on TalkBack.
2. Open Thunderbird.
3. Open a folder.
4. Navigate with TalkBack to one of the messages in the message list.

### Expected behavior

- Tapping with three fingers on the message brings up the TalkBack menu. One of the options is "Actions", which allows the user to choose the left or right swipe actions.
- Swiping up or down on the message cycles through the left or right swipe actions.

### Background

To better serve Thunderbird users with TalkBack enabled, I’d like to request [Accessibility Actions](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/ui/accessibility/principles#accessibility-actions) be added to the message list.

The available actions should at least match the currently configured [swipe actions](https://blog.thunderbird.net/2022/11/thunderbird-android-update-k-9-mail-6-400-adds-customizable-swipe-actions) (Toggle selection, Mark as read/unread, Add/remove star, Archive, Delete, Spam, or Move). 

An example of an Android app with Accessibility Actions is Raccoon, a social media client for Mastodon and Friendica. (See their [commit #567](https://github.com/LiveFastEatTrashRaccoon/RaccoonForFriendica/pull/567) for the rationale.)

- Each post has several buttons below it: reply, reshare, add to favorites, add to bookmarks, and options. 
- If Accessibility Actions were not enabled, then when navigating with TalkBack, the user would encounter each of these buttons, one at a time.
- Instead, with Accessibility Actions enabled, TalkBack only stops once at each post. The buttons are not focused. Instead, TalkBack tells the user: “Actions available. Swipe up or swipe down and double tab to activate.”
- The user can swipe down to cycle through the following actions: reply, reshare, add to favorites, add to bookmarks, link to poster, options, or activate which loads the post into a view by itself, equivalent to tapping in the post body.

#### Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e22caaf-ef40-4126-84b0-a9326838b35d

[Demo transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21101880/raccoon-demo.txt)

This setup allows users to quickly browse posts with a minimum number of swipes, while still having access to quick actions.

By contrast, the official Android Mastodon app iterates through each button under each post. There appears to be no way to jump from one post to another, so browsing a timeline with TalkBack is more time-consuming.

### Implementation in Thunderbird

- An example use case for Thunderbird is: a user is browsing newly arrived messages. Several messages are marketing emails, and the user chooses to delete them directly from the timeline. The user saves time by not navigating to each email individually.

- I believe Accessibility Actions are popular with blind users, based on [these poll results from 23 Feb 2025](https://a11y.social/@dankeck/114054760188213623 ) where 77% of the 30 respondents like using them. 

- It’d be important to do some user research to determine which actions should be included. Bonus points if the actions and their ordering are configurable. This way, a user's most-used action can be available with just one swipe.



### Actual behavior

No Accessibility Actions are available to the user. 

### Logs

_No response_

To better serve Thunderbird users with TalkBack enabled, I’d like to request [Accessibility Actions]([URL] be added to the message list.

The available actions should at least match the currently configured [swipe actions]([URL] (Toggle selection, Mark as read/unread, Add/remove star, Archive, Delete, Spam, or Move). 

An example of an Android app with Accessibility Actions is Raccoon, a social media client for Mastodon and Friendica. (See their [commit #567]([URL] for the rationale.)

- Each post has several buttons below it: reply, reshare, add to favorites, add to bookmarks, and options. 
- If Accessibility Actions were not enabled, then when navigating with TalkBack, the user would encounter each of these buttons, one at a time.
- Instead, with Accessibility Actions enabled, TalkBack only stops once at each post. The buttons are not focused. Instead, TalkBack tells the user: “Actions available. Swipe up or swipe down and double tab to activate.”
- The user can swipe down to cycle through the following actions: reply, reshare, add to favorites, add to bookmarks, link to poster, options, or activate which loads the post into a view by itself, equivalent to tapping in the post body.

#### Demo

[URL]

[Demo transcript]([URL]

This setup allows users to quickly browse posts with a minimum number of swipes, while still having access to quick actions.

By contrast, the official Android Mastodon app iterates through each button under each post. There appears to be no way to jump from one post to another, so browsing a timeline with TalkBack is more time-consuming.

### Implementation in Thunderbird

- An example use case for Thunderbird is: a user is browsing newly arrived messages. Several messages are marketing emails, and the user chooses to delete them directly from the timeline. The user saves time by not navigating to each email individually.

- I believe Accessibility Actions are popular with blind users, based on [these poll results from 23 Feb 2025]([URL] ) where 77% of the 30 respondents like using them. 

- It’d be important to do some user research to determine which actions should be included. Bonus points if the actions and their ordering are configurable. This way, a user's most-used action can be available with just one swipe.

No Accessibility Actions are available to the user.

title: Migrate K9.isHideTimeZone to PreferenceDataStore
body:
The current implementation in Thunderbird Android directly accesses the static field `K9.isHideTimeZone` to determine whether the Time Zone header should be removed from outgoing emails. This approach bypasses the modern PreferenceDataStore, which is the preferred mechanism for managing application settings.

This task involves refactoring all direct references to `K9.isHideTimeZone` and replacing them with proper usage of PreferenceDataStore. This will improve consistency, testability, and alignment with the app’s current architecture for preference management.

title: Migrate K9.isHideUserAgent to PreferenceDataStore
body:
The current implementation in Thunderbird Android directly accesses the static field `K9.isHideUserAgent` to determine whether the **User-Agent** header should be removed from outgoing emails. This approach bypasses the modern PreferenceDataStore, which is the preferred mechanism for managing application settings.

This task involves refactoring all direct references to `K9.isHideUserAgent` and replacing them with proper usage of PreferenceDataStore. This will improve consistency, testability, and alignment with the app’s current architecture for preference management.

title: In-App Notifications - Create in-app notification table
body:
Some types of errors require more attention from the user. For this reason, certain notifications are classified as both system notifications and in-app notifications.

When a fatal error occurs while the application is not running, we need to send a system notification to inform the user about the issue. Additionally, we must ensure that the error is displayed when the user opens the app again.

To achieve this, instead of merely ignoring the in-app notification, we should store it in a database. This way, we can retrieve it when the app is reopened and show a persistent notification to the user.

title: Automate f-droid releases
body:
I think we should take care of this now, otherwise we'll never do it and it will be annoying every time. We currently need to submit f-droid builds manually. There is an opportunity to automate it based on tag updates, but our files aren't ready for this because it uses regex. I think we have two options:

#### 1) Adjust build files to a regexable format
- Set https://f-droid.org/docs/Build_Metadata_Reference/#AutoUpdateMode to enable auto updates
- Set https://f-droid.org/docs/Build_Metadata_Reference/#UpdateCheckMode to Tags and add the appropriate tag pattern
- Set https://f-droid.org/docs/Build_Metadata_Reference/#UpdateCheckData to read from either the respective build.gradle.kts, or a separate version.txt file.
- Adjust our CI especially release process so that version.txt or build.gradle.kts is correctly adjusted.

Upside here is that it is all automated, we adjust our version files once and then f-droid does the rest. Downside is that once we tag (which is early), f-droid will pick it up, so we have no way to hold a build. We should make sure that the regex is fairly stable, so that we don't accidentally break this by changing something in build.gradle.kts and it maybe picks up the wrong version.

#### 2) Add a build step after publish_hold that will send a pull request to f-droid
- Add a step that checks out fdroiddata, updates the yml files, makes sure their linters pass
- Create a pull request such as https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/merge_requests/24167

Upside is that we do it after the publish_hold step and it is similar to the play store review. Downside is they have to manually review each pull request.

#### 3) Defer tagging in our builds until after publish_hold

- Make it so that tagging only actually happens after the publish_hold is confirmed
- Continue same steps as in (1)

Upside is that we can hold builds also for those who use FFUpdater or similar. The build is only considered a release once the publish step completes. We get the upsides from (1) as well. The only downside is that this is more effort since we're making some major adjustments to our release process.

title: Replace Direct Calls to K9.isThreadedViewEnabled with PreferenceDataStore integration
body:

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch K9-Mail
2. On the Welcome screen (or tap “Get started” to go to the account-setup flow), rotate the device to landscape orientation.
3. Try to swipe up or down anywhere on the screen to scroll.

### Expected behavior

The entire screen surface (including the blank left/right margins) should respond to drag gestures and scroll the content up or down,

### Actual behavior

Only the central content panel where text and form fields appear accepts scroll gestures.

Swiping on the empty areas at the left or right edges of the screen does not scroll; the gesture is ignored.



### Logs

### Additional information

- On taller-screen devices, the empty left/right margins become much larger, so an even bigger area is non-scrollable.  
- On shorter-screen devices, those margins shrink, but the scroll-dead zone still remains outside the central panel.  
- In all cases, only the central content area accepts vertical drag gestures; swiping on any blank margin (regardless of its size) does nothing.

title: Convert XML screens to Compose
body:
The goal is to gradually replace XML based views / screens with composables. The view should be a 1 to 1 conversion with minimal changes to the design. If there are better alternatives in the design system they should be preferred .

## In scope

### Settings (global + per-account) and About

- Entrypoints:
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.SettingsActivity` (main settings hub)
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.general.GeneralSettingsActivity`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.AccountSettingsActivity`
- Fragments and related pieces:
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.AccountSettingsFragment`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.AccountSettingsViewModel`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.AccountSettingsDataStore` + `AccountSettingsDataStoreFactory`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.AccountSelectionSpinner`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.AboutFragment`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.SettingsActionItem`, `UrlActionItem`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.OpenPgpAppSelectDialog`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.AutocryptPreferEncryptDialogFragment`, `AutocryptPreferEncryptPreference`

### Accounts, Identities, and Folder management

- Accounts & identities:
  - `com.fsck.k9.activity.AccountList` (accounts overview)
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.settings.account.ManageIdentities` (legacy Java) and `com.fsck.k9.activity.EditIdentity`
  - `com.fsck.k9.activity.ChooseIdentity`
- Folder management:
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.managefolders.ManageFoldersActivity`
  - `com.fsck.k9.ui.choosefolder.ChooseFolderActivity`

### Message source, changelog, push info, confirmations

- `com.fsck.k9.ui.messagesource.MessageSourceActivity`
- `com.fsck.k9.ui.changelog.RecentChangesActivity`
- `com.fsck.k9.ui.push.PushInfoActivity`
- `com.fsck.k9.ui.notification.DeleteConfirmationActivity`
- Generic dialogs: `com.fsck.k9.fragment.ConfirmationDialogFragment`, `com.fsck.k9.view.HighlightDialogFragment`

### End-to-end encryption flows (Autocrypt)

- `com.fsck.k9.ui.endtoend.AutocryptKeyTransferActivity`
- `AutocryptKeyTransferPresenter`, `AutocryptKeyTransferViewModel`
- `AutocryptSetupMessageLiveEvent`, `AutocryptSetupTransferLiveEvent`

### Base UI and shared legacy views

- `com.fsck.k9.view.RecipientSelectView`, `ContactBadge`, `StatusIndicator`, `NonLockingScrollView`, `LinearViewAnimator`, `ToolableViewAnimator`, `ViewSwitcher`, `ThemeUtils`, etc.

## Out of scope

1. Message Compose -> #8837
2. Message List + Search -> #8838
3. Message View + Attachments + Crypto status/details -> #8838

title: Default signature placement creates cluttered email threads and breaks signature stripping
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report. - [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. ### App Thunderbird for Android ### App version 10.0 ### Where did you get the app from? F-Droid ### Android version Android 15 ### Device model Nothing Phone 1 ### Steps to reproduce Hi, Thunderbird for Android allows users to configure a signature that is always appended to emails when they're sent from that particular account. Signatures are configured under "Settings -> select your account -> Sending mail -> Composition defaults". However, the signature is appended to the wrong part of the message body. This is because the default configuration for signature placement is "Settings -> select your account -> Sending mail -> Composition defaults -> After quoted message" What this means in a real life scenario is that if the user has an ongoing email thread with several earlier correspondences, and they reply from their mobile into that thread today, their signature is put at the very bottom at the entire thread after everybody's every reply. I can list at least 4 reasons why this doesn't make sense: - Nobody reads the bottom line of a long email thread with several replies. Essentially this behaviour makes signatures invisible to recipients. - After a few replies, the bottom lines of the email thread will be nothing but a bunch of signatures one after another, as seen on the attached screenshot. Additionally, signatures get mixed and recipients won't be able to tell which signature belongs to which correspoindence. - Signatures lose their contextual connection to the actual message they belong to. - No sane user would expect signatures to work this way :) Additionally, this breaks the "Settings -> select your account -> Sending mail -> Strip signatures on reply" functionality. Even with that feature enabled, signatures are **not** stripped from replies as I guess we can't find them where they are supposed to be. **I recommend that we make 'Before quoted message" the default behaviour for account signatures and perhaps remove "After quoted message" altogether. Alternatively, if we don't remove "After quoted message" because it covers some special use case, fix "Strip signatures on reply" to work with this option.** --- **Incorrect behaviour with the default "After quoted message""** **Correct behaviour with "Before quoted message"** ### Expected behavior Place signatures right after the new reply content but before the quoted previous messages, as seen with 'Before quoted message" enabled. ### Actual behavior The current default is "After quoted message" which doesn't make any sense in most real world scenarios, if ever. ### Logs Don't think logs would help anything here, but happy to provide them if required for the fix.

title: Unified Inbox selection not remembered
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [x] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App

Thunderbird for Android

### App version

10.0

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

Android 15

### Device model

Nothing Phone 1

### Steps to reproduce

There are two problems here but I believe they stem from the same underlying issue, that is, that the default view for each account appears to be its own Inbox.

**Repro 1**
- Install App
- Configure at least 2 email accounts
- Click on the hamburger menu at the top left
- Select "Unified Inbox"
- Click on the "create new email icon" at the bottom right
- At the top left, next to "Compose", click on the "changed my mind" (back) arrow
- Notice you land in your account's Inbox, not in the Unified Inbox where you came from.

**Repro 2**
- Install App
- Configure at least 2 email accounts
- Click on the hamburger menu at the top left
- Select "Unified Inbox"
- Click on the hamburger menu again
- Click on the account name at the top to switch to another account (imagine you just wanted to double check the email address of that account or its folder structure)
- Observe that you immediately land on the individual account's Inbox, rather than staying in Unified Inbox that you have previously selected.


### Expected behavior

For **Issue 1**, if the user comes from Unified Inbox and cancels a draft email, the back arrow should take the user back to the Unified Inbox, where they came from, not to a completely different folder.

For **Issue 2**, just because the user switches accounts, to check for the account's email address or a particular folder, if Unified Inbox was selected before, the selection should be retained, unless the user explicitly selects another folder.

### Actual behavior

Whenever a draft email is cancelled, or a switch between accounts is made, the selection resets to the given account's own Inbox.

### Logs

Don't think logs will be of any use here, but happy to provide them if needed.

### Steps to reproduce
