title: Vietnamese translation issue
body:
Dear, 

The Vietnamese translation has been 98% completed through hosted.weblate for many months. And I have also seen many commits that update the Vietnamese strings.xml into the source code.

But for some reason, I don't see Vietnamese appearing in the app display language selection list in the K-9 Mail.

I once encountered a similar situation with Stremio, their dev forgot to add a language array, causing Vietnamese not to appear even though it was in the source code. Please check it with K-9 Mail.

title: Folder polling is not reliable any more
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.803 (still happening with Thunderbird for Android 16.1)

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

14 (still happening with 16)

### Device model

Pixel 7a

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the app to poll for new emails every 15 minutes.

title: Add note about OpenPGP public key being included in all outgoing messages
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.802

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

LineageOS 20.1 (Android 13)

### Device model

Fairphone 4

### Steps to reproduce

1. add a account as usual
2. enable OpenPGP on that account by selecting a key
    - do not change any other settings concerning OpenPGP / Autocrypt
    - (esp. "Autocrypt mutual" should be disabled)
3. send a new (unencrypted & unsigned) mail to yourself
4. open the newly received mail & check the headers

### Expected behavior

IMO it is reasonable to expect that this mail does not contain an AutoCrypt header with my configured OpenPGP key. I think so because K9-Mail does not declare that additional data might be shared, hence (at least in the EU regarding GDPR) it should only share data which is technically required to send that mail. As that mail is not encrypted & not signed and as mutual encryption was disabled, K9-Mail is not technically required to submit my public key.

### Actual behavior

The sent mail contains an `Autocrypt` header containing the configured OpenPGP key.

### Additional Info

Issue #4836 already reported this misbehavior, but that issue was mostly ignored and did not discuss the potential legal issue arising from that behavior. Because this report is from ca. 4 years ago, I decided to open a new issue.

I understand that it is useful to automatically attach the public key to all outgoing mails, I see following problems in the current implementations:
- The current behavior is neither explained to the user nor can it be specifically disabled. And IMO there are use cases for using OpenPGP without Autocrypt.
- The current behavior can result in a leak of personal data, especially in combination with the multiple identities feature. E.g. if a user does want to send a mail from an anonymous alias and its provider allows this by simply using a different FROM address, K9-Mail can leak the identity of that user. Or that users PGP key might contain additional information they do not want to share with every mail (e.g. secondary mail addresses).
- IMO the current behavior is illegal under GDPR, because that behavior is non-optional, not explained to the user and not technically required for the service the users are expecting (sending an unencrypted, unsigned mail).

title: Decide on Git Branching Strategy
body:
As our Android application grows, we need to establish a robust Git branching strategy to improve our development, testing, and release processes.

Currently, we use a maintenance branch for patches and bug fixes post-release, testing changes in a beta version before merging back. However, this method isn't always followed consistently, leading to issues. For more details see [RELEASING.md](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md) and update #7800.

With our growing team, we need to reassess if the current strategy efficiently handles our development needs.

## Action Points

1. **Define Requirements:** Define requirements based on our project needs and team feedback. This will guide our choice of a Git branching strategy that best fits our needs.
1. **Evaluating the Current Strategy:** Discuss the pros and cons of our maintenance strategy and explore ways to enhance adherence.
2. **Comparing Alternatives**: Review GitFlow, GitHub Flow, and Trunk Based Development to identify a suitable model.
4. **Development vs Maintenance**: Strategies for managing stable production with feature development.
5. **Communication and Collaboration**: Enhance communication and collaboration, especially for maintenance and new features.
6. **Continuous Integration and Testing**: Improve integration and testing processes to ensure thorough testing of patches.
7. **Documentation**: Document the selected strategy in an Architecture Decision Record and update developer documentation.

## Proposed Alternatives

1. **[GitFlow](https://www.atlassian.com/de/git/tutorials/comparing-workflows/gitflow-workflow)**: A structured model with separate branches for features, releases, and hotfixes, though potentially complex.
2. **[GitHub Flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow)**: A flexible, single-branch model suited for frequent releases and parallel changes.
3. **[Trunk Based Development](https://trunkbaseddevelopment.com/)**: Focuses on a single main branch with frequent merges, supporting continuous integration and quick iterations.

## Key Questions for the Team

1. What is the team's preferred development style, and how often do we want to release?
2. Which Git branching model aligns best with our team's workflow and goals?

## Ask for feedback and suggestions

Please share your thoughts and suggestions on the proposed branching strategies to refine our approach for our Android app development.

title: [EPIC] White Label Architecture
body:
We will be implementing a modular white-label architecture to improve the development process for our Thunderbird for Android and K-9 Mail applications. This new structure will allow us to configure brand-specific details either during build or at runtime while maintaining a consistent core functionality. The proposed (#7805) architecture consists of application modules and a common module as follows:

**Application Modules:**

1. Thunderbird for Android: `app-thunderbird`
2. K-9 Mail: `app-k9mail`

These modules will contain app-specific implementations, configurations, resources, and startup logic. They will only depend on the `app-common` module for shared functionalities and selectively integrate other modules as needed to configure app-specific functionality.

**App Common Module:**

1. `app-common`: This module will act as the central integration point for shared code among the applications. It will contain the core functionality, shared resources, and configurations that are common to both apps.

### Tasks

- [x] Create `app-thunderbird` and `app-k9mail` modules for application-specific code and configurations and include them in the project structure
  - #7494
  - #7779
- [x] Create a `app-common` module containing shared functionality, resources, and configurations for both applications. #8000
- [x] Create an app name provider #7924
- [x] Migrate code from the existing structure to the new modules while ensuring minimal disruption to ongoing development.
- [x] Migrate app widgets to work with both apps #7933
- [x] Provide necessary documentation and resources for developers to help them get started with the new architecture.
- [x] Test the new architecture thoroughly to ensure it meets our performance, scalability, and security requirements.

title: Discussing Minimal Standards for Code Contributions 🚀
body:
## Description

To maintain a high quality of code and to streamline the review process, it is necessary to establish minimal contribution standards for this project. This will ensure that all contributions are consistent and align with the project's goals and coding practices.

## Suggested Standards

1. **Code Quality:** All contributions must adhere to the specified coding guidelines of the project, which include but are not limited to naming conventions, code structure, design patterns and commenting.
2. **Testing:** Contributions should include unit tests that cover new features or bug fixes. All tests must pass before contributions are considered for merging.
3. **UI Tests:** For UI-related changes, appropriate UI tests must be included where applicable. This ensures that the visual and interactive aspects of the application function as expected across different devices and configurations.

title: The app doesn't undo local changes when the associated remote operation fails
body:
Currently we don't undo local operations when a remote operation fails. For example, when a user deletes a message, we move the local copy to the local trash folder, then try to perform the move operation on the server. If that remote operation fails, we don't move the local message back to the local source folder so the local state reflects the (unchanged) state on the server.

Related: #1058

The deleted Mail gets moved to the trash folder on the Server

- Create and delete a draft via K9.
- Move a mail from the trash to the Inbox via K9.
- Delete a mail from the inbox of my gmx Email account via K9.

### App version

6.801

### Problem you are trying to solve

I am trying to read an email that uses "advanced" HTML features.

### Suggested solution

K9 should allow basically all HTML. Presumably only the following should be blocked:

- Scripting
- Remote content loads (when not allowed)

This would allow email authors to better control the formatting and provide a better reading experience.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

I originally noticed this issue because I wasn't seeing some expected padding. I eventually figured that this was because it was applied on an `<article>` element and K9 uses a whitelist (https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/main/library/html-cleaner/src/main/kotlin/app/k9mail/html/cleaner/BodyCleaner.kt). (I assume, I haven't read the source too closely.)

At first I thought I would just extend the list, but it seems like a small step and maybe a bigger solution is ideal. It seems that K9 is using a full browser engine to render the mail so it should be possible to input any HTML. This is just like how Thunderbird desktop works. I don't think there is any major issue with this approach. The whitelist already allows any CSS so there is little more that can be done. I guess `<video>`, `<audio>`, `<object>` and `<iframe>` may be interesting. But Ideally those would be implemented with a generic block on remote content. (Actually it would be nice if `<video>` and `<audio>` were allowed, if not automatically when clicking at least when remote-content is enabled).

title: [Android 15] Switch `foregroundServiceType` of `PushService`
body:
Android 15 introduces [restrictions on BOOT_COMPLETED broadcast receivers launching foreground services](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-15#fgs-boot-completed). We do start `PushService` when receiving the `BOOT_COMPLETED` broadcast. So we'll have to switch to a different `foregroundServiceType` value. 

We could either go with [`remoteMessaging`](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fg-service-types#remote-messaging) or [`specialUse`](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fg-service-types#special-use).

title: IMAP: Rename "Send client ID"
body:
In the "incoming server settings" screen users can configure whether the [ID command](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2971) should be sent to the IMAP server (including the app name and version as arguments).

Right now this setting is called "Send client ID". But to avoid confusing it with the CLIENTID mechanism from [draft-yu-imap-client-id-11](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-yu-imap-client-id-11), we should rename this setting. I think a good option for a new name is "Send client information", mostly because the relevant setting in Thunderbird is named `mail.server.default.send_client_info`.

In addition to changing the user-visible string we should also change all associated variable and parameter names.

title: Decide on generic prefix for the default implementation of an interface
body:
Right now we have lots of interfaces that have only one implementation. The name of the implementation for the interface `Interface` is usually `PrefixInterface`. But we use quite a few different values for the prefix (`K9`, `Real`, `Default`). 

Whenever possible we should use a descriptive prefix, e.g. `DatabaseMessageStore` for a `MessageStore` implementation that stores messages in a database.

However, sometimes it's not easy to come up with a descriptive prefix. In those cases we should use a standard prefix. And it probably shouldn't be `K9`, unless the implementation is specific to K-9 Mail (see #7718).

Once we've decided on a prefix, we should rename existing classes that use a different generic prefix.

title: Decide on prefixes for app-specific classes/function names
body:
We need to decide on prefixes for app-specific classes for both K-9 Mail and Thunderbird for Android. This is mostly for app-specific implementations of an interface. But maybe also for app-specific compose functions, e.g. `K9Theme` and `TbTheme` (although in this case maybe having them called `K9MailTheme` and `ThunderbirdTheme` is not a big deal, because those are usually used on a single line together with only an opening brace).

I'm suggesting `K9` for K-9 Mail and `Tb` for Thunderbird for Android. These have the advantage of being short. Which feels important when the interface name already has 3+ components, e.g. `OAuthConfigurationFactory` (→ `K9OAuthConfigurationFactory`/`TbOAuthConfigurationFactory` vs. `K9MailOAuthConfigurationFactory`/`ThunderbirdOAuthConfigurationFactory`).

title: Add a confirmation action for permanently deleting emails
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.800

### Problem you are trying to solve

Prevent accidental deletion of emails in the "Trash", since after they're gone from there, they're gone for good.

One scenario when this can happen (as it just did to me):
You delete an email from inbox, then realize you still had to check something. You go to the trash to get the email back, and verify what you needed to. Then, when you're done with it, you may forget that it's already in the trash, and so you click the "Delete" button again; it's gone for good.

### Suggested solution

Add something similar to the Outlook for Android implementation (default), where a confirmation message is shown before being able to delete an email from the "Trash" folder, and which specifies that the deletion will be permanent.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

Add a new action to the already existing "Confirm actions" menu of the Interaction settings section; maybe something called "Delete (in Trash)".

![Screenshot_20240308-152951-452](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/assets/94257099/df3f6343-f5b1-43be-91cd-ddf272d7dba1)

I would assume that, by default, the confirmation message for these actions are generic, and so if this new action was to be implemented, having a personalized message (like done by Outlook devs) would be beneficial. Otherwise, a user who has multiple confirm actions enabled might confirm without thinking twice, which defeats the whole purpose of the confirmation feature.

Alternatively, you can use a notification to inform the user of the task's progress.

We need to find a replacement for the various places the `ProgressDialog` is used.

title: SMTP for forward-only addresses
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.603

### Problem you are trying to solve

SMTP-only accounts and per-identity SMTP support have been requested previously, but this use case hasn't been satisfactorily addressed.

Here's the problem:

I have an e-mail forwarding account provided by a professional organization.  It has NO inbox.  All mail sent to that account is forwarded to a server I control and appears in the inbox of my server.  That server has several traditional identities that use a local SMTP server.

The local SMTP server can not send from the forwarded address - it fails spf/dmarc and recipients such as gmail bounce any attempt to do so.  Instead, I'm required to send using a SMTP server associated with the professional organization.  (Actually, they outsource to mailroute.net, but it's the same thing.)

In K-9 ("the app"), I can setup an account for this identity that uses the correct SMTP server.  But there is no INBOX.  That leaves me with specifying an invalid IMAP server and setting Poll to never.  And so there is ONLY an OUTBOX.

I can read e-mail to the forwarded address from the account on my server.

But to send from the forwarded address, I have to switch accounts.  Compose/send.  But I can't see the inbox.  So then switch back to see replies or other mail that I need to respond to.

I can't "upload sent messages" because there's no Sent folder - again, just an Outbox.  So I have to Bcc myself, and then manually move the Bcc to Sent..

This is a lot of manual work just to be able to send from the correct identity.


### Suggested solution

SMTP servers should be first class objects, as in Desktop Thunderbird.

Identities should be able to be associated with any SMTP server.

In my case:

The forwarding address would be an identity under my server.  Outbound mail from that identity would use the special SMTP server.  Inbound mail for that identity would appear in the target inbox via it's IMAP server.

Then I can read the mail associated with that identity, and respond all from the same account.  Switching would only be necessary to among identities, not accounts, 

(I do not use a "unified inbox"; my identities are distinct.)

title: Fix support for server settings with authentication type "None"
body:
Currently we don't have an `AuthType.NONE` value that signifies that no authentication should be used (we support this for outgoing servers). The "no authentication" option is currently encoded by using an empty username and password. However, the new server settings screen doesn't properly support this (see https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/7524#issuecomment-1968795638).

Instead of making the server settings screen support the existing encoding, I suggest we add an `AuthType.NONE` value and make `ServerSettings.username` optional by using the `String?` type.

title: Improve SSL connection handling
body:
While working on #7655 I noticed that we use a quite dated implementation to establish SSL connections. As we would like to raise the bar in terms of security (level needs to be decided). This is a good starting point for improvements. 

The classes to look at:
-  `DefaultTrustedSocketFactory` implementation of `TrustedSocketFactory` for all mail backends
   - creates it's own `SSLcontext` and injects `TrustManagerFactory` and `KeyChainKeyManager`
- `TrustManagerFactory` - internally uses a custom `SecureX509TrustManager` which is error prone and not advised
- `KeyChainKeyManager` - Android 4.0 KeyChain API

These need to be evaluated and updated to latest security best practises or replaced by a solid and secure 3rd party solution. Also they are lacking any tests, it would be advised to add them to protect against accidential behavior changes and verify that it works as intended. Also there is no documentation describing the intended behavior.

title: "Remind me of this email" feature
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.710

### Problem you are trying to solve

Receiving new emails that imply some task/response one would like to work on later is annoying as
 - one can either open the email but then needs to use a separate todo app to remind oneself about it later or,
 - one could refrain from reading the full email to make the notification stay there in order to not forget working on it later.

### Suggested solution

A "Remind me of this email" feature would solve the issue.
This has been worked on in this really old PR: https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/1849 - however it was then closed, by reasoning as follows:

> 1. I think "hiding" messages is an important part of a snooze feature. How that's accomplished technically is another matter (I like the 'move to another folder' approach).
> 2. The 'notify again' time doesn't seem to be persisted anywhere. That'll break the feature e.g. when the device reboots. In my opinion a reminder functionality that doesn't work reliably is worse than none at all.
> 3. Right now nothing is preventing snoozed messages from being removed from the device, e.g. when they fall outside the sync window.
> 4. There's no visual indicator for a snoozed message. Also, no way to un-snooze.

Regarding point 1. and 4., I think it boils down to personal preference/the idea one has of the feature whether "snoozed" emails should be hidden. If it's more a "remind me" feature (like Slack has), than a "snooze this email" feature, I see no need at all to hide the email. In fact, I'd think it's better UX to not hide and just re-trigger the notification after a while as one can then still read the email (e.g. while on the go), ponder about what to do with it, and therefore work more efficiently on it later (when being back home). Therefore, at least as a first step I think a remind me feature could/should be implemented without hiding the email in the app. This is a lot less work too, as I understood it. Consequently, point 4. is also not strictly necessary anymore then - a little icon indicating that a reminder has been set would surely be nice but is not _required_ to obtain a solid UX in my eyes.

Regarding point 3.: This is a valid point and I don't know how much work it is to prevent these messages from being removed from the device or to re-fetch them later. Maybe some internal progress since 2016 has also improved this situation in k9 already (?). In either case, while having/making the email still available when the user clicks the notification would surely be better, I think it wouldn't be a deal breaker for this feature if the email is gone then - this should rarely happen as I'd assume the "remind me" feature is rather intended for short term uses (a few hours) than days, making it unlikely emails disappear that fast. Also - is there any difference to leaving notifications intentionally open for that time in the current app? Is there anything that prevents those emails from being removed from the device? If not then this should not be a requirement for this feature either.

This makes point 2. the only remaining blocker for the feature implementation from the PR. But from my experience, I'd assume scheduling a permanent reminder is not that much of an effort (I have never worked with the k9 codebase though).

I opened this as a new issue to start a discussion on what UX is intended for this feature as suggested in the PR from 2016. There has been [this](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/1549) related issue, but I don't think the discussion there has been very constructive. It has been closed because of the different interaction model connected to a snooze feature - however this does not apply to a "remind me" feature as I described here.

I really think this feature would be extremely useful to lots of people. It would definitely save me from a lot of (if not any) worries and annoyances in my day to day life with k9 mail.

That being said, weighting estimated implementation effort against usefulness, I would definitely not say this feature should be low priority (as the snooze feature was classified to be before).

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

A popup to select reminder time can be opened by either of the following means:
- clicking an action on the push notification of an email
- tapping a context menu action of an email in the inbox list view
- swiping an email to the right in the inbox list view
- tapping a toolbar button or menu entry in the email details page.

In the popup, one can select common reminder times like "30 mins", "1 hour" etc. Optionally, more "sophisticated" times like "this evening, 19pm" or "tomorrow morning, 9am" could also be suggested. Potentionally, these times could be configurable in the app settings. Also potentionally there could be an Option to set a custom reminder time in the popup.

title: Improve translation process
body:
The process for updating supported app languages, as outlined in [docs/translations.md](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/blob/main/docs/translations.md), involves manually updating the `language_values` in `arrays_general_settings_values.xml` and `language_entries` in `arrays_general_settings_strings.xml`. 

This approach is suboptimal because it requires keeping the indices of these two declarations aligned and also requires adherence to the Unicode default collation order for `language_entries`.

To improve efficiency and reduce the potential for errors, we should automate this process or try a different approach.

title: Let's encrypt certificates stop working for Android 7.0 and earlier beginning Feb 8th, 2024
body:
Let's encrypt is phasing out their certificate [cross-signing](https://letsencrypt.org/2020/12/21/extending-android-compatibility.html) that allowed Android Devices prior to 7.1.1 to establish TLS connections.

They've announced that it will [phase out](https://letsencrypt.org/2023/07/10/cross-sign-expiration) begining Feb 8th, 2024. 

This will result in a `java.security.cert.CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor for certification path not found.` exception for every domain that renewed their certificate after that date or creates a new one.

We need to change to a trust store that trusts ISRG Root X1.

title: VersionCode should be autogenerated to ease release automation
body:
To streamline our release automation process, it would be beneficial to implement an automatic version code generation strategy rather than relying on manual updates.

Reviewing the [Firefox for Android project](https://github.com/mozilla-mobile/firefox-android/blob/main/focus-android/tools/gradle/versionCode.gradle), I found they use a date-based system for generating a unique and sequentially increasing `versionCode`. Their method utilizes the format `yDDDHHmm`, where:

- `y` represents the last digit of the year minus 16 (e.g., 2017 becomes 1)
- `DDD` is the zero-padded day of the year (e.g., September 6th is 249)
- `HH` for the hour of the day (00-23)
- `mm` for the minute within the hour

This approach stays within the maximum allowed `versionCode` of 2,100,000,000, typically producing a 9-digit code, ensuring each version is unique and sequentially higher than the last.

I propose we adopt a similar, date-based calculation for our version code, incorporating the same format `yDDDHHmm`:

- `y`: The number of years since a base year, with 2024 as the starting point (e.g., 2024 is 0)
- `DDD`: The day of the year in 3 digits, zero-padded
- `HH` The hour of the day in 2 digits (00-23)
- `mm` The minute of the hour in 2 digits

For example:

- 2024-02-09 16:45 -> 0 | 040 | 16 | 45 -> 401_645 -> 6 digits
- 2025-10-12 09:23 -> 1 | 285 | 09 | 23 -> 12_850_923 -> 8 digits
- 2123-02-09 16:45 -> 99 | 040 | 16 | 45 -> 990_401_645 -> 9 digits

Alternatively the format `ymmmmmm`, with even more head room but harder to read:

title: Remove dependency substitutions
body:
We use dependency substitution in our root `build.gradle.kts` file to fix some transient dependency versions. This imposes challenges maintaining the build and dependency updates:

- Substitutions make it more challenging to track which dependencies are beeing used, especially when substituting transient dependencies.
- Can lead to hidden version conflicts, especially when substituted dependencies depend on different versions of dependencies. Imposes risk of runtime errors that are hard to diagnose and fix.
- Gradle's dependency resolution can become more complex and slow down the build process.
- Substituted dependencies might not be fully compatible with the Android version that we target.

However, in some scenarios, dependency substitution might be necessary to resolve conflicting version of a library or there is a need to apply a patch that is not available through the official repositories. In such cases, thorough testing is required to not introduce side effects that surface at runtime.

We should remove the dependency substitutions and improve the dependency declarations to pin transient dependencies where needed. 

We could try the [dependency analysis gradle plugin](https://github.com/autonomousapps/dependency-analysis-gradle-plugin), to help resolve issues with our dependency declaration.

1: settings , account settings

4: Mail appears to send, but later the notification appears:

Failed to send some messages
From header must be equal to ....

Where the ... is e.g. graeme@mydomain.com (the initial identity) 





### Expected behavior

I use Thunderbird on Linux to send main email. This is entirely because **I can set the from header** (the only other way is the use sendmail directly on the command line). So my outgoing email is always from:

graeme.\<companyname\>@mydomain.com  ... never graeme@mydomain.com

Then, as usually happens they sell my e-mail address and I start to get SPAM,  I block that address.

Currently I can't send email while away from the house (and a desktop Linux system) . The move of K9 to be Thunderbird for mobile meant I was finally able to send email "on the move"

The UI seems a little different. I expected to just be able to type in the **from** line in each mail message. It seems I had to go through the steps to create an new identity of each and every company I deal with (so this list is going to grow to hundreds)  ...Thunderbird does have this concept of create a new identity , I also use this for example to use encryption with certain people, but I one need one or two of these.

I see there are feature requests to allow the direct edit of the from header and I'd add my voice to those, but in the meanwhile I would expect the message to send.

FYI: I did a wireshark trace and I did not see any traffic from K9 to the SMTP server, so it looks like the bug is "local" ... I know my MTA will accept the graeme.name format as this is what I do on every email via Thunderbird



### Actual behavior

Failed to send some messages
From header must be equal to ....

(AFYI I tried the graeme+name@  style and this failed in t he same fashion.

none

title: High priority notification even if "do not disturb" enabled
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.603

### Problem you are trying to solve

Ability to provide a high priority notification if an important email is received.  This could be based on subject or based on sender.  High priority should be able to override "do not disturb" setting if needed and be an option by user for each topic/sender.

### Suggested solution

Example scenarios where immediate attention is required and "do not disturb" should be ignored (by user selection)
- Sensor in home detects water leak and sends email notification which is critical
- Utility notifies of potential water leak
- Important contact (spouse, business associate, etc) sends message that you are waiting for
- Important topic (home purchase details, etc)

There are lots of reasons why an email might be critical to know about as soon as received.  If it comes in at night, it might be important enough to be woken up for.  Push notifications work if both parties are on them but sometimes email is the only mechanism to send such a message.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

I have been using K9 for years and have never seen this feature though looked in app many times.  I searched the github but found nothing.  The K9 community forum seems to be offline so I don't see any other vehicle to make such a request.

title: Enhancing Test Code Contributions: Clear Guidelines for Better Collaboration
body:
As dedicated contributors, we all appreciate the straightforward guidelines enforced by Spotless and Detekt when adding test code to our project. These automated checks make contributions a breeze.

Yet, there's a layer of complexity that remains unaddressed. Buried within our existing test code are 'hidden' rules, not immediately apparent to contributors. Much of this code is outdated. Relying on outdated examples to decipher these rules is far from ideal and a shaky foundation for assumptions.

It's time we demystify these unwritten rules. Clear, accessible guidelines are not just a convenience—they are a necessity for efficient and effective collaboration.

We recognize the need for transparency and ease in our contribution process. Here's our action plan to smooth out the contribution process:

1. **Prioritize Automation:** Whenever possible, let's encode our rules into our automated systems. This step will not only save time but also ensure uniformity across contributions.
2. **Documenting the Undocumented:** When automation isn't feasible or is too resource-intensive, we'll create a clear, concise set of guidelines. This 'Dos and Don'ts' list will be a valuable resource, guiding contributors away from common pitfalls and aligning everyone with best practices.

By implementing these steps, we aim to make contributing a more seamless, frictionless experience. Let's work together to enhance our project's code quality and maintainability.

title: Optimise Lint configuration for translation issues and weblate
body:
Lint has a set of default checks that look for translation issues. But our translation tool Weblate also comes with a set of checks. We should lower the severity to WARNING for those checks that are already validated by weblate.

This leaves legacy issues:
- We transfered translations from our previous translation tool into weblate. These have not been reviewed or checked again after the transfer.
- Not all modules in the project are checked by lint yet. So there are still undiscovered issues, that go beyond translation issues.

We also need to define what to do with those lint findings.

title: [Account setup] Don't allow navigating back to transient special folders screen
body:
When special folders are automatically configured by the server, the user only sees transient screens ("Fetching list of folders…" and "All special folders have been configured automatically by the server"). Currently we allow the user to change the special folder assignment anyway. That's also why we allow the user to navigate back to this screen. 

![image](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/assets/218061/104f8059-0f0c-4f0b-bb53-89190cb4de9b)

We've now decided that we want to keep things simple and don't allow users to change the special folders assignment (during account setup) when the server provided a complete mapping. In that case, the success screen is completely transient and we don't need the "Edit special folders" or "Next" buttons. When navigating back from the following screen, the special folders screen should be skipped.

However, if the server didn't provide a complete mapping, we prompt the user to configure special folders. In that case, navigating back from the screen that follows, should display that special folders screen again.

title: [Account setup] Prefill server text field in manual setup flow
body:
When the app can't find a configuration, users have to manually specify the server settings. In the past we've suggested a server name (e.g. imap.EMAILDOMAIN). The idea was to save the user time typing the server name when there's a good chance our suggestion (partially) matched the actual server name. However, often the name wasn't correct but users assumed the app auto-detected the value. So they went ahead and tapped the "Next" button, only to get an error when checking the server settings.

To avoid the above scenario we could suggest the name ".EMAILDOMAIN" (e.g. `.domain.example` when the user's email address ends in `@domain.example`). It has the advantage of being an invalid hostname. So users will see an error message when tapping the "Next" button without making a change.

![image](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/assets/218061/78764dbb-fb95-4f20-8127-ff6e181718f1)

### Problem you are trying to solve

I have a Dovecot IMAP server configured with OAuth2 with Authelia as OAuth2 backend. After adding an entry for my server to `app/k9mail/src/main/java/com/fsck/k9/auth/AppOAuthConfigurationFactory.kt`:
```kotlin
private fun createLebihanConfiguration(): Pair<List<String>, OAuthConfiguration> {
    return listOf(
        "lebihan.pl",
    ) to OAuthConfiguration(
        clientId = "myapp",
        scopes = listOf("openid", "profile", "email", "groups"),
        authorizationEndpoint = "https://auth.lebihan.pl/api/oidc/authorization",
        tokenEndpoint = "https://auth.lebihan.pl/api/oidc/token",
        redirectUri = "${BuildConfig.APPLICATION_ID}://oauth2redirect",
    )
}
```
I was able to successfully authenticate with my OAuth2 backend. Adding every email server configuration to that file however isn't very practical. K-9 should automatically retrieve that configuration.

title: Improve Message List for TalkBack users
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.603

### Problem you are trying to solve

- Navigating the message list on thunderbird-android using TalkBack is cumbersome, because TalkBack users have  to perform multiple swipes to get to the next or previous message in the message list.
- If a TalkBack user needs to perform an action on a message in the message list, like delete, they have to long press on a message and then find the buttons to perform a desired action. And if the user wants to move or copy a message, they have to long press on it, then  find the "more options" button, where they will find the options to move or copy the message. This becomes tedious and reduces efficiency.

### Suggested solution

- When navigating through the message list, TalkBack should only focus on the message and not on buttons like "Select". 
The message and the visible buttons should be added to [content groups](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/ui/accessibility/principles#content-groups) and buttons like "Select" should be added as an [accessible action](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/ui/accessibility/principles#accessible-actions)
- Consolidate all the available actions for a message in TalkBack actions.
To access TalkBack actions for a particular element, open any app that supports TalkBack actions (like Gmail).
Then focus on an element that has TalkBack actions (like a message).
Later, swipe up or down on the screen using one finger to hear all the available actions and double tap to perform that action.

If the "Continuously active VPN" function is activated, Thunderbird should recognise when the flight mode is switched on or no network connection is available.

title: Permanently acoustic notifications probably by K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, but in most cases no new emails in Inbox
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.711

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

Android 10

### Device model

LG K50 s

### Steps to reproduce

When my smartphone generates acoustic notifications probably invoked by K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, in most cases no visual notifications about new mails in the Inbox of K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android gets displayed on the Launcher Screen of my smartphone and no new mail has arrived in my main email account at my mailhoster, or such a visual notification gets displayed on the Launcher Screen for maximally one second and then disappears, but in fact a new email has arrived, but this time in the Inbox of the alias email account of my main email account at my mailhoster, and this new mail is displayed in the corresponding folder in by K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android and in the email program KMail on my laptop.

When I notice an acoustic notification by my smartphone, I first check the Launcher Screen if it displays a visual notification about a new email in K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, and if the Launcher Screen does not display such a visual notification I check my main mail account at my mailhoster with its alias mail account in the email program "KMail" on my laptop, and in most cases in K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android, too. In most cases it appears that now new mail had arrived in my main email account at my mailhoster.

Sometimes in these situations as described above, the acoustic notifications are not fully generated regarding their length, i. e. they get abruptly stopped before they reach the end of their acoustic signal sound file.

How often does this behavior occur?

To give you an impression about how often this behavior occurs: This morning between 5 and 7 A.M. my smartphone generated 3 acoustic notifications, while in these three cases no new mail had arrived in the Inbox of my main mail and alias mail account.

While I am writing this bug report, my smartphone has generated appr. 10 times such a "ghost" acoustic notification until now. OK, I am a little bit slow in writing this report because my mother tongue is not English. I think it will take me two hours to write and finally save this bug report here.

Some days ago my smartphone generated more often these "ghost" acoustic notifications than compared to today's morning. Like every 20 minutes or so. Note that the version of K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android installed some days ago (6.6xx) was older than the version which is currently installed on my smartphone (6.711). Today I updated K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android to its newest available version in the F-DROID store.

Note that the behavior described above occurs at home. I did not take my smartphone out of my apartment since about two weeks. My smartphone uses Wi-Fi at home to be connected to the Internet via my router.

I think that the behavior described above started from the moment on when I had changed the Wi-Fi name of my router (its SSID) here at home. In the settings of my router I added the text string "_optout_nomap" at the end of the name of the SSID of my router, i. e. this way:

"<SSID>_optout_nomap"

According to Mike Kuketz, a German IT security and data protection specialist, this SSID name extension tells Microsoft, Google and other similar providers (location mapping services) not to process such SSID's for registering their location geo data, which are used to locate the positions of smartphones and other devices. This information can be found (in German) in chapter "WLAN-SSID: Opt-Out" here:

https://www.kuketz-blog.de/empfehlungsecke/

Note that I am using K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android in connection with OpenkeyChain on my smartphone, and that the adblocking app Adaway is running on my smartphone with several active ad blocking filters.

This afternoon I logged one of these "ghost" acoustic notifications on my smartphone using the logging/debugging functionality of K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android. This "ghost" acoustic notification which I logged occurred today at 14:58 o'clock German Winter Time.

This is what K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android has logged today at 14:58 o'clock German Winter Time:

[Note: Having uploaded this quote from the K-9 Mail log file, I noticed that it does not properly gets displayed here, although I used the "code" tags for that. I will upload the quote of the log file separately, just a moment, please.]

General description of how I set up K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android:

- K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android accesses one main email account at my mailhoster which has one alias email account which K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android accesses, too. Incoming mails in the main email address and in the alias email address are both shown in the the Unified Inbox.
- Access to these two mail addresses at my mailhoster via IMAP
- Push is not activated at all
- K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android retrieves (looks for new) mails every 15 minutes

I could upload the exported settings of my K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android setup, but I would do that first, if you think that there is something strange documented in the log information above.

### Expected behavior

K-9 Mail/Thunderbird-Android should only notify me with acoustic notifications about new emails in the Inboxes of my main email account and of the alias mail account. 

### Actual behavior

Refer to section "Steps to reproduce"

title: Can't see true sender anywhere when using Firefox Relay
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.603

### Where did you get the app from?

None

### Android version

8.1.0

### Device model

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

1. Receive an email from an alias address provided by Firefox Relay 
  1.1. One can easily be set up for free at https://relay.firefox.com/
2. In the overall inbox/folder view (where multiple message previews are shown): notice that the original subject is displayed, but the sender is listed as the relay address, and the sub-header / preview text is "This email was sent to your alias...". On its face this behavior may make sense, as the "sender" is technically the relay email, but it is not useful or helpful. I will contrast it to Thunderbird for desktop which lists in the "correspondents" column the useful and helpful value of "sender@domain.com [via Relay] <relay@mozmail.com>".
3. In the detailed view (after clicking on the message): The original sender is not displayed anywhere at all - instead it just shows relay@mozmail.com. Again I'll contrast this to Thunderbird desktop where the "from" field clearly shows who sent the message to the relay.

Note that item 3 and the issue title is not _strictly_ true, as you can click to view the headers when in the detailed message view and dig through all of those to find the original sender. However this is inconvenient, the sender is not easy to quickly see among numerous other technical headers, and finding the sender this way may never occur to an average non-technical user.

### Expected behavior

Allow me to view the true sender in the same way Thunderbird desktop does: 
original@sender.com [via Relay] <relay@mozmail.com>

### Actual behavior

Described thoroughly in steps to reproduce.

title: Figure out what to do about using (exact) alarms for refreshing push connections
body:
To refresh a push connection, we need to wake up the device. Currently we're using [AlarmManager.setExactAndAllowWhileIdle()](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/AlarmManager#setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(int,%20long,%20android.app.PendingIntent)). We don't really need exact alarms for this. A window could work. The alarm being triggered early is fine, being triggered late isn't. Unfortunately a `AlarmManager.setWindowWithHardDeadlineAndAllowWhileIdle()` method currently doesn't exist.

The use of exact alarms is denied by default on Android 14. See https://developer.android.com/about/versions/14/changes/schedule-exact-alarms

We'll have to figure out whether we can switch to using inexact alarms and still being woken up when the device has entered [doze mode](https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby#understand_doze). If not, we'll have to continue to use exact alarms and then need to add code to guide users to add the app to the exemption list.

title: Reply behavior violates RFCs when a List-Post header is present
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.603

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

10

### Device model

SM-G960U1

### Steps to reproduce

Reply to a message that contains a "sender" header

### Expected behavior

Address the reply to the address in the "From" header or to the address in the "Reply-To" header if present.

### Actual behavior

The reply is addressed solely to the address in the "Sender" header.

For several years a simple "reply" to a message sent via a mailing list
went solely to the address in a "List-Post" header, if present, rather
than to the original author in the "From" or "Reply-to" headers. 
That seems to have finally been fixed, but now, as of V6.603, a simple
reply is being sent solely to the address in the "Sender" header, if
present. 

Neither behavior is or was correct at any time, and the problem is
exacerbated by the "To" field in the reply composition containing only
"+1", so the person replying has no idea that this unexpected and
unwanted behavior is present.

Could we PLEASE conform to the relevant RFCs? A reply is to be addressed
to the "From" address(es) in the original message unless a "Reply-To"
header is present, in which case the reply is to be addressed there. Full
stop. A Reply-all should go to the "From" or "Reply-To" as well as to the
"To", "CC", and, if present "Bcc" addresses placed in the same headers
going back. 

From RFC 5322 Section 3.6.2 (updated but unchanged by RFC 6854): 

"The "From:" field specifies the author(s) of the message, that is, the
mailbox(es) of the person(s) or system(s) responsible for the writing of
the message. The "Sender:" field specifies the mailbox of the agent
responsible for the actual transmission of the message. For example, if
a secretary were to send a message for another person, the mailbox of
the secretary would appear in the "Sender:" field and the mailbox of the
actual author would appear in the "From:" field." 

"The originator fields also provide the information required when
replying to a message. When the "Reply-To:" field is present, it
indicates the address(es) to which the author of the message suggests
that replies be sent. In the absence of the "Reply-To:" field, replies
SHOULD by default be sent to the mailbox(es) specified in the "From:"
field unless otherwise specified by the person composing the reply." 

And from Section 3.6.3: 

"When a message is a reply to another message, the mailboxes of the
authors of the original message (the mailboxes in the "From:" field) or
mailboxes specified in the "Reply-To:" field (if it exists) MAY appear
in the "To:" field of the reply since these would normally be the
primary recipients of the reply. If a reply is sent to a message that
has destination fields, it is often desirable to send a copy of the
reply to all of the recipients of the message, in addition to the
author. When such a reply is formed, addresses in the "To:" and "Cc:"
fields of the original message MAY appear in the "Cc:" field of the
reply, since these are normally secondary recipients of the reply. If a
"Bcc:" field is present in the original message, addresses in that field
MAY appear in the "Bcc:" field of the reply, but they SHOULD NOT appear
in the "To:" or "Cc:" fields."

title: Don't trigger initialization code more than once when using `LaunchedEffect`
body:
We have a couple of places where a Composable kicks off (initialization) work in a `ViewModel` via `LaunchedEffect()`.

Example:
https://github.com/thundernest/k-9/blob/2125358e5cd3cb4a8eba665878124b2e99433726/feature/account/edit/src/main/kotlin/app/k9mail/feature/account/edit/ui/server/settings/save/SaveServerSettingsScreen.kt#L34-L36

However, an activity restart, e.g. after a configuration change, will trigger this again. This is rarely desirable. So either we use a different mechanism for initialization or we have to keep track of whether the (initialization) action has already been triggered and ignore subsequent events.

One alternative would be to start the initialization from an `init {}` block in the `ViewModel`. However, this can be fragile when the lifetime of the `ViewModel` doesn't match that of the screen. It could also make it a bit harder to test the initialization code.

However, an activity restart, e.g. after a configuration change, will trigger this again. This is rarely desirable. So either we use a different mechanism for initialization or we have to keep track of whether the (initialization) action has already been triggered and ignore subsequent events.

13

### Steps to reproduce

Add a minimum of 2 email adresses (issue noticed on IMAP) 
Choose an old incoming email to search for
Set emails to fetch to local folder so that the email will not be listed (local folder size 50, email in question Being number 51 or further back) 
Select an account other than the one that received the email
Go to unified inbox
Use that search menu to search for the email

### Expected behavior

The app should search all inboxes, folders etc all the way back in time. Or it should display the same "search everywhere" option and the magnifying glass (server search?) it displays when doing this in the account that contains the email.

"search everywhere" and server search in a different email address' inbox search menu will also not fetch the email. 

This would not be an issue if the app did not also lag severely with large inboxes if one sets inbox to fetch all emails from the address to local inbox ( issue #3472 ) 

I have looked through settings and am unable to find anything that allows unified inbox search to server search all accounts. Unsure if this is a bug, a feature not implemented or I have missed a way to enable this.

title: Create workflow running `spotlessCheck` when only Markdown files change
body:
Right now we [ignore changes to Markdown files](https://github.com/thundernest/k-9/blob/afb80619e5a663aa40e77616e157fc02ac84b917/.github/workflows/android.yml#L11) when running the Android workflow (that includes running `spotlessCheck`). However, `spotlessCheck` will also check Markdown files. 

So it's possible for a pull request to be merged that adds/changes a Markdown file violating some of our style rules (see #7215). And only the next pull request that triggers running the Android workflow will report a violation.

We should add a workflow that runs `spotlessCheck` when a Markdown file is changed and the Android workflow is not running anyway (e.g. because a code file was also changed).

title: Set the new unread email system notifications timestamps to match the email metadata's date and time from the IMAP server, instead of the time of notification emission
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.602

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

LineageOS 16.0 (Android 9)

### Device model

Any

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure IMAP folder "A" (ex: the inbox) and folder "B" to be 1st class / to emit notifications on new messages
2. In K-9 mail, go to folder "A", swipe the sidebar open to see the list of folders
3. In another email client elsewhere (i.e. a desktop email client, or webmail interface), mark one old email from folder A as unread, and move that email to folder B
4. In K-9, pull down the folders list to force a refresh (or wait for it to eventually periodically poll all folders by itself, but that would take longer)

Note: While this scenario might seem uncommon, this is actually also pretty close to how things might happen with email filters sometimes, depending on timing (for instance, I have some email filters that cannot be handled server-side, so they are handled client-side by my desktop email client, so there is some delay).

Alternate scenario / alternate way to reproduce:
1. Leave your phone disconnected, powered off or in "Airplane mode" for a while
2. Arrange for some new emails to come in to your email account
3. Reconnect your phone, and see K-9's notifications come in... probably with the wrong timestamps

### Expected behavior

Notify about the "new" unread mail, but set the notification's timestamp to the email's "received" timestamp, not the time at which the notification is emitted. This will keep them in chronological order and will help me go through them by priority.

### Actual behavior

New/unread email notifications are emitted to Android system notifications "with the current timestamp at the time at which the notification was created / when the check was done", instead of using the email's "date/time received" timestamp from the server.

So in practice, I might get 30 email notifications timestamped as "Now", in disorder, most of which do not actually require my attention, instead of the notifications reflecting the time at which the emails were received by the IMAP server.

### Logs

Here are some screenshots showing the mismatched notification timestamp using the 2nd method (airplane mode while an email gets received by the server, then reconnecting K-9).

First, notice the timestamp of the received mail (12h52) vs the current time (12h56):

![Screenshot_20230926-125659_K-9_Mail notification timestamp mismatch (crop pix)](https://github.com/thundernest/k-9/assets/479401/30fe6172-54d8-4a92-bf70-d7cb38a09d7a)

...then, notice the timestamp of the notification ("Now", i.e. 12h56):

![Screenshot_20230926-125643_K-9_Mail notification timestamp mismatch (crop pix)](https://github.com/thundernest/k-9/assets/479401/8d65215a-cf35-44bb-bf93-e139ae15bda2)

---

## Is this actually possible?

It would seem so; in comparison, some other Android mail clients (like FairEmail) are able to correctly set the notification timestamp in the past.

K-9 shows embedded mail like a quoted mail below the actual mail text.

--===============2691111782005021451==
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="us-ascii"

```

body:

- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.602

### Problem you are trying to solve

The default view in k9 is the unified inbox, which is great. It is currently possible to select several messages in the unified inbox and then delete them or archive them, but it is not possible to move them to a folder in a particular mailbox.

I understand that this is probably due to the fact that it might seem strange to move mail from one mailbox in to a folder of another mailbox BUT this feature is available in other clients and it is useful. It can be viewed as an instant forward of a mail to yourself.

### Suggested solution

My preffered solution for this would be to make it so that it is possible to move any piece of mail in the unified inbox in to any folder of any mailbox. However I would also think that it would be an improvement to be able to move multiple mails into a folder if and only if they are in the same mailbox (i.e. the move button could be greyed out if mails from several mailboxes were selected).

### Steps to reproduce

An Update of K9-Mail to the latest version led to a settings corruption and led to the problem mentioned in https://github.com/thundernest/k-9/issues/1547

I updated the App via F-Droid.

### Expected behavior

Expected behavior is probably to keep the unmodified settings when updating K9 Mail?

### Actual behavior

I updated the App via F-Droid.

When receiving E-Mails, everything behaved exactly the same (with the correct login methods on the server-side, using password authentication via imaps)

When sending/replying to E-Mails, the update changed the behavior, and started to use username@domain.tld as the login for username, and therefore failed on the server-side, which expected only "username" to be used for the AUTH step.

The response from postfix was kinda super useless in terms of googling the problem, because it was simply "<username@domain.tld>: sender address rejected. Not owned by user username." even though there were no aliases or anything fancy configured on the server-side, and the username itself is the owner of the mailbox username@domain.tld.

Afterwards, I verified on Thunderbird with identical client settings that the server is still working, while in parallel diffing all server configuration files to rule out that an update on the server changed the configuration files or implied defaults there.

When I didn't find any solutions online (and basically figured out that all stackoverflow answers are super useless on these keywords), I tried to clear the cache and storage of the Android App, Uninstall the App, went to the Files app to remove all remaining folders, and reinstalled K9-Mail.

Following the wizard with identical client settings for imap/smtp, it worked again.

I think there might have been a quirk when updating the app or that there might be a settings migration feature of an old settings format that led to the "username@domain.tld" being used behind the scenes, instead of using the "username" as a login!? That's the only way this bug makes sense to me, because in the UI the settings were identical and both using the "username" as the preferred login.

body:

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.

### App version

6.602

### Problem you are trying to solve

When starting K-9 Mail, it always opens the inbox of the first account. In many use cases this seems to be counterproductive:

- Mail sorting usually is done server-side (Sieve, for example), so incoming mails are stored in the defined folders. Not necessarily in the inbox.

- When using different accounts, the user needs to decide in which account he needs to work. Always opening the inbox of the first account is, in my opinion, not helpful.

### Suggested solution

The user should be able to select what is shown after starting the app.

- This could be a selectable message view of a selected folder in a selected account.
- But this also could be the folder list (sidebar) of a selectable account.
- In my use case, I would prefer to see the sidebar with the account list - so it is easy to see, how many new / unread mails every account has.

Go to an email with a very long email chain (causes reply to be shrunk at some point to single character lines)

1. Use an account with multiple identities.
2. Send an email to someone from an identity that is not the default.
3. Find the email within the Sent mail folder.
4. Select "Reply All" to send a follow-up email to the same recipients, from the same identity, or "Reply" to send a follow-up email to the same main recipient from the same identity.

### Expected behavior

K9 should behave the same way it does when replying to an email from the inbox:

When replying from the sent folder, it should identify that the From address in the sent email being replied to matches one of the identities defined in the account, and select that as the From address in the composed reply.

It seems this bug only exists when replying from the sent mail folder.

The bug is worse if you don't realise K9s error before you press send - assuming it will have chosen the from address correctly as it usually does, and so end up sending the email from the wrong identity, which has happened to me before.

### App version

6.700 on Android 7

### Problem you are trying to solve

This probably relates to closed #4653. After many years of using K9 on this device, a couple of months ago some deletions started failing to be actioned on the server. I mark several messages in the Unified folder, delete them, they disappear from the K9 list, and I close K9. When I check later on my desktop, Thunderbird downloads the supposedly deleted message from the servers. The more complex the deletion (ie several messages across several accounts) and the quicker I close K9, the more likely this will occur. 


### Suggested solution

My guess is that K9 correctly deletes the messages locally and queues the server instructions which are not executed before I close K9 either because K9 + my device are slow, or, more likely, because an unresponsive server delays the execution of the queued instructions. 

This didn't happen at all or as much before, so I am wondering if something has changed in K9. Could the process be accelerated by executing instructions on different servers concurrently? Otherwise, if the process can't be accelerated, could K9 continue doing its job in the background? If that's not possible, possibly because my overwhelmed Android kills the backgrounded task, can K9 indicate somehow that it is busy so that users wait before they close K9? 

I believe that the queued instructions are eventually executed if I wait long enough, force K9 to refresh, ~~or rerun it~~, but when none these happen and you find later that deleted messages are still on the server it is confusing and annoying. 

EDIT: When I rerun K9, the messages that were supposed to have been deleted previously, reappear and they show as unread too. This may be a bug after all.

Instead, we should return the input text as is.

title: Option to translate the IMAP special folders in the sidebar
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.509

### Problem you are trying to solve

Currently, the IMAP special folders (`Archive, Deleted, Drafts, Junk, Sent`) are not translated into the app language. I honestly think this is a design error:
1. It assumes that anyone is able to understand the English names for those folders.
2. The _Folder settings_ insinuate that the translations are to be used, only to show the folders untranslated in the sidebar. This is very confusing.
3. It is already abundantly clear what IMAP folder is actually used for the special folder inside the folder settings: they are explicitly mentioned when _Automatic_ is chosen. As such, there is no harm to use the translated names in the sidebar.

I just had a family member come to me in a panic, thinking they might have lost a long email they had just sent. I reckon this is definitely not the first time that would have happened due to this design choice.

What's more, imho it doesn't look tidy at all, and in the ensuing confusion, my first reaction was actually to check on Transifex if the translations were complete.

Related issues (this problem is mentioned, but it is not the core issue there): https://github.com/thundernest/k-9/issues/4300#issuecomment-564115499 and https://github.com/thundernest/k-9/issues/3449#issuecomment-781264989

### Suggested solution

Use the app translations for the special folder in the sidebar.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

title: Tap-to-scroll or Page turning for a better UX / UI on e-ink display
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.400

### Problem you are trying to solve

I use K-9 to read my e-mail on an e-ink tablet (Boox Max3) and an e-ink phone (Hisense A5).

Scrolling on an e-ink or e-paper display isn’t a great experience because it is slow, and leaves artifacts on the screen (like grey pixels remaining where black characters where printed)

Used to read my e-mails for years with a mutt client on GNU/Linux desktop, pressing space for viewing the next page is not a new thing, but with the lag of low fps display, it became a new necessity :-)

### Suggested solution

Having a tap-to-scroll option for passing to the next page, like what you can find in pdf viewer (or basically any pager like `more` on *nix systems).

This gesture could to be complementary to the swipe to go to next/prev message.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

Tap-to-scroll is exactly what it sounds like:
- By tapping on the right side (or bottom, or a button) of the screen, the page advances ~90%.
- By tapping on the left side (or top, or a button) of the screen, the page rewind ~90%.

Tap-to-scroll is useful to users on many devices beyond e-ink tablets. Some people enjoy it as a kind of page-turning function.

Indeed, this feature could be optional, disabled by default if community don't grok it.

### App version

6.509

### Problem you are trying to solve

Sometimes people compose text and include URLs in parentheses. This presents a challenge to apps trying to linkify URLs in this text because `(` and `)` are valid characters in a URL that don't have to be encoded.

Examples:
* `some text here (https://domain.example/path)`
* `(some text here: https://domain.example/path)`
* `(some text here and then a URL on a new line`
  `https://domain.example/path)`
* `(some text here :) https://domain.example/path)`
* `(some text here https://domain.example/path_(still_part_of_the_url))`

`https://domain.example/path)` is a valid URL, but probably not what the sender meant.

For a human reader it's mostly easy to see what is part of the URL and what is part of the surrounding text. However, I hope you can see that a piece of code trying to come to the same conclusion gets very complex pretty soon.

### Suggested solution

Make things easier for apps trying to find URLs in plain text, by surrounding URLs pasted from the clipboard in angle brackets (that can't be part of a URL in their unencoded form).

The examples from above turn into:
* `some text here (<https://domain.example/path>)`
* `(some text here: <https://domain.example/path>)`
* `(some text here and then a URL on a new line`
  `<https://domain.example/path>)`
* `(some text here :) <https://domain.example/path>)`
* `(some text here <https://domain.example/path_(still_part_of_the_url)>)`

title: Messages with 0, 1 or 2 preview lines have the same height
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.501

This issue didn't exist in 6.400. I did not try 6.500 because F-Droid skipped that version.

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

LineageOS 15.1 (Android 8.1)

### Device model

Xiaomi Redmi 4X

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to `General settings` > `Display` > `Message lists`
2. Change the `Preview lines` option to any value out of `0`, `1` or `2`
   Other options are:
   - [X] Show stars
   - [ ] Show correspondent names
   - [X] Correspondent above subject
   - [ ] Show contact pictures
   - [X] Change colour when read
   - [X] Threaded view
3. Check the message height in any folder

### Expected behavior

Lowering the number of preview lines reduces their height to fit more messages on the screen at the same time.

### Actual behavior

Messages on lists are given the same height when the number of preview lines is either `2`, `1` or `0`, leaving vacant layout space if 1 or 0 preview lines are shown. Increasing the height above 2 increases the message height to fit that exact number of preview lines as expected.

### Logs

_No response_

title: opening message from widget broken (for non-first account)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.400

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

7.0

### Device model

HUAWEI P9 lite (HWVNS-L31)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure at least three different mail accounts. On the main settings page, you can order them. In the following, I'll name them in this order: account 1, account 2, ..., account n.
2. Add the message list widget to the home screen.
3. Minimize the app while a message list of account X (X != 1) is open
4. From the widget, open a mail that belongs to account Y, where Y != X and Y != 1

### Expected behavior

The app opens showing the opened mail, after tapping the "back" button the messag list of this mail shows up and the list of account Y is visible in the sidebar.

### Actual behavior

The Inbox view of Account 1 shows up, with the sidebar listing the folders of account X.

### Logs

The log file was empty.

### Problem you are trying to solve

According to the new message design shown in https://blog.thunderbird.net/2022/12/thunderbird-for-android-preview-modern-message-redesign/

I think there are two many colours, buttons and boxes. It does feel that the structure and design is not consistent.

Also discussing with a colleague we think that it would be good to have a different design or structure, so I hope these suggestions could be useful.

### Suggested solution

I would like to propose a radical different approach for the layout, based on bubbles to resemble to an instant messaging app. This is a conversation-oriented structure to make things clearer (maybe a too radical/risky design).

A bubble contains the the subject, pointing to the person who created the message, since it is more visual and easier to identify.
And I think that icons to "Respond" and "Favourite" should be inside the bubble, since it refer to the message, no to the person.

title: Proper formatting when sending RTL/BiDi messages
body:
### Checklist - [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request. - [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. - [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features. ### App version 6.400 ### Problem you are trying to solve I'd like to be able to send messages containing RTL/BiDi text, which will be rendered correctly by the receiver. Currently, when I send such messages, they render correctly only in k9 itself (and that only under specific circumstances), but not, e.g., in Gmail. It's actually a bit complicated, so bear with me... RTL languages (such as Hebrew / Arabic / Persian) are written right-to-left -- this refers both to the fact that the text is aligned to the right rather than to the left, as well as the fact that the second letter of a word is written to the left of the first letter, and the second word is written to the left of the first word, etc. When mixing RTL and LTR text in the same paragraph, things are even more complicated. Proper rendering of such text is done by the BiDi (bidirectional) algorithm. Specifically (and simplifying a bit), part of the algorithm is that the paragraph direction is determined by the language of the first character. In the following examples, "אבג" is the first logical word, with its first letter being "א" (Hebrew letter Aleph). The second word is "abc", and the third word is "דהו". As explained above, since the first character is in Hebrew (an RTL language) , the entire paragraph should be aligned to the right. body:
### Checklist

### App version

6.400

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

13

### Device model

Pixel 4a

### Steps to reproduce

1. Thunderbird 102.5.1 (Mac--haven't tried others), set up account to "Attach my PGP key when sending signed messages". (Encryption subject also set to "off", but doesn't seem to matter.)
2. Send a signed (unencrypted) message. (I sent it to myself.)
3. In Thunderbird the sig checks out OK.
4. In K9, the encryption icon shows "?". Clicking on it says, "Plaintext: end-to-end signature contained an error".
5. In Thunderbird, turn off "Attach my PGP key".
6. Send a signed (unencrypted) message.
7. In Thunderbird the sig checks out OK.
8. In K9, the encryption icon shows "blue check". Clicking on it says, "End-to-End signed plaintext: from verified signer"

I can also reproduce by manually attaching my public key in Thunderbird.

If Thunderbird automatically attaches the key, the MIME header is:

```
Content-Type: application/pgp-keys; name="OpenPGP_0xA165F24CF846C3C8.asc"
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="OpenPGP_0xA165F24CF846C3C8.asc"
Content-Description: OpenPGP public key
Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
```
And if I manually attach it, it's:
```
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8; name="OpenPGP_0xA165F24CF846C3C8.asc"
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="OpenPGP_0xA165F24CF846C3C8.asc"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
```
but the issue repros on K9 either way. 

Also, to repeat, this was my key mailing to myself.

### Expected behavior

I would expect K9 to show the message as signed correctly regardless even if the public key were added as an attachment to the message.

### Actual behavior

K9 only showed the signature as valid if the public key wasn't attached to the message by Thunderbird.
