### Problem you are trying to solve

Android 13 (API level 33) introduces a predictive back gesture for Android devices such as phones, large screens, and foldables.

### Expected behavior

WebView process should exit when the app is closed.

Starting as usual the service is fine.

When I open the app and view some mail, WebView process is started. But it never unloads after the app was closed, just keeps hanging along with the push service and wasting memory no matter what. Also there is no dedicated exit button in the app to properly close it.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13597663/200127027-7a559ab7-8fbc-4265-81aa-550f1a920514.png)

Force stop WebView app from its info page.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13597663/200127459-15586db0-f554-4b2b-aa28-9ee67d893692.png)

Or kill the process using some process viewer (requires root).

Notification on new email(s) appears in the notification bar.

Expected behavior should be: deleted notifications should stay deleted after their first removal.  
Can you help me? I am adding the log file. 
Thank you!

title: Allow to disable push on specific time periods (weekends, nights)
body: ### Checklist - [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request. - [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible. - [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features. ### App version 6.202 ### Problem you are trying to solve When using the app with professional email accounts on a personal phone, it can be unsettling or even stressful to receive push mails in a non-working period (in my case : weekends, nights). Right now the only solution (while keeping sync) would be to either disable regularly push on the app, or disable notifications for K9 at the system level. Doing this every day isn't a viable solution. As a side note, I precise that the "*right to disconnect*" is a rising concept in Europe, with some countries trying to regulate it with law (see this [article](https://www.ft.com/content/a552b919-16ef-453d-a0f1-3725d168fe9c) and the references therein), and the European Union starts to consider a continent-wide [directive](https://www.eurofound.europa.eu/observatories/eurwork/industrial-relations-dictionary/right-to-disconnect). So it might be a feature more people will be interested in in the future. ### Suggested solution I think that it would be a healthy feature to allow the user to select the periods in which the app looks for new emails. Basically defining a "sleep mode" (off work mode? Quiet mode?) . ### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details - The parameters would by default leave push on all the time, and could be change from account settings > receiving mail - I think that the "quiet mode" should be defined at the push level and not the notification level. Two arguments for this: - When the "quiet time" is over, I'd like to be notified of all the mails I missed during off work. - In a scenario where I need to check an older mail while off work (meaning I *have* to open the app) I'd rather not see that new mails are incoming. - There exists an app doing this for Gmail, called *[Quiet for GMail](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sgarcia.quiet_for_gmail&hl=fr&gl=US)*. From a user perspective the app is very easy so setup: - We can define quiet mode account per account (different behaviors for work/personal accounts) - The app seems to use native android forms to select the days/hours we want push to happen. Something similar to what an Alarm app would display? See screenshot below -

resolve dns name with local dns server.

UknownHostException

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make sure *General settings → Display → Threaded view* is enabled (this is the default)
2. Add the message list widget to the home screen
3. Tap a message that is part of a thread, but is not the latest message in that thread (the one that is displayed in the message list inside the app). Note: The message list widget doesn't group messages in a thread.


### Expected behavior

The message is displayed. Pressing the "back" arrow in the message view screen should display the list of messages in that thread (using "back" once more should bring the user to the Unified Inbox).


### Actual behavior

The message list for the Unified Inbox is displayed.

This is because `MessageViewContainerFragment` "returns" to the message list if the message it is supposed to display can't be found in the message list (that is used for the "swipe to next/previous message" feature).

The probably easiest way to fix this issue, is to also show the threaded list in the message list widget.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a folder with two threads that are displayed next to each other in the message list
2. Use two fingers to tap both threads in the message list at roughly the same time
3. Crash

Note: For the crash to happen only the first item clicked needs to be a thread. However, it's easier to reproduce if both list items are threads. Then the order of clicks doesn't matter.

title: Use DNS BIMI records and Clearbit API service in order to display company logos in list view
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.306

### Problem you are trying to solve

Display as many company logos (avatars) as possible in list view - Visual and usability benefit

### Suggested solution

There are two free options which can be used:

**First option --> DNS "BIMI" records** - this type of DNS record is a specification allowing for the display of brand logos next to authenticated e-mails - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_Indicators_for_Message_Identification
Important! - The BIMI record has an "a" attribute (a=https://url.to/certificate.pem) - the Verified Mark Certificate - which is so far optional (https://powerdmarc.com/your-complete-guide-to-bimi/). You should put a checkbox in the K-9 Settings, unchecked by default: "Allow self issued Verified Mark Certificate logos display" which allows the displaying of self issued BIMI logos. If the checkbox is not marked, only authenticated VMC logos will be displayed. If the checkbox is marked, the "a" attribute (a=https://url.to/certificate.pem) is ignored and all BIMI logos will be displayed.

If BIMI record does not return a valid company logo:
**Second option --> Clearbit API Service** - https://clearbit.com/logo - A free logo API service which allows you to quickly lookup company logos using just their domain. You need to credit them in the credits section of the Settings menu. I have seen this implemented in Spark email client and it works like a charm :)

I think that a cascaded lookup of BIMI records and Clearbit API will populate most of the logos in the list view, providing users a more pleasant visual experience, and also a usability benefit.

Hope my suggestion helps :)

body:

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

11

### Device model

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

Some mail providers seem to forbid SMTP connections when the HELO hostname is `127.0.0.1`.
I found the history to this change originating in #2793 (changed in PR #3798).
The question came back in issue #4428.

I have read theses issues and understand that it has been changed so for privacy reasons, and agree that sending the actual real IP or hostname would be detrimental to privacy. However, I believe we can try to find another value that won't be blocked by mail providers. This could potentially be an opt-in option in each SMTP server settings. I'd be ready to make a PR if that is something you would be willing to accept. We could have a select option with values like `127.0.0.1`, `192.168.0.1`, `10.0.0.1` and a final value of `"Send actual IP address (not recommended)"`. This way the user still is in control of what is sent and can still use the app even if the mail provider denies privacy conserving values (most providers won't be willing to change their server configuration on user requests).

### Expected behavior

Being able to send mail to servers denying the 127.0.0.1 HELO hostname

### Actual behavior

Connection to the SMTP server rejected due to a forbidden value of 127.0.0.1 in the HELO message

### App version

### Problem you are trying to solve

When you delete or achieve a message there isn't really anything that indicates you performed such an action (except when you delete, there is the confirm option), or if you have changed your mind, you would need to do a manual move to get it back.

A similar request was made at #624 for an undo option, but I'm not sure what happened.

### Suggested solution

Most modern email clients show a small fading hint that you've deleted or achieved that email. There could also be an undo button just in case you did it by accident or changed your mind. Changing the confirmation window to this fading hint would be more optimal and useful for both delete and archive. Those who prefer not to have to press again, but still want a notice.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

In the settings it could be something like "Enable hint window for deleted message" & "Enable hint window for achieved message".

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.301

### Problem you are trying to solve

When using threaded view, hitting the beginning or end of a thread will "gate" the next/previous actions (formerly arrow buttons, now swipes) to stay within the thread. This is good; it makes it obvious when you have read all the messages in the thread (it was even better with the on-screen arrow buttons because they would be greyed out). If you open a single message in threaded mode, however, there is no gating. You can swipe to the next thread, but now the behavior changes and swiping does not switch between messages within that thread, it instead moves on to the next thread, even if there are multiple messages in that thread. This is very confusing.

### Suggested solution

Add an option to treat all messages as being part of a thread, even single messages. This would apply the gating rule to all messages, preventing swipe / arrow button actions from ever switching threads.

body:

title: Message view redesign
body: We're currently working on a new design for the message view. A (non-final) preview can be seen below. ### Current state ### Preview ![Message header - HiFi - no download](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/218061/190913577-e27dd2f1-6b93-4a7b-a332-3cb3ada070f6.png) Notes on the image: - The chip containing "Thunderbird Ryan" is the name of the account the message belongs to. The chip is colored using the account color. It will only be displayed if there's more than one account. - The text below the chip is the subject of the message. - The circle-shaped image is the contact picture of the sender of the message. - The text at the top of the gray area, to the right of the contact picture is the name of the sender. - To the right we have a reply action and an overflow menu containing more actions. - Below the sender name there's information about the recipients. If the account only has one identity and the message was addressed to it, "to me" will be displayed. If the account has multiple identities the text that is shown will be "to <name of identity>". If the message was addressed to someone else their display name will be shows. For now at most two recipient names will be displayed. If there's more recipients "+x" will be shown. - If a crypto provider is enabled for the account, an encryption indicator is displayed in front of the recipient text. - The "Important, Todo, Work" text is labels added to the message. This won't be relevant until #769 is implemented. - The "show remote images" button is not final and might move and/or change appearance. Tapping any part of the gray area other than the action buttons on the right (reply, overflow menu), will open a bottom sheet containing details about the message. ![Message header - Bottom Drawer HiFi](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/218061/190913663-8bb66aa2-3bbc-4b31-8479-21d770af4d73.png) If there are a lot of recipients the bottom sheet can be dragged up to make it cover the whole screen. In that case we intend to provide a way to search/filter the recipient list. ### Feedback We're still working on the design. But if you're missing a feature or have other feedback, please let us know in a comment. --- ### Initial design considerations A message view redesign should include the following features: - #6180 And it should keep in mind these features that we want to add further down the line: - #6181 Email addresses need to be far enough apart so tapping them reliably is not a problem. - #1119 We probably want to display the email address below the name and then hide the recipient addresses. - #769 Figure out where to display them. - #762 Figure out where to display the folder name(s) (JMAP supports messages living in multiple folders). - #6197 All of the per-message information/actions should live in the message header area, because at some point we'll want to display more than one message in this view. We need some touch area that collapses/expands the whole message. - #1397 We need an overflow menu or some other place to put (less important) per-message actions like this. This is what the message view looks like in other apps… Gmail: Outlook: FairEmail: EDIT 2022-09-18: Updated with latest design.

title: Conversation View
body: In addition to the current threaded view, add support for a conversation view that displays all messages in a conversation. This is what most mobile clients do these days. In the message list, we show one entry per conversation just like we do for threads. Only when conversation view is enabled, tapping this entry will not open an additional message list screen, but a message view screen that displays all messages, one below the other, starting with the oldest message. Messages that are already marked as read should be displayed in a collapsed state so only some basic information is visible (contact picture and display name of the author, date/time, message preview?). The view should scroll to the first unread message. Unread messages are displayed in an expanded state where the message body is visible (we should probably collapse quoted text, though). This is what a conversation looks like in the Gmail app: This is a conversation in FairEmail (latest message first, only one message can be expanded at a time): Open questions: - How do we determine exactly which messages are part of a conversation? By default sent messages are saved to the Sent folder. So we definitely want to include those messages. What about archived messages? Drafts? Some messages might be in totally different folders. Do we care about those? - How do we handle long conversations? Do we break them apart after a limit is reached (I believe Gmail is doing that). If not, we need a way to only load/display parts of a conversation. Show a placeholder like the Gmail app? Display only relevant parts of the "list" and lazy load the rest? Note: This is very similar, but not the same as - #735

title: Can't switch account from POP3 to IMAP
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

6.000

### Where did you get the app from?

Google Play

### Android version

11

### Device model

Pixel3

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open settings for an account configured for POP3
2. Switch to IMAP, configure.
3. Tap Next for test.

### Expected behavior

Connection to IMAP server.

### Actual behavior

It's still using the Pop3Connection to connect to the IMAP port. So all test connections fail, with a display of the list of Capabilities returned from the IMAP server.

### Logs

```
at com.fsck.k9.backend.pop3.Pop3Backend.checkIncomingServerSettings(Pop3Backend.kt:128)
at com.fsck.k9.controller.MessagingController.checkIncomingServerSettings(MessagingController.java:1726)
at com.fsck.k9.activity.setup.AccountSetupCheckSettings$CheckAccountTask.checkIncoming(AccountSetupCheckSettings.java:504)
```

> D Pop3Connection: <<< QUIT BAD Error in IMAP command received by server.
> E AccountSetupCheckSettings$CheckAccountTask: Error while testing settings

The IMAP server is returning a set of RFC-valid Capabilities. It's obvious that it used the wrong protocol to query the server. I think I did completely exit/close the app and then re-enter to get the same results. So, as I recall, it doesn't seem to reset whatever flag is used to determine the POP3/IMAP protocol until after a successful test is done.

My solution was simply to create a new account, as IMAP and remove the POP3 account. This eliminated any possible issues related to local folders versus remote folders. This might be the best solution, although in the process, account settings for reading and writing are lost.

So one approach to resolving this might be to prevent us from changing the protocol type of an existing account between POP3 and IMAP.
Another approach would be to address the protocol selection, and check folder settings to make sure existing POP3 folders and their settings are not lost in the process of loading resources from a new IMAP server.

title: Button's should grey out, not disappear and thus move others
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.000

### Problem you are trying to solve

I am using the unified inbox. One of my mailboxes (let's call it A) has an archives folder, others do not.
When I select a message in mailbox A, then on the top of the screen there is an archive button. When I select a message of any other mailbox, there is no archive button, causing the other buttons to move one position ot the right _so that the (un)read button takes the place of the archive button_.
The effect is that I'm used to the (un)read button being in the position of the archive button, so when I want to mark a mail from mailbox A as (un)read, I inadvertently tend to archive it.
Worse: by default, the buttons have no label, so I had no idea what the button even did, and it's not easy to google if you only have a pictogram to go by.

### Suggested solution

I've been able to disable the archive button by setting the archives folder for mailbox A to `none`.

However, that's beside the point in my opinion. I think a good solution would be to grey out the archive button when it doesn't apply, rather than removing it, so that all buttons keep their place.

title: EHLO keyword contains invalid character
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

d13352a4cd7f5ea540eba738155ff377ee48da62 - 2205202769770bc37feb98414bb8a1ae084b9c98

### Where did you get the app from?

Other

### Android version

11 (LineageOS for microG)

### Device model

Fairphone 3

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set up an email account
2. Go to outgoing server settings
3. Fill in everything and click next

SMTP server: `<REDACTED>`
Security: SSL/TLS
Port: 465
Require sign-in: Yes
Username: `<REDACTED>`
Authentication: Normal password
Password: `<REDACTED>`
Client certificate: No client certificate

Note: This happens on my own self-hosted mailserver, not on a public provider. I obviously don't want to make authentication info for it public, but if it helps to debug please send me an email and I'll get you some login credentials.

### Expected behavior

Succesfully set up SMTP, like it did on K-9 Mail v6.000

### Actual behavior

An error message shows:

# Setup could not finish
Cannot connect to server.
(EHLO keyword contains invalid character)
[ Continue ] [ Edit Details ]

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1885159/167604225-40801927-8e97-44b4-b177-0732d62d22df.png)


### Logs

Using git bisect, I was able to pinpoint it to the following commit:

title: Allow space to complete an email address in recipient fields
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same feature request.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

6.000

### Problem you are trying to solve

User wants to send a message to two recipients and performs the following steps:
1. Open screen to compose a new message (To field has the focus)
2. Enter text `user1@domain.example user2@domain.example`
3. Change focus to another field

K-9 Mail does not recognize two addresses separated by a space. It will try to parse it as one address and display an "Error parsing address!" error.

### Suggested solution

Support "completing" an email address using a space character.

This is a bit tricky because a space might also be part of the display name, e.g. `Firstname Lastname <user@domain.example> second.user@domain.example`.

### Note

Fixing this probably involves writing a custom email address parser and changing the way the TokenAutoComplete library works (or replacing it entirely). It's not something someone new to the project should attempt.

title: Option to pre-download images for particular folders.
body:
### Problem you are trying to solve

I have some folders that I want to be available for offline use but the content contains critical pictures. For example:

- Tickets and Passes
- Comics

It would be nice if some folders could be fully available offline, including any remote content. 

Note that a similar issue exists for attachments. 

### Suggested solution

Provide a per-folder option to pre-download images upon fetching the message. This should probably take 3 possible configurations:

- Fetch images for all messages. 
- Fetch images for messages from contacts. 
- Don't pre-fetch images.

### App version

6.000

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

Moto G7

### Steps to reproduce

I will have to enable debug logs tomorrow. Today I have screenshots.

I started with 4 accounts that had messages:

- Blue: 4 new messages
- Orange: 1 new message
- Yellow: 2 new messages
- Green: 7 new messages
- Dark Green: 3 messages (it was off the screen)

Screenshot 1:
![Screenshot_1_starting](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47018474/165319684-957e5a3b-501a-4d2c-b2b2-638c0cb7946f.png)
 
Next, I expanded the first message in the green account and selected it. It took me to the message, and I deleted it, which took me to the Unified Inbox (this is all as expected and correct behavior).

When pulling down notifications it appears to have changed in a couple of ways. First, there are now summary messages showing the total count - but only on the blue and dark green accounts. Though I had deleted a message from the green account, and its list is not showing the "FC" message, it's showing at the top with an unchanged total and it should say `+5`. The Orange account is gone, and the Yellow account is showing one instead of two messages. It's as if when deleting a Green, it took one notification away from the Orange, Dark Green and Yellow.

Screenshot 2:
![Screenshot_2_removed_wrong_notification_and_summarizes](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47018474/165320983-f609545d-922c-420b-b8eb-98b4ecfe5222.png)

To double-check the Dark Green account, I swiped up the notifications, and changed to the Dark Green account from within the app. Yes, there are 3 messages.

Screenshot 3:
![Screenshot_3_account _has_3_not_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47018474/165321627-9593d944-9f21-4e72-baad-ac2608d4e435.png)

Swiping notification back down shows that the in-app access of the Dark Green account has elminated its notifications, as expected. The Yellow account now has the one message expanded (it actually has 2 unread messages in it). So it still seems there is a cross-account notification reduction of some kind.

Screenshot 4:
![Screenshot_4_removed_wrong_notification](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47018474/165321917-e96a73bc-ff6d-4d3a-8c69-457faffd8363.png)

But the next part is weirder. I swiped the notifications up, and then swiped back down, and it showed no more notifications from the Yellow account. There was no app activity between the swipes except making the app the focus again - this might point to a LineageOS-level notification issue but I have not noticed this with other apps. Not sure about this one.

Screenshot 5:
![Screenshot_5_after_clicking_last_notification](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47018474/165322260-43a88e55-2d3f-4104-9735-45633d50c329.png)

I never accessed the Yellow account in all of these steps. I will get logs tomorrow, thanks.


### Expected behavior

Notifications reflect expected account-level app activity

### Actual behavior

It seems notifications are being modified in a way incongruent to the account-level app activity

### Logs

coming tomorrow

title: Too easy to inadvertantly select message content while scrolling
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have used the search function to see if someone else has already submitted the same bug report.
- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.

### App version

5.905

### Where did you get the app from?

F-Droid

### Android version

12

### Device model

Samsung Galaxy S20 Ultra 5G (SM-G988U)

### Steps to reproduce

Open any email and scroll the message content (it's obviously easier to repro if it's a lengthy message). If you "drag" your finger across the screen to scroll (i.e. instead of "flicking" it)  and move too slowly, the contextual pop-up window appears much too "easily". It seems to be more likely to happen in emails with images and/or hyperlinks than text alone.

### Expected behavior

The context pop up that appears on "long tap" should have more of a delay and/or should only appear if the finger is tapped (i.e. no scrolling).

### Actual behavior

The pop-up menu seems to appear much more "easily" than with other scroll-intensive apps (e.g. Twitter, text editors, browsers). This makes scrolling and reading longer messages (especially those with lots of images and links) rather annoying, because the menu appears and blocks the content.

body:

- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

5.807

### Problem you are trying to solve

Reduce the amount of personal information being disclosed should an android device be compromised with malware

### Suggested solution

I am aware that this is not a perfect privacy solution and there are ways around it but it would be useful to have K-9 block the ability to take screenshots.

While the risks / concerns of someone remotely taking a screenshot of K-9 on most peoples devices phone are low there are still users who are high risk, it is a possibility that some malware is setup to take screenshots of open apps.  Given the nature of email this could include sensitive information

Additionally with screenshots blocked, switching apps would result in you seeing k-9 is your list of open apps but not seeing the screen it's contents 

My suggestion would be to add a toggle option to `settings -> general settings -> privacy` that would allow people to toggle on or off the blocking of screenshots.

Some apps that do that have this option if examples/comparison is needed

  * Signal (allows toggling screenshot capture on or off)
  * Protonmail (always blocked)
  * Aegis (allows toggling screenshot capture on or off)


### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

discussion of possible ways to do this [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28606689/how-to-prevent-screen-capture-in-android)

### Device model

Fairphone model 2

### Steps to reproduce

(I don't really have steps to reproduce (other than "try to update the mail list via POP3") as this isn't a problem that occurred always when doing X but an issue that occurred over time)

Yesterday about that time my phone app was still working just fine. I have it set to fetch mails on a 3-hour schedule and besides some minor occurrences where the app needed about 15 seconds to finish the update of two accounts (which already is long from my point of view) I never had any problems with k9. But yesterday at about 6 pm I unlocked my phone to see the usual notification about mail updates being performed but after what I would estimate as two or three minutes the notification still didn't go away and was still on the first account (with no new mails to fetch as I checked aside from k9). So, not having any other method to stop this action, I force stopped k9 (several times in fact in my debugging process), at some point disabled the scheduled mail update (as k9 would only get stuck in this process again as soon as I opened the app again), cleared the cache several times, restarted the phone (one time even in safe mode where the app obviously can't work).

At some point I considered that this might be a server connection problem, so I opened up the account settings to (re-)configure the incoming and outgoing servers. **Is it correct that if I enter these sub-settings and click "Next", the server connection is (re-)validated and depending on the outcome of this action I can verify the state of the connection?** In the following I assume that's how that works, as (re-)configuring the incoming server had the same "problem" than updating the mail list with the benefit that this process is user-cancel-able whereas mail polling isn't.

What I know so far (please ask if you have any other ideas of how to pinpoint the exact issue better):
- I always use POP3 on all devices. That means that I can state for a fact that the POP3 connection in theory can work as Thunderbird can still retrieve my mails from the same accounts.

title: Add option to never remember email account password.
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I will describe the problem with as much detail as possible.
- [X] This issue only contains a request for one single feature, **not** multiple (related) features.

### App version

5.806

### Problem you are trying to solve

With the rise in demand for more security in mobile applications (as evidenced by requests like https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/753, https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/1352, https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/3318, https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/3377, https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/3920, https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/4796, https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/5260, https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/5740) a lot of users are trying to seek solutions for common security risks such as unauthorized device access and network sniffing for credentials.  I understand K9 isn't an advanced security application, nor should it be, but I think this can give some users a much wanted peace of mind.

### Suggested solution

I'd like to have an option for K9 to NOT remember my email account password and just prompt the user to enter it if and when needed.

This way the user can rely on a third party application for encrypting their credentials or they can remember their password manually.  While this won't prevent unauthorized access to existing data on the device, it will prevent new data from being sent to the device and give protection against unauthorized users sending data using the saved account.  

It can also help the user to be more aware of the network they're connected to in the event they're connected to a rouge network or otherwise at risk for a man in the middle type of attack.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

If implemented, it'd probably be good to have an option in the per account settings, probably under general settings.  It could just be a simple checkbox for "Remember password" that's checked by default.

Another checkbox could be added when adding a new account to "remember" the password that would have to be unchecked. 

There could also be a global setting in the main General Settings under Privacy that unchecks it for all existing accounts (perhaps with a warning that any existing stored passwords will be removed) and keeps the creation checkbox unchecked by default.  

The effects could cause the app to prompt the user for the password for a given account when the app is opened, when a manual or automatic update is triggered, or when sending an email or other server request.

When entered, the password would be used for that connection attempt and "forgotten" when finished.  It would be similar to how Thunderbird operates if you decline to have it remember account passwords.

title: Push updates via distributors
body:
Currently there is the push feature that requires a running background process.
That's great, but wastes a lot of battery and isn't perfect for everyone. I propose the creation and an external push functionality that relies on an external distributor to receive updates. The architecture would be a self hosted server that checks for the updates in the specific folders. The app gives the servers these credentials. The server doesn't keep track of all emails, just enough information to determine when a new one arrives. When it does, it sends out a notification via a distributor. There are two main ones I think should be supported:
Google's FCM
UnifiedPush (https://unifiedpush.org/users/intro/)

The user can configure which to use. The app would detect each distributor on the phone and use whatever is available. A data message should be sent containing no identifying information such as message content or email. The server and client should configure some uuid for the email account in question and use that to alert the app that an update is available. A uuid for folders can be used too. A background service is than ran to poll and fetch the updates for that particular account. 
Biggest advantage for this setup is battery efficiency and instantaneous notifications of new emails.  It would require some setup from the user, but would be in line with the FOSS individuals who already self host stuff. Exploring how to privatize the passwords/connection on the server side would be nice too so a user can use a publicly shared endpoint while not risking their security. Not really possible on initial thoughts, but I could be incorrect.

title: Prompt users to configure special folders during account setup
body:
If the IMAP server doesn't support the [Special-Use extension](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6154) to let clients know which folders to use as special folders (Archive, Drafts, Sent, Spam, Trash), prompt the user to configure special folders when setting up an account.
The UI should be initialized with sensible defaults. If there's a folder called "Drafts" chances are good users will want to use it as their Drafts folder. Ideally, the app correctly guesses which folders to use for what role and the user only has to click an "OK" button.

Currently we default to not using a special folder when the server doesn't support the extension or no folder is tagged with a particular role. But most users don't expect e.g. sent messages not being uploaded automatically, especially if there's a folder called "Sent".

title: Support custom notification sound on Android 7 and older
body:
On Android versions prior to Android 8 we display our own notification sound picker ("New mail ringtone"). The component uses [`RingtoneManager`](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/media/RingtoneManager) to retrieve the list of notification sounds. But on Android versions prior to Android 10 `RingtoneManager` will only return custom notification sounds if the app holds the [`READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/Manifest.permission.html#READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE:kotlin.String) permission. Since we no longer request that permission custom notification sounds can't be selected.

I don't want the app to request the `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission just to support custom notification sounds. Given that, I believe we have two options:
1. Use the system picker for notification sounds: [`ACTION_RINGTONE_PICKER`](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/media/RingtoneManager#ACTION_RINGTONE_PICKER:kotlin.String). ~Investigate whether this will allow picking custom notification sounds without the calling app having the `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission.~ (seems to work on an API 24 emulator)
2. Use the storage access framework to pick a notification sound, then copy it to app-private storage and expose it via a content provider to the system, e.g. using [PublicFileProvider](https://github.com/cketti/PublicFileProvider).

title: Automatically retrieve keys
body:
In the actual version (5.904), if I want to write an encrypted message to a person and I don't have the public key of that person, I have to switch to the OpenKeyChain app. Then I can search for the key there and I have to go back to K9Mail to continue to write/send the mail.

It would increase the usability of K9Mail, if the app would search for missing keys automatically. Then users would only need to enter an email what they already did before and the app would begin to look for a key. Examples for products that are acting this way are Mailvelope which is a browser extension and KMail which is an email client for GNU/Linux.

title: Wrong "to" list, when replying to Google Groups
body:
Google Group is set so that replies should go to the group, not the sender. However, “reply” in K9 puts both the group and the sender in the “to” list. K9 should only send to the group, which is the behaviour of other email clients, such as Outlook.

For illustration, in an email with the below headers, when "reply" is clicked, K9 puts both MEMBERNAME@MEMBER.DOMAIN and GROUPNAME@googlegroups.com in the "to" list. It should only include GROUPNAME@googlegroups.com


Delivered-To: MYNAME@MY.DOMAIN
Envelope-To: MYNAME@MY.DOMAIN
Sender: GROUPNAME@googlegroups.com
From: GROUP MEMBER NAME <MEMBERNAME@MEMBER.DOMAIN>
To: <GROUPNAME@googlegroups.com>
Reply-To: GROUPNAME@googlegroups.com
Precedence: list
Mailing-list: list GROUPNAME@googlegroups.com;

title: Leave Messages on Server with Google POP3
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Use case: Desktop email client is the historical email repository, so desktop email client should be the only application that archives or deletes email on the server.  Desktop should contain every email received.  K-9mail is used when away from the desktop for new email while away from the desktop (not for having a complete set of email on the phone).  The problem I'm encountering is email is accessed by k9mail, the message is gone, and no longer available to the desktop client, and the desktop client no longer is a complete record of all emails.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
K9mail would pull from POP3 server but leave the mail on the server.  Gmail configuration allows POP3 to have deletion, archival, etc "when messages are accessed".  I would like K9mail to access the messages, but not take any action on the server. 

This had been working earlier, for many years.  When I was away from home, I'd get new mail on my phone, and when I got back to the desktop machine and pulled email, all the email would go to the desktop client, and I had Gmail configured to trash when pulled by the desktop email client.  Thus, no need for a lot of space provided by Google.  But something happened and now the mail gets removed by the first email client to get to the email message.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I looked at IMAP, but that seems to require that Google hold on to all of my email.  I don't want or need Google to hold on to all of my email.  I want my local desktop machine to hold all my email, which gives me the ability to index and search most quickly.

title: Support for forwarding services headers
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I use SimpleLogin, which helps me more easily create one email alias per service. Because of this, my emails all look like they come from email addresses like reply+iwehobhuhuoeahfewouhb@simplelogin.co instead of the forwarded address.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
SimpleLogin adds several headers to each email, allowing you to see the original sender:

https://github.com/simple-login/app/blob/ee0ed7d9ec822bcd5355c0d61930aa0f1ddccdb0/app/email/headers.py#L27-L30

For example:
```
X-SimpleLogin-Envelope-From: noreply@github.com
X-SimpleLogin-Envelope-To: my_alias@example.com
```

It would be great if K-9 Mail could use these headers to display the from and to address that the emails are forwarded from.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Another option would be perhaps to talk to the SimpleLogin app, but this seems more complex and also harder to extend to other forwarding services like AnonAddy.

**Additional context**
This should probably be something the user should enable manually (something like Email -> Forwarding Service -> SimpleLogin), to prevent malicious emails using such headers to spoof.

title: "K-9 Accounts" widget stops working after device reboot
body:
**Describe the bug**
A "K-9 Accounts" widget (launcher shortcut, really) configured to open a particular account, will open the default account or Unified Inbox after a device reboot.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Drag the "K-9 Accounts" widget tile to the home screen
2. In the configuration screen select an account that is not the default account
3. Tap the newly created widget to confirm it is opening the configured account
4. Reboot the device
5. Tap the widget
6. It behaves like tapping the app icon: the default account or Unified Inbox is opened (depending on your configuration)

**Expected behavior**
The configured account should be opened after a device reboot.

**Environment:**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.904
 - Android version: 11
 - Device: Pixel 2, Pixel launcher


I suspect it's because we serialize a `LocalSearch` instance in the launch Intent and deserialization fails after a reboot.

title: Unread email counter display wrong information in notifications
body:

Even if I enable notification for new emails only for first class folders (in which I have only inbox folder), when I receive a new email, the counter on Icon app and status bar display the number of all unread messages including unread messages of each archives and trash folders.

A third option would be to not display the counter of unread message in the status bar and on the the icon app, but just a message in status bar and an overlay on icon app saying that there is new email.

Hoping it could be solved.

Best regards

Philippe

I did a quick search through the code to see if I could find which part handles the (1), (2) etc suffix, but it seems my 'grep' skills were not quite good enough to find it.

title: Hard to reply in new UI
body:
**Describe the bug**
The new UI is great looking, but sometimes less practical than the other one as it was [already shown](https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/5447). I also have today troubles with a new problem: I can't answer an email efficiently. For now, I've two methods to answer an email:

Method 1:
- scroll to the top of the email (usually after reading the email, you are at the bottom)
- click on the arrows: it will open a menu
- click on "Answer" or "Answer All"

Method 2:
- click on the 3 dots at the top part of the screen ([hard to reach](https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/5447)...), it will open a first menu
- click on "Send": it will open another menu
- click on "Answer" or "Answer all"

3 steps to answer an email is too much... I'd much prefer as before a few buttons at the bottom of the screen, where I can answer/answer/forward all in one click.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Try to answer an email in less than 3 steps

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.806

title: Spam messages Missing, No body, then OK
body:
**Describe the bug**

My wife reports missing messages in the Spam folder after the upgrade to 5.806.  I forced stopped k9, cleared cache then went into Spam folder and forced a reload (pull down) but it made no difference.  Then I exported the settings, forced stop k9, cleared data, imported settings and went into both fetching and sending to get my self-cert accepted and (a) message now synched down but the body was missing (verified by view headers and comparing message-id).  Finally, I went to the server, rm .Spam/dovecot* files (this resets UID, I believe), no difference till after I force quit k9.  Then upon startup (b) The message now downloaded correctly.  No errors on the server side.

I grabbed a logcat from (a) but I don't see any references to the message or even Spam folder.  Also grabbed a log from (b) but this was for the correct behavior so useless.

**To Reproduce**
I have not been able to reproduce the problem yet.  My wife will compare messages in the Spam folder using k9 wand mutt and identify missing messages.  Suspect this bug will reoccur, so looking for advise on how to trigger relevant log events when this occurs again.

**Expected behavior**
k9 should show all messages available in Spam folder.  Btw, I verified that Fetching mail have no limits (all messages, any time (no limit), any size (no limit)).

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.806
 - Android version: 11
 - Device: Samsun Galaxy S10
 - Account type: IMAP
 
**Additional context**
Folder poll frequency: Never, i.e. Push-only.

**Logs**
The logs that I have collected do not demonstrate the error, so looking for advise on how to obtain a logs for this particular problem.

title: Bar with new/next/previous mails... hard to reach on new theme
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I recently upgraded K-9 Mail: the new theme is great looking, but not always practical. Notably, the bar containing the buttons to create new emails, or go to the previous/next email has been moved to the top part of the screen. On mobile phones this is quite hard to use with a single hand since I need to stretch my finger to reach the top part of my screen every time I want to write an email or move in a conversation.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like an option to move this bar to the bottom part of the screen, like before.

title: Two small improvements:
body:
My settings are set to "Never download pictures" and it works as intended. Sometimes I want to load the pictures and use the "Load pictures" button.

**In the case of emails in which the images have already been loaded, the "Load images" button should not be displayed in the first place.**

-------

K-9 can can generate an * .eml file from received mails if you select "forward as attachment". From time to time I would like to save a mail locally as * .eml because I am interested in the headers. So far, this has only been possible via the detour "send to yourself" and then save the attachment.

**An extension would be nice if one could not only delete the generated attachment before sending it, but also save it. It would be even nicer to be able to save a generated * .eml file via share.**

body:
Hi,

I've been using K9-mail for 9years now and always been satisfied.
Recently, I noticed that some emails (from my Google account illustrated here, but also from my professional account) are not displayed, even if they appear when using the webmail.

This is most probably linked to #1422, but I use a version >5.7xx in which this bug should have been fixed.

Description of the bug:
- K9mail version: 5.802
- See corresponding screenshots below: Some emails are visible using the webmail (left, bottom). For example, the Easyjet email, but this is also the case for "Google Team" message and the "Esp@ace Client" message.
- But they remains not visible in K9-mail (left, top)
- The local search (from K9 mail) does not find he Easyjet mail. The server search from K9 does find it. Once it has been found by the server search, the email does appear in the K9 mailbox (right).

I indicate:
- mails are not group into conversations
- I haven't found (yet) a pattern in the email that are not displayed (no matters when the email was sent, whether I'm or not the only recipient, ...).
- The fact that it is shown at the right place when the server search has been done suggests that K9-mail ingnore it to start with.
- I haven't seen anything obvious in the header of the email that are ignored and not sync-ed. Yet, I've posted the header of the Easyjet email below.

Hi,

I've been using K9-mail for 9years now and always been satisfied.
Recently, I noticed that some emails (from my Google account illustrated here, but also from my professional account) are not displayed, even if they appear when using the webmail.

This is most probably linked to #1422, but I use a version >5.7xx in which this bug should have been fixed.

Description of the bug:
- K9mail version: 5.802
- See corresponding screenshots below: Some emails are visible using the webmail (left, bottom). For example, the Easyjet email, but this is also the case for "Google Team" message and the "Esp@ace Client" message.
- But they remains not visible in K9-mail (left, top)
- The local search (from K9 mail) does not find he Easyjet mail. The server search from K9 does find it. Once it has been found by the server search, the email does appear in the K9 mailbox (right).

I indicate:
- mails are not group into conversations
- I haven't found (yet) a pattern in the email that are not displayed (no matters when the email was sent, whether I'm or not the only recipient, ...).
- The fact that it is shown at the right place when the server search has been done suggests that K9-mail ingnore it to start with.
- I haven't seen anything obvious in the header of the email that are ignored and not sync-ed. Yet, I've posted the header of the Easyjet email below.
- I tried to recreate my mailbox from scratch (recreate a second time my gmail account): the emails that were ignored are still not fetched.

title: K9 uses default account when clicking mailto link in secondary account.
body:
**Describe the bug**
When multiple accounts are setup and one is selected as the default sending account, `mailto` links opened from emails in the other accounts will still use the default account as sender.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Setup multiple accounts.
2. Set one of the accounts as the default account for sending emails in the account settings.
3. Open an email in one of the "non-default" accounts.
4. Click on a `mailto` link (e.g., unsubscribe in a newsletter or such).
5. The new email will have the default acocunt selected as sender instead of the current account.

**Expected behavior**
I cannot think of any situation in which I would want to open an email-link from a mail in account `B` but want send a mail from account `A` instead. While the sender can of course be changed during drafting the new email, I think the more natural behaviour would be to answer the mailto link from the account that received the message containing said link.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.8.0.6
 - Android version: 10
 - Device: Google Pixel A3

title: Weird format on OpenPGP encrypt message subjects.
body:
**Describe the bug**
I have multiple email accounts in the K-9 and only one account has this problem. The problem is that after enable the "Encrypt message subjects", the mails sent with 'sign and encrypt' has a weird format that neither Thunderbird nor Interlink w/ Enigmail can decrypt the encrypted subject. Only pEp can recognize this weird format.

I manually decrypt the weird format between the -----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE----- and -----END PGP MESSAGE----- as below:
```
Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
Content-Type: text/plain;
 charset=utf-8; protected-headers="v1"
Subject: =?UTF-8?B?bW9uZXkg8J+kkQ==?=

happy birthday
```
So, the problem is this format doesn't provide a independent MIME block for the protected-headers="v1".

I reviewed my other accounts, they all have the mail format with independent MIME block for the protected-headers="v1". So the worked format is that the protected-headers="v1" opens a new nest of MIME block (multipart/mixed) and include the actual mail body in its sub-block.

My conclusion (a guess) is that when you compose a new mail with simple text with the configurations "automatic message format" for the account, then you will get this weird format when K-9 decides to compose the message as plain text.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Configure account to enable "Encrypt message subjects"
2. Configure account to "Automatic" "Message format"
3. Compose a new mail with simple text.
4. Enable the encrypt (i.e. sign + encrypt)
5. Send the mail.
6. Receive the mail and read it by Thunderbird and Enigmail powered mail clients.
7. You can't see actual mail subject just "Encrypted Message"

**Expected behavior**
Users of Thunderbird and Enigmail powered mail clients should be able to get the actual mail subject.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

 - Android version: 10
 - Device: NOKIA 5.1 Plus
 - Account type: IMAP

Add any other context about the problem here.

title: Replying to a text/plain-only message generates unfavorable HTML
body:
**Describe the bug** When replying to a message containing only a `text/plain` part and K-9 Mail is configured to send HTML messages, the app will generate HTML that puts the quoted text inside a `
` tag. This leads to long lines not being wrapped in other clients. It works in K-9 Mail because we add the class `k9mail` to the tag and add a CSS rule for that class when displaying messages. However, this CSS style is not included in the message.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Receive a `text/plain` message, e.g.
   ```text
   Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2021 17:14:52 +0200
   From: 
   To: 
   Subject: Long line, text/plain
   Message-ID: 
   MIME-Version: 1.0
   Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
   Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
   
   A line extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely extremel=
   y extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely long long long long lon=
   g long long long long long long long long long long long long long long=2E
   ```
2. Make sure *Settings > [Account] > Sending mail > Message format* is set to *HTML*.
3. Reply to the message from step 1
4. The resulting message looks similar to this:
   ```text
   Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2021 17:16:03 +0200
   From: Bob 
   To: 
   Subject: Re: Long line, text/plain
   User-Agent: K-9 Mail for Android
   In-Reply-To: 
   References: 
   Message-ID: 
   MIME-Version: 1.0
   Content-Type: multipart/alternative;
    boundary=----G7YE98IGHS1BNE3I2L90D9ODGHKSOP
   Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
   
   ------G7YE98IGHS1BNE3I2L90D9ODGHKSOP
   Content-Type: text/plain;
    charset=utf-8
   Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable

   What is K-9 Mail doing with this when replying?

   On August 22, 2021 5:14:52 PM GMT+02:00,  wrote:
   >A line extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely extrem=
   ely extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely long long long long l=
   ong long long long long long long long long long long long long long long=
   =2E
   
   ------G7YE98IGHS1BNE3I2L90D9ODGHKSOP
   Content-Type: text/html;
    charset=utf-8
   Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable

   What is K-9 Mail doing with this when replying?
On August 22, 2021 5:14:52 PM GMT+02:00, =
   <alice@domain=2Eexample> wrote:

   
A line extremely extremely extremely ex=
   tremely extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely extremely extreme=
   ly extremely long long long long long long long long long long long long lo=
   ng long long long long long long=2E

   ------G7YE98IGHS1BNE3I2L90D9ODGHKSOP--
   ```

**Screenshot**

In Thunderbird the message is displayed like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/218061/130361530-f177ef95-852a-44ce-9d67-b1925121aa04.png)


**Expected behavior**
Use HTML that leads to the message being displayed in a sensible way by other clients. We probably shouldn't put the quoted text inside a `
` tag.

I'm guessing the main problem is that we don't distinguish between HTML for local display and HTML that is included in outgoing messages. 

**Environment:**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.900-SNAPSHOT (97b53fb685a0c6522c28bdaa5fbd5a141c036a06)

title: Mute thread functionality like in thunderbird
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Being subscribed to some medium level maling-lists it is sometimes frustrating when you *know* that a) a thread does not interest you in the slightest, b) there will be many more replies to it, that you can't do anything about this. In thunderbird you can mute that one thread (`k` for kill, [see here](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/ignore-threads)) and still get notifications and unread emails for other threads from that list.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Having an option in K-9 which can mute a thread. This would (to be discussed) have the following result:
* All emails currently in this thread are marked as read
* The thread is never shown as unread in the message list (i.e. automatically mark new incoming emails as read?)
* No notifications for new emails in said thread are generated
* The thread gets a special icon indicating it as ignored (thunderbid uses this: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/105185/130355104-1101a05e-112c-4372-9d46-1013f0afa927.png))
* It gets an option to unignore the thread, which would enable it for notifications and unread statuses again

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Not really any idea.

**Additional context**
It would be super nice if this ignored thread status would sync via imap to other clients, especially that it works interoperable with TB. I don't know if Thunderbird currently even syncs this to the server though. But maybe we can request that as a feature there as well :-).

**Some related work:**

* https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/pull/5114 (abandoned but also slightly different scope)
* https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/4330 (for hiding messages from ignored threads altogether, related but distinct functionality)

title: Re-opening via App-Icon does not remember last state.
body:
**Describe the bug**
When the app is running open in the background, say with an email opened and one uses the app drawer/home screen icon, the app will open up and return to the start view (inbox of the default account or whatever is set) instead  of  showing the last opened view.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open app and navigate to random view (e.g. open any Email).
2. Go to the android home screen (i.e. minimize K9).
3. Re-open K9 from the "active apps" screen.
4. The app will open with the last state (i.e. the email we opened in 1.).
5. Go to home screen again.
6. Open K9 via home screen or app drawer icon.
7. The app opens with the default start view instead of the previously opened view.

**Expected behavior**
If the app window is already running in the background, I would expect all entry points to show the same app view, which is the currently active view.
The current behaviour in step 6-7 rather resembles a restart of the app then a re-open.
Also, it is quite easy to navigate back to the start page from any point in the app, but can be quite difficult to return to the previously opened mail/view from the start page.

**Environment**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.8.03
 - Android version: 11
 - Device: Google Pixel 3a (likely all)
 - Account type: all

title: App attempts to connect to accounts before password has been entered
body:
**Describe the bug**
After importing account details and choosing not to enter passwords immediately, I believe the app will attempt to login with no password, triggering protective measures (e.g. fail2ban) at the server 

***Background***
My email provider (WebArchitects Co-op https://www.webarch.info/) started to refuse connections from my home Broadband. When I contacted them, they said this was because of repeated attempts to login using invalid credentials. Resetting my router would temporarily "fix" the problem, because it would be assigned a new (unbanned) IP address by my ISP. Connecting using the phone's mobile internet would also (temporarily) fix the problem.

I have been testing phone custom ROMs, and the devices I am testing all use K-9. To save time, I have exported all the account settings. The problem stated to occur after I had imported the settings on a new  installation, but chosen not to input account passwords immediately. I don't have logs, but what I assume is happening is that K-9 is repeatedly attempting to login to the email server without a valid password, ad eventually triggering fail2ban (or whatever else the provider uses to protect the server).

**To Reproduce**
1. Install K-9 and run it for the first time
2. Choose 'Import settings' and select a file containing one or more valid account details. In my case these are all IMAP accounts, configured for Push
3. When prompted to enter passwords, choose 'Later'
4. Leave the phone switched on
5. Some time (several hours?) later, try to connect to the email server - in my case using Thunderbird on a laptop, *or* using the server's webmail interface in a browser - from the same intenet connection as that used by the phone. Connections are refused by the email server

**Expected behavior**
It would be good if K-9 did not attempt to connect to an email server if no password has been set for an account

**Screenshots**
Sorry - none available

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.802. But the problem occurred previously on June 14 2021, though I didn't work out why, bit I was also testing phone custom ROMs around that time. I would have been using whatever 5.7nn beta was current at that time, maybe 
 5.734?
 - Android version: Note version dependent. Occurs on both Android 10/Q and 11/R

 - Account type: [e.g. IMAP, POP3, WebDAV/Exchange]

**Logs**
Again, no logs available - sorry

title: Read mails momentarily revert to unread
body:
**Describe the bug**
When reading mails in an IMAP account with PUSH active, messages that have been read will snap back to the unread state for a few seconds before the action fully syncs to the server, after which the message will correctly return to the read state. 4. Observe older messages popping in to the sequence

**Expected behavior**
K-9 should locally remember the read status of messages and sync them back to the server in the background.

 - Android version: 11 (LineageOS 18.1)

We use this issue tracker to keep track of the work that needs to be done. If you wish to discuss the account overview screen please use the [forum](https://forum.k9mail.app/).

title: Improve experience when clicking the summary notification
body:
When clicking the summary notification on old Android versions or clicking on grouped notifications on new Android versions, we open a message list screen showing the new messages. 

We should do the following, in order:
- [x] When the Unified Inbox is enabled and all messages belong to a folder that is included in the Unified Inbox, open the Unified Inbox.
- [x] When all messages belong to the same folder, open that folder.
- [x] Otherwise, open a message list view that only includes new messages.

The last one is a bit tricky, because we want to remove the notifications as soon as that view is opened. However, if we do that, we lose the information about which messages are "new". So we need an additional flag in the `messages` table to mark a message as "new" and use that for displaying the list of new messages, rather than the `notifications` table.

title: Don't create notifications when first syncing a folder
body: When a folder has never been synchronized (or all local state has been discarded) all unread messages that are downloaded during initial sync are currently considered new and a notification is created for each of them. title: v5.802 doesn't retract android notification on delete of unread message
body:
**Describe the bug**
Separate IMAP client deletes unread message, v5.802 does not retract New Message notification previously posted when IMAP PUSH saw new msg arrive

**To Reproduce**
1.  send message to an account watched via IMAP PUSH by K-9 v5.802
2. K-9 posts a notification immediately (cool)
3. via another IMAP client (desktop, even K-9 v5.600 on another android), delete the message before marking it read
4. Android notification previously posted by K-9 v5.802 is not retracted and stays visible  (note that v5.600 properly retracts in such a case)

**Expected behavior**
A message never marked read but deleted by another client should retract K-9's previously posted new-message notification.

**Environment:**
 - K-9 Mail version: v5.802
 - Android version: 8.0 // old, I know
 - Device: LG V20 // old, I know
 - Account type: IMAP (gmail)

**Additional context**
Note as mentioned above, v5.600 (K-9) does retract notifications in such cases

A work-around that the end-user may practice is as follows:

Whichever separate non-K9(v5.802) IMAP client is being used (desktop client of some form on another machine, K-9 v5.600 itself on another Android device), if you FIRST mark the newest message read, THEN delete that newest message, K-9 v5.802 DOES properly retract the previously posted new-msg android-notification.

So I'm wondering if K-9 v5.802 could be changed to treat a message deletion (for a message just received and for which the android system notification was posted, and which is still an unread message) as experiencing both an "is read" and "is deleted" state change?

I realize, having briefly scanned the issues list here that there are many challenges surrounding android notifications, and that this may not be an easy thing to track down and solve.  I hope I've provided enough info.

In summary:

message arrives, remains new/unread, is deleted from another IMAP client, K-9 v5.802 leaves the android notif up (while 5.600 removes the notif under the same conditions).

conversely:

message arrives, remains new/unrerad, is first marked read from another IMAP client, then deleted from another IMAP client, K-9 v5.802 tears down the android notif previously posted for the new message.

title: Add support for custom notification light color on Android 8+
body:
Android 8 has introduced [notification channels](https://developer.android.com/training/notify-user/channels) where an app can only provide an initial configuration. After creation a notification channel can only be configured by the user via Android's notification settings. Unfortunately their settings screen doesn't allow setting a color for the notification light.

It seems like our only option is to use our own UI to allow users to select a color for the notification light. Then we'll have to delete the existing notification channel and create a new one (copying the configuration of the old notification channel).
We will also have to use a different ID for the new notification channel. So we have to dynamically create that ID and keep track of it instead of being able to use a static identifier.

See also #5543

title: Move to folder search handling of spaces
body:
**Summary:** Searching for the folder "foo " (including trailing space) matches all folders. 

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When moving a message to a folder, and then clicking the search button (something I do many times per day to navigate my 10,000 folders), I sometimes use SwiftKey's autocompletion to finish the name of the folder/keyword. When I do so, SwiftKey adds a space at the end of the word. Then K-9 matches all folders until I backspace to remove the space.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
At the least, I think the search field should be trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace. This is likely a one-line change. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The current behavior seems to be to OR together substring matches for each word. I can't think of a use for this. Perhaps more natural would be to take an AND? Then this issue would disappear (though for efficiency, it'd still be a good idea to trim).

title: "Waiting for new emails" notification should use low priority
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

First of all, congrats on the 5.800 release! It's clear it was a long road to get here, but it looks and works great.

A family member is stuck on an older version of Android (7.1) and is finding the new push "waiting for new emails" notification annoying. It appears with normal priority (so it's interleaved with all of their other notifications) and it doesn't appear possible to disable it without disabling _all_ notifications for K-9 (which would sort of defeat the purpose of having push enabled in the first place).

We took a look at the documentation [for silencing or disabling the notification](https://forum.k9mail.app/t/how-to-configure-push/1102/1#notification-3), but these instructions don't appear to apply to Android 7.1 or below. Specifically, there doesn't appear to be a mechanism for granularly disabling or silencing specific kinds of notifications from an app -- it's all or nothing.

The notification on Android 7.1 looks like the one covered in the FAQ post:

![ss1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/567041/128258318-d837de77-3de0-4512-8afa-42c7799db649.png)

However, long-pressing the notification reveals this menu instead of one that allows you to toggle individual notification types:

![ss2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/567041/128258559-73eed04e-d2aa-4df4-b8ce-ab36ffbdd3f9.png)

The "More Settings" option doesn't offer more granular configurability either:

![ss3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/567041/128258649-c56f75c3-8dc2-4105-8bca-ff51a6321314.png)


**Describe the solution you'd like**

Other apps seem to solve this problem by using low-priority notifications. For example, when [Signal](https://www.signal.org/) is running in an environment without Play Services, it'll spawn a persistent notification similar to K-9's. However, the notification doesn't have an icon that appears in the status bar -- you have to pull down the notification shade to see it at all -- and it appears at the very bottom of the notification list, in a slightly dimmed colour:

![ss4](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/567041/128259232-b5453345-f1cb-446c-9d81-668b58f33762.png)

Signal _message_ notifications, of course, appear with normal priority.

Absent any way to hide specific kinds of notifications for a given app on older versions of Android, having K-9 do this seems like it would be the best and least obtrusive solution.

In case it helps, I took a quick look in Signal's code -- [this appears to be the method and parameter in question](https://github.com/signalapp/Signal-Android/blob/1a56924a56a191a1271ba70b2e12a3af3ad289bc/app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/messages/IncomingMessageObserver.java#L275), using `androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat.Builder`. The [docs for the method](https://developer.android.com/reference/androidx/core/app/NotificationCompat.Builder#setPriority(int)) explain:

> On platforms `Build.VERSION_CODES.O` and above this value is ignored in favor of the importance value set on the notification's channel. **On older platforms, this value is still used, so it is still required for apps supporting those platforms.**

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

The family member could disable push and enable polling instead. (This is slightly annoying, since push/IDLE seemed to work fine on previous versions of K-9 without the notification, with battery optimizations disabled. My understanding is that the notification is necessary specifically for new versions of Android, which is fair enough.)

Or they could roll back to an older version of K-9. This would definitely be a shame -- and probably not ideal long-term for security and maintenance -- but would fix the notification annoyance.

title: Show accout list in app home screen. (or option to set it as default behaviour)
body:
Everytime an app is updated and I read "UI changed" in the "what's new" it makes me cringe. This means too often loss of functionality, usage hassle/difficulties (unrelated to learning curve), loss of productivity and too little actual gains. 
Sadly K9 updating to 5.8 followed this same pattern.

I manage multiple email accounts. 
More often I need to work with a different account when I open K9 then the account I used last time. Up to now K9 was the perfect and high performance choice and with PGP integration. 
With version 5.8 however the changed UI follows concepts used by many other email apps, concepts which made those apps very hard to use and thus poor choices for such multiple account management.

**Desired behaviour**
- when I open K9 app (first open), show me the account list and let me choose which one I want to manage right now.

I have nothing against the current behaviour, personally. There may be sound rationale behind UI redesigns and some users benefit from them. 
I wouldn't recommend however alienating existing users (including supporters and advocates) by brutally removing key features that made this app their app of choice.

While keeping the new behaviour as default, showing account list in app home behaviour could be made available to users really needing it via a checkbox in settings/display.

**Current behaviour:**
- 5.8 displays by default the inbox of the first account in the account list and forces the user to perform at least 3 taps, maybe additional scrolling (depending on screen size and number of accounts), to get to use any of the other accounts.
This is only viable to the user if the there is overwhelming focus on the first account ONLY and the others are seldom used. 
This is horrible when managing multiple accounts with balanced focus among them.

Alternatives?
- none viable found in app settings
- unified inbox may be of use for some users, but not for a well ordered and structured mind.
- downgrading for now
- eagerly waiting for positive K9 development response

For now, the only viable (for me, at least short term) solution was to downgrade to v5.6 according to this https://forum.k9mail.app/t/how-to-downgrade-to-an-earlier-version/1432 

As I read further in the forum, there are quite a number of users seriously affected by this UI loss of function in v5.8 and other issues as well. Not talking about disgruntled persons not liking the changed UI.

title: Add support for poll intervals smaller than 15 minutes (foreground service)
body:
I regularly need to get notified of certain events in the shortest possible amount of time. Due to regional restrictions and technical limitations, SMS notification and push notifications (eg. via Pushr) are not available to me. So email is the only available option to me.

Before the most recent update (the one with the UI change) I was able to set the fetch interval of individual mail accounts to very low settings. I always did that temporarily and with the explicit permission of the mailservers owner and administrator. (By the way: "Email push" is not available to me and has proven to be unreliable in the past, when I was on a different setup.)

Unfortunately with the new update, the shortest configurable fetch interwal is 15 minutes. I do understand that this is fine for most use cases but it puts me in a difficult situation. 15 minutes are at least 10 minutes too long (if not more) if I have to get notified asap.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I do understand that I might be somewhat of an edge case but I do want to politely ask for allowing users to set fetch intervals blow 15 minutes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If the removal of short fetch intervals was a measure to protect people from themselves, I want to suggest to hide the option for short fetch intervals inside a debug menu or "advanced" menu, which would prevent casual users from accidentally choosing "too short" fetch intervals.

title: Add support for setting account images (avatar)
body:
Some people add all of their email addresses to one system contact. And so all of their accounts in K-9 Mail show the same image.

To improve this situation we should allow users to pick what to display as the account image. I'm thinking we could have these options:
- contact picture (the current behavior)
- custom image (requires an image picker and probably a cropping tool; image should probably be included when settings are exported)
- no image (displays the placeholder image we currently use)

Especially the *custom image* option is probably quite a bit of work. So I suggest we start with just supporting the *contact picture* and *no image* option.
