title: k-9 5.800 causing vodafonemail.de to block the account
body:
**Describe the bug**
After Update to k-9 5.800 on Android 6.0.1, due to k-9's changed Push notification handling, k-9 seems to "hammer" IMAP servers more than before. This causes one of my mail providers, Vodafonemail.de, to block my account automatically every day, and I have to manually mail their support to un-block my account. Only to have it blocked again the next day. Their explanation (plus loose translation):

"Dein Email-Account war ungewöhnlich aktiv. Zur Sicherheit haben wir ihn gesperrt."
"Your email account has been unusally active. For security reasons, we blocked it."

and:

"[...] unsere Analysesysteme haben festgestellt, dass Dein Passwort mit hoher Wahrscheinlichkeit von Fremden ausgelesen wurde [...]"
"[...] our analysis engines found that your password was very likely obtained by a (malicious) third-party [...]"

This is simply untrue, and it started right after k-9 was updated to 5.800 on my device by Play Store.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. On Android 6.0.1, install k-9 pre-5.800
2. Setup an IMAP account with vodafonemail.de, activating poll every 12 hours as well as push with "Refresh IDLE connection" every 12 minutes
3. Enjoy k-9 working just fine, as it has been working for years
4. Update k-9 to 5.800
5. Wait a day or two until all IMAP logins get rejected, then log in via web interface to find said mail from abuse@vodafonemail.de

**Expected behavior**
k-9 should access the IMAP server the way it did before 5.800, without triggering any security automatisms.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.800
 - Android version: 6.0.1
 - Device: OnePlus 2
 - Account type: IMAP/SMTP

**Additional context**
Other IMAP accounts (Yahoo, as well as my accounts on a shared hoster) do not seem to have issues, thus far.
Apparently, I'm not the only user affected by this:
* https://forum.k9mail.app/t/account-blocked-email-provider-authentication-failure-5-800/1992
* https://forum.vodafone.de/t5/MeinVodafone-MeinKabel-E-Mail/IMAP-Passwort-ge%C3%A4ndert-funktioniert-aber-nicht/m-p/2682469 (forum in German)

title: Configurable message list actions
body:
**The Problem**

I use K-9 as well as mail clients on a PC. Generally I do two things with K-9: check new mail and sort spam. The actions I mostly use are: mark as read/unread (or star), mark as spam/ham, rarely delete. The actions that are available at the top of the screen in the folder view after marking (long-pressing) messages are: delete, mark read/unread, archive, (and move on horizontal screens)  don't match my workflow. The former two are available in the message view. I'd really prefer to have a spam/ham button instead of delete or archive.

Another place where quickly available actions don't match my routines are notifications. I'd prefer having spam/ham button instead of delete here too.

**Possible solution**

Make the order of actions fully configurable, so every one can customize the set of actions they have available as buttons/icons to match their own needs in all three contexts: the message list, the message view, and the notifications.

**Additional context**

Having #1793 implemented would also help me sort my spam/ham.


P.S. Thanks for the great new 5.800. It looks great and works like charm.

- `AccountSettingsDescriptions`
- `strings.xml`
- `Account`

title: Version 5.800 stopped recognizing user-installed CA
body:
**Describe the bug**
When using TLS with a a server whose certificate is signed by a non-mainstream CA, despite the CA certificate is installed in Android's CA store, K9 throws a dialog saying that the signer is unknown, and offering to accept server's certificate individually.

**To Reproduce**
1. Have a CA.
2. Have an SMTP / IMAP server that has certificate signed by the above CA.
3. Install certificate of the CA into Android's "trusted CA" store.
4. Verify that Chrome and Conversations (XMPP client) connect to web and jabber servers that use certificates signed by the above CA without warnings.
5. Try to configure K9 / have previous version configured to talk to an email server that uses certificate signed by the above CA.
6. Observe error message saying "Trust anchor for certification path not found", offering to accept or reject "key". 

**Expected behavior**
Like other TLS-capable Android applications, and like the previous version of K-9, TLS session with the server should be opened without complaint.

title: K-9 mail  doesn't register in microG for push notifications
body:
**Description**
For receiving push notifications, K-9 mail have to register in Google's cloud messaging service.
When using microG, the framework is rebuild by microG. The user has the possibility to see which apps are registered, as well as to "unregister" those apps which had registered themselves but where the user don't want to have push notifications from.

Usually, all registered apps are displayed there (e.g. messangers like Signal/Whatsapp, Google Play Store, GitHub, Firefox, ebay etc.), either in the "active" or in the "disabled" section.
Unfortunately, K-9 isn't displayed there.

I also re-installed latest K-9 mail v.5.800 to ensure a proper registration to the push services, but with no success.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Take a modded/rooted phone with microG installed instead of original Google framework, e.g. a phone with /e/ installed as OS.
2. Install latest K-9 mail v.5.800.
3. Import some email accounts.
4. Go to microG settings --> "cloud messaging" to see that K-9 hasn't registered itself.
5. In consequence, emails are only loaded manually, at least as long as you don't switch to polling.

**Expected behavior**
K-9 should be registered in microG / "cloud messaging" sheet installation.
A "self test" functionality for push messaging in the K-9 mail app would be also fine, if possible. :-)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.800
 - Android version: 11
 - Device: Xiaomi Poco X3, running ArrowOS (vanilla) with microG,
rooted with Magisk
 - Account type: IMAP (only one tested, others may be affected as well)

**Logs**
I guess they're not able to help, because I had to "capture" the push notification registration process - no idea how to do / how to force that.

title: Multiple notifications while reading emails on another device
body:
**Describe the bug**
When reading emails on another device (IMAP IDLE enabled on mobile), the new notification sounds on every new email marked as read (total new mail count is decreased as I am reading emails).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Enable IMAP IDLE on mobile
2. Wait for some new emails (more than one), notification properly appears on mobile (with sound)
3. Read some of the new emails on another device (e.g. desktop)
4. As soon as some of the mail is marked read on server (number of new emails is changed), new notifications pops making sound.

**Expected behavior**
I think the proper solution is not to make a sound again, update the existing notification instead (which should result to no-sound update). Unless another fresh email arrives - this would raise a new notification with sound.

**Environment:**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.800
 - Android version: 9
 - Device: Sony Xperia XZ1 Compact
 - Account type: IMAP with IDLE (Dovecot IMAP server)

body:

title: "What's new" snackbar might never be displayed
body: The intention was to only show the snackbar after app updates, but not when first installing the app. However, the "last version" remembered by `ChangeLog` is only written when the changelog/what's new screen is displayed. So unless users manually visit the screen they'll never see the snackbar on app updates (because the app still thinks it's the first run ever).

title: linebreaks are added to text of messages retrieved from server
body:
Ever since i use k-9, i notice that k-9 shortens line-length of messages, which it retrieved from the server (emphasizing that it is not about composing messages).

I guess that k-9 does this in an attempt to adjust text-content to the device's screen width. If the user zooms out/in, then k-9's adjusted line lengt is maintained and the text shrinks, leaving wasted "white area" horizontally, or the text expands beyond the screen area, respectively.

I consider this as a (design) bug, because it affects readability of text severely. Instead, k-9 could/should maintain the original line length and just wrap the text at the screen/window-edge, just as we are used to from our email clients on "desktop" environments: If the user zooms in, then the characters (should) become "larger" and wrapping (at screen/window-edge) is done "earlier" and more frequent, while if the user zooms out, then the characters (should) become smaller and the screen-edge-wrapping is done "later" and less frequent.

The problem in k-9's current approach becomes even worse when there is a "larger" image embedded into the content of the viewed message. Then, lines are typically modified* by k-9 to cover only a low number of words. Causing an extreme "gap" between the perceived text-"column"-width and the required zoom-choice in order to view a reasonable portion of the embedded image.

(*Yes, i do understand that the source code of a message is not modified by k-9 for other clients that might read the message later as well. The modification is of course only on k-9-displaying-level, therefore let's call it a "virtual" modification).

In the mentioned case of an embedded larger image, it only slightly matters whether k-9 zooms in to fit the "narrow" text-column (which it produced by adding virtual linebreaking) to the screen-width automatically vs. whether it zooms out to fit the image into the screen width automatically. Either way, I believe it is not the best choice.

title: immediate expunge doesn't expunge
body:
If an imap account in v5.734 is configured with...:
- no folder for deleted/deleting messages
- on deleting (a) message(s), also delete it/them from the server
- immediate expunging after moving etc. of (a) messages(s)

then i would expect that...:
- first: the message(s) is/are marked as deleted (on server)
- second: displaying of the referred message(s) in k-9's UI as "is-marked-as-deleted" (if that is available at all?) being skipped
- third: the message(s) is/are physically deleted (from server and from k-9's cache)

but instead k-9 does not perform the last (expunge) step (at least not successfully. I didn't yet check a server logfile on whether expunging was tried but failed, or whether it was not tried at all. all imap servers, on which my accounts are run, are dovecot on ubuntu.).

However, if k-9's config is set to expunge-on-each-sync, then it's done successfully with the first manually triggered sync-command after the previous message-deletion-command.

That's why I guess that there is no basic expunge-compatibility-problem between k-9 and the servers, but instead a problem with k-9's execution of its immediate-expunge-setting.

body:
**Describe the bug**
After searching for (older) email, used Reply and Reply All before selecting "Download Complete Message" resulted in error.  First time returns K9 to the inbox list.  After repeated attempts, K9 will FC. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. From inbox or unified inbox, searched for older message
2.  found message with "Download Complete Message" shown at bottom (doesn't matter if attachment or not)
3.  Did NOT click on "Download Complete Message" but instead selected Reply (and Reply all - same result)
4.  After clicking Reply or Reply all, K9 reverted to inbox list of email (did not show new email response)
5.  With (2 or 3) repeated attempts, K9 then crashed/FC

**Expected behavior**
Reply or Reply All yields a new message that can edited/typed and sent.

**Screenshots**
n/a

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.734
 - Android version: 10  (Samsung ver FFUE1)
 - Device: Galaxy S9 SM-G960F 
 - Account type: IMAP

**Describe the bug**
After searching for (older) email, used Reply and Reply All before selecting "Download Complete Message" resulted in error.  First time returns K9 to the inbox list.  After repeated attempts, K9 will FC. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. From inbox or unified inbox, searched for older message
2.  found message with "Download Complete Message" shown at bottom (doesn't matter if attachment or not)
3.  Did NOT click on "Download Complete Message" but instead selected Reply (and Reply all - same result)
4.  After clicking Reply or Reply all, K9 reverted to inbox list of email (did not show new email response)
5.  With (2 or 3) repeated attempts, K9 then crashed/FC

**Expected behavior**
Reply or Reply All yields a new message that can edited/typed and sent.

n/a

 -  5.734

title: Separate PGP keys for multiple identies under the same account.
body:
I have an email solution set up where I have a single account, and multiple forwarding only addresses set up so that I can use filtering rules to sort my mail based on the address the sender has been given. Because I do not want all these addresses to be visible to the public, they have separate PGP keys, not all of which are available on the public keyservers.

Because of this, it would be nice if I could set a separate PGP key for each identity on a single email account.

title: mail not sent without user notification after change of credentials on server
body:
Please search to check for an existing issue - done

**Description**
After changing the credentials on the mail server the user is notified by K9 for the inbox (wrong password message) **BUT not for the outgoing mail**! This results in mail being kept in the OUTBOX as unsent. I only recognized that several days after the change of the credentials that emails are stuck in the outbox.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Change password on mail server - in my case this is GMX. GMX requires credentials for send (SMTP) and sync via IMAP to the device
2. Compose new email and press send
3. Check contents of OUTBOX folder on the device - the email just created and sent sits there idling

**Expected behavior**
Error message/warning that the mail could not be sent (possibly with reason).

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.600
 - Android version: 9
 - Device: Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 (mido) /w LineageOS
 - Account type: IMAP

**Additional context**
This is a very irritating behavior: the user is notified about the wrong credentials immediately, as soon as K9 is trying to fetch new mail via IMAP. The correct password supplied in the K9 prompt is only used for sync of inbox and folders  with imap.gmx.net (required credentials are user and password) but not for the OUTBOX folder which is connected to mail.gmx.net (SMPT server for outgoing mail; required credentials are again user and password).

title: App crashes when moving a message
body:
Please search to check for an existing issue (including closed issues, for which the fix may not have yet been released) before opening a new issue: https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues?q=is%3Aissue

If you are unsure whether or not you have found a bug please post to the support forum instead: https://forum.k9mail.app

**Describe the bug**
The app crashes, when I try to delete an email.
In this case, I try to delete an email which is 157 times in the send items because the app crashed every time during sending.
k-9 is fresh installed.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to 'Send Elements'
2. Click on on a conversation
3. Select an email
4. Click the delete icon
5. The app crashes

**Expected behavior**
The email gets deleted and the app doesn't crash

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.734 (latest beta from play store)
 - Android version: 6.0.1
 - Device: Lenovo YT3-X90F
 - Account type: IMAP (It's a work account from outlook.office365.com)

title: Configurable message actions
body:
Different people use email in very different ways. Some actions on messages (delete, archive, mark as unread,  move, reply, …) are very important to one group of users, but are never used by others. K-9 Mail currently offers limited support to alter the list of actions that are displayed in the toolbar when viewing a message. This can be configured under 
`Settings > General settings > Display > Visible message actions`.

The existing feature isn't very flexible and works in ways that is surprising to many users. I suggest to change it so actions can be freely reordered or completely removed from the toolbar. The user interface for configuring message actions could be a list consisting of three sections. The first one contains the items that are displayed as icons in the toolbar, limited to a sensible number (maybe 4 or 5). The second section contains items that are displayed in the overflow menu (three dots). The third section contains additional actions that the user doesn't want to display at all.
Items in the list can be reordered using drag and drop, which also allows moving an item from one section to another.

The fact that we have sub-menus ("Send…" and "Refile…") makes this a bit more complicated. For a first implementation I suggest we keep the items of the sub-menus fixed and only allow the sub-menus itself to be reordered. The contents of the sub-menus should also exist as single items that can be placed individually. This may lead to an action being available twice in the toolbar, e.g. "Move" as icon and then as part of the "Refile…" sub-menu. But the same is true with the current implementation.

Another complication is the fact that we support a split-screen view where the message list and the message contents are displayed next to each other. In this view we "merge" the toolbar actions. Suggestions on how to best handle this situation are welcome.

Related: #3530

title: Message bodies for remote search results aren't downloaded automatically
body:
**Describe the bug**
The body of a message fetched during a remote search isn't downloaded automatically when such a message is opened for viewing.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Set up an IMAP account
2. Check `Settings > [Account] > Search > Enable server search'
3. Open an IMAP folder (message list screen)
4. Tap the magnifying glass to start a local search
5. Tap the magnifying glass with the cloud icon to perform the search on the server
6. Wait for the search to complete so you don't run into issue #4412
7. Open a search result message that was fetched from the server (doesn't show a preview)
8. Message body is empty and "Download complete message" button is displayed

**Expected behavior**
The message body should be downloaded when a search result message is opened for viewing.

**Environment:**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.734-SNAPSHOT
 - Account type: IMAP

**Additional context**
This used to work. `MessageLoaderHelper` contains code to download the message body when neither `Flag.X_DOWNLOADED_PARTIAL` nor `Flag.X_DOWNLOADED_FULL` is set. But one of the storage refactorings broke this. Currently one of these flags is always set.

title: Unified Archive Folder
body:
If feasible it would be great to have a unified archive folder in addition to the already existing unified inbox. The reasoning for this boils down to my workflow:

I love to keep my inbox clean. So the mails there are the ones I actively need to work on. If I'm done with an email, I'm moving it to the archive folder. If the email needs to be revisited later (e.g. I'm waiting for a reply) I also flag the email before moving to archive. Somewhen in the future, I navigate to the archive folder and filter for flagged emails to figure out if there's anything which needs further action.

While this is certainly possible right now with K-9 by navigating to each archive folder of every account, it would be easier if there's one archive folder showing messages from all accounts. Like there is one for inboxes.

title: Mixed encoding personal name only displays part of the name
body:
**Describe the bug**
I've just received a phishing email that K-9 shows as being from "UPS(GB)". The spacing is wrong, but it's easy for someone to confuse it with a legitimate UPS email. Viewing it in Thunderbird, I see that the name is "(krumhqcx) UPS(GB) (neejeugsesjvdbymtb)". That is FAR easier to spot as a malicious email.

Looking at the headers, I see that the From address has an encoded UTF-8 block, which is the only bit that K-9 is showing:

```
From: (krumhqcx) =?utf-8?B?VVBTKEdCKQ==?= (neejeugsesjvdbymtb)
 <joracing@hotmail.it>
```

I don't know whether the spammers are intentionally triggering a common bug to have a longer unique name that spam filters ignore but that then only displays the short name to users, or whether it's just an accident.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use default "show friendly name" view
2. Receive email containing a mix of ASCII and encoded UTF-8 blocks in the friendly name part
3. Compare name in header versus name in K-9
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
K-9 should show the full name from the header when displaying the header and not just a substring of it (as long as there is sufficient space)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.600
 - Android version: 10
 - Device: OnePlus 5
 - Account type: IMAP

**Additional context**

Given how spammers/phishers operate, this is a security risk for users (even if it's not a security vulnerability in K-9 itself)

title: Neither list of mails nor view of individual mails show sender address or domain, makes phishing possible
body:
An organization was recently subject of a phishing attack were mails were send to many employees. The mail claimed to come from a high-level corporate officer. Let's call him Big Boss with his regular mail address of big.boss@corp.com. The authors of the phishing mail were aware of the corporate officer's name and sent the mail in his name, but with some randomly generate mail address: Big Boss <abc123@google.com>
K-9 Mail, used in version 5.732, shows in the list of all mails (mailbox content) just sender's claimed name ('Big Boss'), subject, and part of the mail body. When opening the mail for reading, still only claimed sender name, subject, mail body and other information is shown, but not the sender's mail address or at least the domain of the email address ('corp.com' vs 'google.com'). A well-crafted phishing mail cannot be discerned from a valid email of the real sender, despite that *it would be really easy to see in this case if the sender's mail address would be visible*.
I know that there is a 'show headers' function which allows you to inspect the underlying data including the sender's email address, but this is quite technical (thus not an option for many laymen) and requires to scroll through a lot of headers to find just the one line you are looking for.

title: Only hide attachment boxes for images that are actually displayed inline
body:
Currently we hide attachments with a `Content-Disposition` value of `inline` and a `Content-Type` value matching `image/*`. Most of the time these are inline images referenced in a `text/html` part. But we should check to make sure that's actually the case. Otherwise users won't be able to access attachments that are not referenced in the `text/html` part. 

I noticed this happening on a mailing list where the `text/html` part was stripped. The `text/plain` part does reference the images using `[cid:…]`. But displaying images in `text/plain` parts is not something K-9 Mail supports right now.

body:
I'm running K-9 mail 5.731. Here's an issue.

Yesterday I _seemingly_ successfully sent an email (I used an already sent one and hit "Edit as new message") however today I've found out that it **only** exists in the Sent folder of my K-9 application, i.e. it's not on the server (I'm obviously using the IMAP protocol with plain TLS authentication, i.e. no Oauth2 or other shenanigans).

Now I've got a number of questions:
1. How can I know whether I've actually sent it or not? The message contains Message-ID (`<UUID@domain.com>`) but I've no idea whether the ID is generated by the app or was given to the app by the server. I do not want to sent the message again.
2. How can I actually save the message to my Sent folder? Whenever I hit Refile, I get, "Cannot copy or move a message which is not synchronized with the server".

I've already asked my email provider support whether they've actually sent the message or not but it's not certain whether they'll reply or confirm.

Today I've sent two test messages, first normally via "Compose" and then I sent an old one via "Edit as new" and everything works as expected, so I've no idea what the glitch was yesterday.

title: Save account passwords with settings
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If you have multiple accounts (10, atm...), it can get tiresome to go through all passwords if you need to reinstall.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add an option to save passwords along setting (in same or separate file).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If adding encryption code is beyond scope, just add option to save them in plain text, and keep it disabled by default, with a warning about plain text.

**Additional context**
About saving plain text passwords: you may just want to keep a local copy of your settings, in case you need to reinstall, in which case, if the device is ever compromised to the point they can be read from a plain text file, that will be the least of your problems.

***
Unrelated, but not worth opening an issue for, imv:
Portuguese (pt-pt) language translation for end-to-end encryption setting says "OenPGP", missing a "p".

title: K-9 Mail size is heavy and it is impossible to reduce it
body:
**Describe the bug**

K-9 app uses 676 Mo of user data on my phone. It is impossible to clear that data because it is not cached data.

I found that this data is mainly composed of an `app_webview/BrowserMetrics` folder (616Mo) that can't be deleted.

If it is email cached data, we need a way to clear that cache.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to the application information menu in Android Parameters > Applications > K-9 Mail
2. In "Storage and cache", I can see that user data is big.

**Expected behavior**

If that data are email data, I expect them to be in the cache data of the app to have a way to clean it.
If that data in `BrowserMetrics` are just some metrics, I think that they can be automatically deleted or never stored. 

**Screenshots**

title: [Feature Request] Compose - Delivery Status Notification & Attach My Public Key
body:
On Mozilla Thunderbird when Composing a new email, there's a few options including Return Receipt, Delivery Status Notification, Do Not Encrypt or Require Encryption, Digitally Sign This Message and Attach My Public Key 🗝. 

The two that K-9 Mail does not have which would be useful are Delivery Status Notification and Attach My Public Key. 

It would be great if you could add those two to the top right menu on the Compose view. Although I imagine that you might have to work with the Developer(s) for OpenKeyChain to add the Attach My Public Key option. 

Also could you please make it clearer when either of those are selected, such as make a checkmark ✅ appear when selected? Because right now when we tap on "Return Receipt" for example, there's just a toast notification that appears at the bottom for a brief moment. 

Thank you.

title: Add support for the signal encryption protocol.
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I use openPGP so now and then, but it is very cumbersome to use, since you need to share your public key with every person you want to be in contact with (and vica-versa). 
That makes people not wanting to put the effort in it, to properly secure their private e-mails. Since it takes away too much time to exchange each others public keys.

The signal encryption protocol takes away this inconvenience, because it uses a more practical form of end-2-end encryption.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I really love to see the signal encryption protocol being added to the application.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There are not very much alternatives, that take away the inconveniences that openPGP causes, while keeping the data secure.
Since the Signal encryption protocol is open source, very secure, and very easy to use; I think that every e-mail software should have this built in by default.

Have a nice day!
Dave

title: Use UnifiedPush for push notifications
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I would like to be able to use android without google services. Currently notifications must use FCM unless each app developer hosts a notification gateway which drains battery.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I suggest using [UnifiedPush](https://unifiedpush.org/), the community successor to [OpenPush](https://bubu1.eu/openpush/). I believe the technical approach would be to use the "FCM-added" form of the UnifiedPush [android-connector](https://unifiedpush.org/developers/android/) library so that users who don't care about the minimal FCM data can continue to use it as before.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Although UnifiedPush is brand new, I'm not aware of any other app-independent implementation. As mentioned before, it is possible to avoid FCM if each app developer hosts their own server and the client wakes up frequently, draining the battery life.

**Additional context**
The only currently available UnifiedPush app is FluffyChat, implemented in [lib/utils/firebase_controller.dart](https://gitlab.com/famedly/fluffychat/-/commit/124a5eedf84854f4dcbbf7b9dc2a4a5ea2387f5a?view=parallel).

title: Notification rules
body:
Not all emails are equally important and deserve a notification. Right now K-9 Mail offers the following options:
- never create a notification for new messages
- only notify for messages from contacts
- don't show notifications for messages where the sender address is one of your account's identities
- only notify for messages in certain folders (using the clunky folder class mechanism)
- don't notify during "quiet time"

Often more flexibility would be nice. But I don't want to keep adding special cases. Instead I'd like us to have a generic rules-based system for deciding whether or not to create a notification.

A notification rule should have the following properties:
- **description/comment**: so users remember what the rule was all about
- **enabled state**: sometime you want to disable rules without deleting them
- **action**: the action that should be performed when the rule matches
  - *mute*: don't create a notification
  - *notification_channel*: create a notification using a particular notification channel; that way you can have different notification sounds, vibration on/off, etc
  - … maybe more in the future
- **action_extra**: argument for the 'action' method, e.g. the ID of the notification channel
- potentially multiple **clauses**: a rule matches when all clauses match
  - **property**: which property of the message is used for matching (e.g. sender, subject, body, header)
  - **property_extra**: free-form text to further describe the property, e.g. a particular header name
  - **match**: how to match the property (e.g. equals, contains, starts-with, etc.)
  - **match_extra**: free-form text to provide the argument for the 'match' method

We still want dedicated user interfaces for certain features, e.g. mute sender, mute thread/conversation. But we'll also want a user interface that gives access to all properties of a notification rule.


### Examples

#### Separate notification channel for company-internal emails
```
clause:
  property: sender
  match: matches
  match_extra: *@company.example
action: notification_channel
action_extra: company
```

#### High priority messages
```
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: X-Priority
  match: equals
  match_extra: 1
action: notification_channel
action_extra: important
```

#### High priority messages from company-internal senders
```
clause:
  property: sender
  match: matches
  match_extra: *@company.example
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: X-Priority
  match: equals
  match_extra: 1
action: notification_channel
action_extra: important
```

#### Mute sender
```
clause:
  property: sender
  match: equals
  match_extra: annoying-user@domain.example
action: mute
```

#### Mute mailing lists
```
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: List-Id
  match: exists
action: mute
```

#### Mute particular thread
```
clause:
  property: header
  property_extra: References
  match: contains
  match_extra: <messageid@domain.example>
action: mute
```

### Implementation notes

- Notification rules should be per account (per folder?)
- Create dedicated database tables for notification rules
- Add support for importing/exporting notification rules

title: PGP/MIME subjects from Thunderbird are not decrypted/shown
body:
**Describe the bug**
The actual subject of a PGP/MIME message (as sent by Thunderbird 78.6) is not decrypted and shown in the message list or message display.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Send an encrypted message to yourself in Thunderbird with a descriptive subject.
2. Use K9 to view the message list for that account.
3. Open the encrypted message in K9.
4. Return to the message list and find the encrypted message again.
5. Note that subject fields in all views contain only "...".

**Expected behavior**
After the message is opened the subject encrypted in the PGP/MIME multipart message should be displayed in both the list and the message itself, similar to what's done for messages sent by K9 itself.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.727 (from F-Droid)
 - Android version: 10
 - Device: Pixel 2 XL
 - Account type: IMAP

**Additional context**
This may be related to [this pull request](https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/pull/3309); a comment there (from two years ago) says it's not on the Play Store yet, but I suspect that's out of date.

Looks like turnabout is fair play, in that [Thunderbird can't read subjects encrypted by K9 either](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1687379).

title: Add release dates to changelog
body:
With #5098 merged, the changelog now supports a `date` attribute on `<release>` elements. Someone should go back and add dates for past releases to the changelog. 
All releases are tagged in the Git repository. Using the date of the tagged commit should be close enough to the actual release date. 

The date format should be `YYYY-MM-DD`.
The changelog can be found here: https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/blob/main/app/ui/legacy/src/main/res/raw/changelog_master.xml

Example:
```xml
<release version="5.726" versioncode="27026" date="2021-01-06">
    <change>Updated password input fields to be able to reveal passwords</change>
    <change>Added support for going back to previous steps when setting up an account</change>
    <change>Fixed a couple of crashes</change>
    <change>Updated translations</change>
</release>
```

title: Broken message aborts folder sync with NullPointerException
body:
**Describe the bug**
When refreshing the message list of an IMAP folder that contains a message broken(?) in some way, the folder refresh aborts at the broken message. No messages that have arrived to the mailbox after the broken message, including the broken message, are displayed. Other IMAP clients like Thunderbird and Roundcube show all messages in the folder.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Have a message that triggers the bug in a folder on IMAP server
2. Refresh that folder in K9
3. See the list of messages in that folder not contain messages after the broken message, including the broken message
4. Also see the exception displayed in the folder list

**Expected behavior**
No exceptions to be shown and folder message list in K9 to show all messages in the folder.

**Screenshots**
Attached is a screenshot of the folder exhibiting this issue, cropped from the folder list.
![Screenshot_20210118-025501](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2458254/104861933-58ef8700-593a-11eb-9154-7c4a3667d41d.jpg)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.600 (latest release from Google Play Store)
 - Android version: 10 (OxygenOS 10.3.7)
 - Device: OnePlus 6T (A6013)
 - Account type: IMAP (Dovecot server)

**Additional context**
The triggering message is a malformed mime multipart/alternative spam email with text/plain and text/html parrts. Other mail clients do not seem to display what the spammer intended either, but they don't cause the folder to "freeze" to the point in time when the mail arrived, i.e. they show all other messages that arrived after the broken email.

**Logs**
Debug log starts from the point of refreshing the message list for "bugfolder", which only contains this one broken message to reduce clutter in the log. The bug also manifests itself in folders with more messages. Some identifying details of the server account and the email/address have been replaced.
[k9nullp2-redacted.txt](https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/files/5827234/k9nullp2-redacted.txt)

title: Notification spam (one notification per new email)
body:
**Describe the bug**

When using polling (since IMAP push is not available in current beta) I get notification spamming every time emails are fetched. this is because every new email gets its own notification triggered, so if you get many emails between the polling intervals, you don't get one *ding* per account but one *ding* per email, which can be quite disturbing when you get lots of them.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Set your poll interval for example to 30 minutes.
2. poll your emails
3. close K-9
4. send yourself many emails (10 for example) from another device - make sure you have "notifications for own messages" enabled.
5. wait for the next poll
6. Receive 10 times *ding*

**Expected behavior**
Usually there should be one notification stating that there are x new emails.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.724
 - Android version: 11
 - Device: Google Pixel 4a
 - Account type: IMAP


P.S. Of course, having IMAP PUSH back would be much better :-)

title: Show folder drawer when pressing back button from message list
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
To make the folder drawer appear (the thing that slides from the left side of the screen), the only option is to slide your finger all the way from the left side of the screen. This motion is uncomfortable and also takes significant time (in UX terms).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Many apps show such drawers when the user presses the "Back" button on their devices. This is valid on the last-before-exit screen. It would make it much easier and faster to open the drawer. This behavior would not really add much overhead to users that don't rely on it but are used to exiting the app with pressing "Back", "Back", "Back", ... since they would just add one more "Back" press (which they might already do; I argue that very few people are so careful to count their "Back" presses when they just want to close the app).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None.

I noticed that you had suggested and implemented #4313. I think that from a UX perspective, the behavior I describe above is preferable. The user opens the drawer to do sth, e.g. select a folder or account. That action already closes the drawer once performed. Even if the user just wants to close the drawer without performing an action, there is the option to simply tap on the semi-hidden message list or swipe clumsily to the left from **anywhere** in the screen. This means that the level of accuracy and effort required is less than minimal. On the other hand, opening the drawer is disproportionally hard.

I have a phone with a 6.5" screen and switching accounts is very difficult. I have to stretch my thumb all the way to the top left corner, a very uncomfortable motion.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great if the icons were moved (optionally?) to the bottom of the drawer (the thing that slides in from the left side of the screen). This does not have to be sth super slick and intelligent, just a new row with the account icons in series one by one. If you have more that the row can show, it would just be scrollable. This would also solve the issue that when more than 3 accounts are in place, using the account icons at the top of the drawer is unintuitive and only cycle among 3 accounts only.

The top space of the drawer would show what is still does, but the account **selection** buttons (not the bigger one that shows the active account) could be replaced with account, folder and general setting buttons. This way the "Settings" option would be moved from the bottom to the top as a non-frequently used option (I would argue that users don't visit the settings more than they switch accounts).

Here is a rough example:

![example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11805218/98535591-aab6c980-2286-11eb-9ed7-7b277e17338d.jpg)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I tried using either the account icons or the drop down list, but they are both at the left top corner. I also tried using the unified inbox, but I turned it off. It also wouldn't solve the issue of switching accounts for other things other than reading the inbox.

title: [EPIC] Simple Phishing Protection
body:
Often, not to say almost always, when a mail contains a link with a link text looking like an URL is not matching the actually link target. Usually it is due to tracking wrappers but it could also be to deceive the reader in some phising mails.
The problem in the later case is quite obvious, while the one in the former one is mainly that links don't open in their corresponding apps. For example clicking a YouTube link opens it in the browser instead of the NewPipe app...
So this could be either just a convenience problem but also a privacy (tracking) or security (phishing) problem.

What I like to have is the option, ideally enabled by default, which after clicking such a link displays a dialog that briefly informs about the problem, shows both links (the link text and the actual URL) and allows choosing which one to open.
Optionally there could also be the option to remember the decision and not to show the dialog again.

body:
If I understand all correctly k9 fetches the whole letter and `Preview lines` only set how much lines to display.
Thus, it takes a very long time to fetch a mailbox with a lot of messages (like a maillist), especially on the cellular internet.
Yep, there is a message size limit to fetch, but it's not that I want. I'd like the same behaviour as on desktop thunderbird:
1. Only headers are download.
2. The full message is loaded that time it's opened.

com`
The app will now see every line as single address and think you want to send mails to `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz@outlook.` and `com`.

**Expected behavior**
The app should see the address as a single one, even after a new line.

**Environment**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.721
 - Android version: 10
 - Device: Samsung Galaxy A9

title: Mails with empty body text not sent
body:
**Describe the bug**
When creating a new mail, it is (quietly) not sent, when no text is entered for the body (even if attachments exist), using the latest beta from Play Store

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create new mail
2. Enter recipient and subject
3. Do not enter a text in the body
4. Send mail
5. Email is not sent but no message is shown and mail disappears


**Expected behavior**

**Expected behavior**
Prompt the user for a storage location. Download and write the file to that location.

**Environment:**
 - K-9 Mail version: 5.721
 - Android version: tested with Android 11

**Note:**
I don't want us to request the `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission just to be able to use `DownloadManager`. So we'll probably have to download the image ourselves. Ideally we'll use an existing library for that. Suggestions welcome.

title: Remove POP3 support
body:
Remove support for the POP3 protocol.

K-9 Mail never supported POP3's "download then delete from server" model. The app tries to treat POP3 accounts similar to IMAP where we download copies of messages but treat the server as single source of truth. Some settings exist to weaken that model, but the goal of #4970 is to get rid of these, too.

The hardest part about the removal is a deprecation strategy. We'll have to inform users that support for POP3 is going away before we actually remove it. They should have plenty of time to prepare moving to another protocol or another email client. I propose we show a non-dismissable info message above the message list. Clicking it could lead to a blog post with more information on the topic.

I don't want us to automatically delete user data. So once POP3 support is removed I propose we convert remaining POP3 accounts to read-only accounts. Users will still be able to view messages. They won't be able to copy, move, delete, or compose new messages from that account.

*This is part of the effort to [remove support for local messages](https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/4970).*

title: Remove setting 'sync server deletions'
body:
Remove the setting 'Sync server deletions' and always delete the local copy when a message has been removed from the server.

Since this is a behavior change for people who don't use the default value where server deletions are synced, we need to inform those users about the change. I propose to disable automatic sync (and Push) and to show a warning message in the message list screen above the message list. Clicking this warning will display a dialog with more details. Acknowledging this message will restore the previous automatic sync and Push settings. 
Manually refreshing a folder should probably also display this dialog if the change hasn't been acknowledged by the user yet.

*This is part of the effort to [remove support for local messages](https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues/4970).*

body:
Remove the setting 'When I delete a message' and always delete a message from the server when it is deleted locally. 

Since this is a behavior change for people who don't use the default value of "Delete from server" we need to inform those users about the change. title: Remove support for local messages
body:
### Motivation

K-9 Mail currently offers a couple of features that lead to the creation of local messages, i.e. messages that are not connected to a message on the server. However, K-9 Mail doesn't properly support such messages leading to all kinds of problems. 

Changing K-9 Mail to properly support local messages requires a lot of work. It would also require a way to import and export local messages so users can change devices and/or clients without losing their messages. While all of these are desirable features I don't see us getting there anytime soon.

Instead I'd like us to concentrate on making K-9 Mail an email client that works great for managing messages stored on a server (the IMAP model). Of course K-9 Mail will still keep local copies of messages and it will still be possible to compose emails while being offline. So we still need limited support for local messages. But those messages will be linked to a message on the server once the app had a chance to upload them. This should require a lot less special cases.

### Steps
- #4971 Remove setting 'when I delete a message' (messages deleted locally will always be removed from the server)
- #4973 Remove setting 'sync server deletions' (server deletions will always remove the local copy)
- #4974 Remove POP3 support

body:
### Expected behaviour
The desired behaviour for me is that I can add the 'Move' action to action taskbars at the top of the screen by amending the options under 'Settings > General settings > Display > Visible message actions'

It would be great if the app itself could indicate that it is currently fetching, for example by a different color of the grey underline.
I am using this app via the Android beta program.

title: File attachment name broken - Filename scrambled / wrong encoding
body:
### Expected behavior
I want file attachments in mail drafts/sent mails to be shown and opened correctly even if the filename contains german umlauts (äöü...). I want k9mail to cope correctly even if they have badly encoded filenames.

### Actual behavior
If I add an attachment from k9mail everything works as intended. As soon as I use another client to add a file attachment to a draft email and store it to the imap drafts folder, this attachments name is not properly downloaded via imap from my (gmx) draft folder to k9mail. The same happens if i add the attachment and just send it. k9mail is not showing the mail attachment correctly in the sent mail and in the inbox if I send it to myself.
Instead the filename is scrambled in a more or less URL/percent-encoded way and is shown as a attachment with the name (example) UTF-8''%45%69%6E%76%65%72%73%74%C3%A4%6E%64%6E%69%73%65%72%6B
I also cannot open the file with k9mail.

If I url encode this I get back `UTF-8''Einverständniserk` which is parts of my original file name "Einverständniserklärung.pdf"

I actually add the attachment to the mail draft using Thunderbird 68.10.0 (64-Bit) with Windows OS.
As soon as I sync my imap in k9mail, I can see the mail draft including the broken attachment

Note: When I add attachments without umlaut characters, k9mail shows the attachment name as intended.
Note: When I log on to my email provider web-account the attachment is always shown correctly! So the provider seems to be more robust to such filenames.

### Steps to reproduce
1. use thunderbird (on windows) to add a file attachment with umlauts to some email draft
2. sync the mail account with imap
3. use k9mail to also sync imap
4. watch the draft or to send it to somebody
5. check the attachment file name, it is scrambled

### Environment
K-9 Mail version: 5.600
Android version: 10
Account type (IMAP, POP3, WebDAV/Exchange): imap

title: URLs in reopened drafts are bracket expanded not delimited (recursively)
body:
### Expected behavior
URLs in drafts are left as written or is delimited once according to common practice and recommendations ([RFC 3986, app. C](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#appendix-C)).

The recommendation and long standing practice (tracing back to an [appendix of W3C's URL specification from 1994](https://www.w3.org/Addressing/URL/5.1_Wrappers.html) which the RFC builds upon) is to **delimit** URLs using angle brackets to allow a somewhat consistent interpretation (introduces some robustness to especially added line breaks).

### Actual behavior
Every URL present in a draft is expanded, not delimited, with a space and itself in angle brackets when it is reopened for editing. Such that fx. `http://example.com` becomes `http://example.com <http://example.com>`.

The expansion is even recursive, so when reopening a saved draft for the second time this occurs again for both the original URL and the URL in brackets such that fx. `http://example.com <http://example.com>` becomes `http://example.com <http://example.com> <http://example.com <http://example.com>>`, and this will continue.

This seems to me to be a misunderstanding trying to provide a rendered representative text for an URL, like the anchor text of a HTML anchor or a Markdown hyperlink. A bit like Markdown's ["autolink" which uses angle brackets](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax#autolink) as a shortcut to creating HTML hyperlinks with the URL as duplicate anchor text in the rendering. However, I think K9 is not intended to do any interpreting of the text here. And I'll be surprised if this has has anything to do with the IMAP store (gmail).

As a side note, it also looks like [Wordpress has been discussing the use of angle brackets in links being sent, and they lost](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/44589).

### Steps to reproduce
1. First edit; Write new mail containing an URL (body="Http://example.com"), see screenshot 1
2. Save as draft (back->Save as draft or menu->Save as draft), see screenshot 2
3. Second edit; Reopen draft message, observe the expanded URL yielding one duplicate, write some more text ("Test"), see screenshot 3
4. Save as draft (back->Save as draft or menu->Save as draft), see screenshot 4
5. Third edit; Reopen draft message, observe the two URLs each expanded yielding 3 duplicates, see screenshot 5
6. Continue editing, if this is your idea of fun ;)

### Environment
* **K-9 Mail version**: 5.717, see screenshot 6
* **Android version**: 7.0, see screenshot 7
* **Account type (IMAP, POP3, WebDAV/Exchange)**: IMAP (gmail)
* **Phone model**: Samsung Galaxy S8, SM-G950F

The recommendation and long standing practice (tracing back to an [appendix of W3C's URL specification from 1994]([URL] which the RFC builds upon) is to **delimit** URLs using angle brackets to allow a somewhat consistent interpretation (introduces some robustness to especially added line breaks).


Every URL present in a draft is expanded, not delimited, with a space and itself in angle brackets when it is reopened for editing. Such that fx. `[URL] becomes `[URL] <[URL]

The expansion is even recursive, so when reopening a saved draft for the second time this occurs again for both the original URL and the URL in brackets such that fx. `[URL] <[URL] becomes `[URL] <[URL] <[URL] <[URL] and this will continue.

This seems to me to be a misunderstanding trying to provide a rendered representative text for an URL, like the anchor text of a HTML anchor or a Markdown hyperlink. A bit like Markdown's ["autolink" which uses angle brackets]([URL] as a shortcut to creating HTML hyperlinks with the URL as duplicate anchor text in the rendering. However, I think K9 is not intended to do any interpreting of the text here. And I'll be surprised if this has has anything to do with the IMAP store (gmail).

### Expected behavior
Performing multiple editing sessions on a draft message in K9 should synchronise all changes to IMAP, allowing to start a message in K9 while on mobile to continue and finish it using an IMAP desktop client.

title: if key changed by the counter party, then the "Key has been changed" should be displayed to the user
body:
Please search to check for an existing issue (including closed issues, for which the fix may not have yet been released) before opening a new issue: https://github.com/k9mail/k-9/issues?q=is%3Aissue

### Expected behavior
If counter party has changed his/her gpg key, this should somehow be shown to the user. 
1) if Autocrypt mode is ON then 
  the email message display should contain something like "Key has been changed" and K9 should put the new key into Open keychain automatically

2) if Autocrypt mode is OFF then
  the email message display should contain something like "Key has been changed" and K9 should propose to add the update the key for this counterparty in Open Keychain manually

### Actual behavior
Tell us what happens instead
In both cases (Autocrypt ON and OFF) K9 does not display any warnings regarding the change of the key and the new key is being added into the Open Keychain
 
### Steps to reproduce
1. Connect delta chat to the same IMAP account without transitting autocrypt auto setup, so that 2 isntances of deltachat have two different private/public key pairs for same email
2. send email from #1 instance of delta chat to the test account in K9
3. send email from #2 instance of delta chat to the test account in K9
4. Check Open Keychain -- now it has two different keys for the same email and the last one is active for K9 (marked with K9 icon)

### Environment
K-9 Mail version:
5.717

9

title: Run a foreground service during mail checks initiated by the user
body:
When running periodic mail checks WorkManager makes sure the system knows K-9 Mail is currently doing work in the background and shouldn't be killed. 
When the user triggers a folder/account sync in the UI and then closes the Activity the system currently has no way of knowing that K-9 Mail is still doing work in the background and shouldn't be killed. This could lead to the sync being interrupted but the sync notification remaining visible (and animated) until the next sync successfully completes and removes the notification (see #4747).

The easiest way to fix this is to always start a foreground service for user-initiated mail checks. This means always showing the sync notification even when not enabled by the user (we should probably get rid of the setting then).

Right now we show and hide the sync notification for each individual folder. We probably need to change this to start the foreground service once, perform all folder/account syncs currently queued up, and then stop the service.

title: Display error indicator when email is not standard-compliant
body:
Display an error indicator when we detect that the email isn't standard-compliant and it's likely that this has caused us to improperly parse/decode the message.

Ideally we'd include useful information on what exactly our parser didn't like so users can forward this information to the sender of the message.

See #4846

title: A new subfolder should inherit the settings of the parent folder
body:
A newly created subfolder should inherit the settings of their parent folder.

Example:
I create a new subfolder (Inbox/mailing-list) in my inbox for emails from a mailing list.
Using a thunderbird filter all mails with "[mailing-list]" in the subject are moved to the new folder.
Now I'd still like those emails to pop up in the common inbox of all accounts.

Current behaviour:
After refreshing the folder list the folder will be created with default settings and new emails in that folder won't appear in the common inbox.
The current behaviour always requires some time to configure new subfolders.

Similar to #3516, which was closed without further info from the OP.

The message should be marked as read in the server when read in k9.

title: [Autodiscovery] Change ConnectionSettingsDiscovery interface
body:
We need to make some changes to the `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` interface to be able to make optimal use of the functionality provided by `SrvServiceDiscovery`.

The `ProvidersXmlDiscovery` autodiscovery method either gives us a complete set of server settings (exactly one of each incoming and outgoing server settings) or it doesn't. With `ThunderbirdDiscovery` that's not necessarily true, but it probably is in practice. But with `SrvServiceDiscovery` there's a real chance we could get any combination of one, none, or multiple server settings for both incoming and outgoing server. This is fine and we want to make use of all the information we can get in order be able to automatically set up an account. For the whole plan see issue #4721.

**Input**: When a `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` implementation is used in a later stage, we might already have working server settings for either the incoming or outgoing server, and are only looking for settings for the missing server. So there should be a way to let the `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` instance know which type of server settings it should look for (incoming, outgoing, or incoming + outgoing).

**Output**: We want to support situations where a discovery mechanism returns more than one server setting candidate for each server type (incoming, outgoing). We also want to support getting server settings candidates for only one server type. With `SrvServiceDiscovery` (and maybe other methods in the future) we need to distinguish between trusted and untrusted server settings. Where trusted settings are ones we can use to automatically set up an account. Untrusted server settings will only be used after the user has confirmed it's okay to do so. Since the `ServerSettings` class we currently use is also used elsewhere, I suggest creating a new class that is similar but specific to the autodiscovery phase.

With `ConnectionSettingsDiscovery` changed, we can update `SrvServiceDiscovery` to expose all the information it collected. Whether or not settings from DNS can be trusted should be determined by either
a) are the SRV records signed via DNSSEC
b) is the server's host name identical to the email domain or a sub domain of it, e.g. we trust mail.domain.example as incoming or outgoing server for user@domain.example.

This is a sub task of #4721

### Expected behavior
Refreshing folder list should display all folders on the server

These messages repeat in alternating numbers that seem to match the number of folders displayed.

title: 'Checking e-mail' notification in infite loop
body:
When the IMAP connection stops during a manually initiated 'checking for e-mails', the small rotating arrows in the top left notification bar and the message in the Android notification list remain there in an infinite loop.
It's also impossible to delete the message by swiping it to the left or right.
Currently I restart the phone when this happens, otherwise this drains the battery.

A solution might to implement a timeout, which both stops the 'checking for e-mails' internally and erases the animated notification icon and the message.

### Steps to reproduce
Setup an account with an unreliable server-side IMAP connection (e.g. yahoo.com) or disconnect the network connection during 'checking for e-mails'.

### Environment
K-9 Mail 5.713 on Android 10
IMAP account (yahoo.com)

title: [EPIC] Automatic account setup / server settings autodiscovery
body:
Thanks to @wiktor-k (PR #3879 + #3980) we have code to retrieve server settings from Thunderbird's ISPDB. Thanks to @livmackintosh (PR #4719) we'll soon have code to retrieve server settings via DNS SRV records (see [RFC 6186](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6186)).
But in order to actually use these methods to automatically set up an account, K-9 Mail's code needs to be changed quite a bit. In this issue I'll try to list all requirements and propose a plan for an automatic account setup feature.

### Goal
The goal is to make it as easy as possible for users to add their email account to K-9 Mail. Ideally, that means they only need to provide their email address and the app is figuring out the rest. In practice the authentication process also requires some kind of user interaction (provide password, allow access to an account using an OAuth workflow etc). 
It should still be possible to manually provide server settings, but we want to avoid asking users for their server settings if possible at all.

### Requirements
- The process needs to be secure. It should not be possible for a man-in-the-middle attacker to get the app to automatically send the user secret to an untrusted server. When server settings are found, but can't be trusted automatically, we ask the user to confirm using them.
- The process should be reasonably fast. In practice that means not trying all supported method sequentially, but in parallel.

### Autodiscovery methods we want to support (ordered by preference)
- bundled providers.xml (we'll remove all entries that are covered by another method)
- RFC 6186 DNS SRV records
- Configuration server at ISP (Thunderbird method)
- Thunderbird's ISPDB
- Use MX record to look up provider in the ISPDB (useful when using a custom domain with a known provider)
- Guessing (imap.example.com, smtp.example.com etc)

1. Asking for the user's email address
2. Finding server settings
3. Testing server settings and finding out which supported authentication methods are offered by the server
4. Asking the user for authentication credentials
5. Using the credentials to log in and maybe retrieve additional server capabilities to make the final decision on whether or not K-9 Mail supports this email account

But different autodiscovery methods might return the same server settings and we don't want to test them twice. So we need a mechanism to collect the results and only test unique server settings once. But we also don't want to wait for all autodiscovery methods to finish step 2 to test server settings in step 3. Ideally, we respect the order in which the autodiscovery methods return server settings. But there should be a timeout value X after which we take the most preferable server settings that tested successfully without waiting for any, potentially better, matches.

Step 2: The DNS SRV lookup returns "imap" and "imaps" results.

In this case we'd cancel the remaining tests in step 3 and select the "imaps" server settings.

- Group 2:

- Group 3:
  - Use MX record to look up provider in the ISPDB
- Group 4:
  - Guessing

Step 2 for the next group is started once the current group finishes step 3 or X seconds have passed.

title: use day of week in message list
body:
Currently, message time in the message list is formatted as either time of day or as calendar date depending on whether the time is of the current day or earlier. Most interfaces in a similar context employ such an approach, but further use the day of the week to format dates from the past week. As such, if the current day were Monday, then the date of a message that is 72 hours old would be represented by a string indicating Friday.

I suggest augmenting the existing formatting logic for this special case.

title: Is there an intent to make K9 check email? Or could one please be introduced? So that checking could be triggered while in ‘doze’, by other apps
body:
Until K-9 figures out what to do about the ‘doze’ thing, there are apps like Automate or Tasker, which seem to successfully wake up periodically when K-9 does not (mostly by presenting a persistent notification, which thankfully can be ‘minimized’). So, if there were an intent that I could send to make K-9 check for new mail, then I could set up Automate to poke K-9 every fifteen minutes.

I looked through the manifest and the issues, but it seems there's no such intent now. Would it please be possible to add one?

title: unable to type in an address while creating new mail
body:
K9mail 5.600 from F-Droid Store.

Unfortunately I am not able to complete typing an e-mail address in the address field, here is an example: 

You put some.body@example.com into the Addressbook so that lookup works. 

then type:  some.body@o

 and the cursor ends up in the new message field. You are unable to finish typing therdomain.com


You are also unable to fix the Address you have just typed which is annoying. 

Only Workaround is to copy and paste the e-mail Address which is even more annoying.

The only thing I am missing is the ability to – besides replying to a message and marking it as read – also delete it right from the notification.
